# Chapter 1 Requirements Understanding


## 1.1 Current System Status Analysis of the Hall Application System

### 1.1.1 Overall System Architecture

The Hunan Provincial Government Services Hall Informatization Project (hereinafter referred to as "this Project") is a critical infrastructure for Hunan Province's efforts to deepen the "Streamlining Administration, Delegating Power, and Improving Services" reform and advance the digital transformation of "One-Stop Online Government Services." This Project encompasses 9 core subsystems that collectively form an informatization support system covering the entire government services workflow. The overall system architecture adopts a three-tier design philosophy of "unified front-end entry, mid-tier business support, and back-end data integration," built upon microservices architecture and containerized deployment technologies, achieving a highly available, highly scalable, and highly secure government services informatization platform.

This Project was initiated in 2018 and, through multiple phases of iterative upgrades, has established a government services informatization support system spanning provincial, municipal, and county levels. The overall system construction adheres to policy requirements including the *Implementation Plan for Integration and Sharing of Government Information Systems* (No. 39 [2017] of the General Office of the State Council) and the *Hunan Province "Internet + Government Services" Integrated Platform Construction Guide*, designed and built in accordance with the "Six Unifications" principle: "unified identity authentication, unified matter management, unified acceptance and approval, unified electronic certificates, unified service evaluation, and unified data sharing."

#### 1.1.1.1 Functional Description of the Nine Subsystems

**(1) Unified Identity Authentication System**

The Unified Identity Authentication System is the core foundational support system of the Government Services Hall, responsible for providing unified user identity authentication, authorization, and single sign-on services for all government services applications. The system employs an OAuth 2.0 + JWT technical architecture and supports multiple authentication methods, including resident identity cards, digital certificates, facial recognition, and SMS verification codes. The system interfaces with the National Unified Identity Authentication Platform and the Hunan Provincial E-Government Extranet Unified Identity Authentication Platform, achieving unified identity authentication interoperability across provincial, municipal, and county levels. The system processes approximately 150,000 authentication requests daily, with peak periods reaching up to 250,000 requests per hour, and the system availability requirement exceeds 99.95%.

The system employs a Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA) mechanism, categorizing authentication security into three levels: Level 1 — SMS verification code authentication (applicable to general inquiry-type services); Level 2 — password + SMS dual-factor authentication (applicable to matter application services); Level 3 — biometric + digital certificate authentication (applicable to critical approval services). The system has established a comprehensive risk engine that conducts real-time risk assessments through multi-dimensional features including device fingerprinting, IP address, geographic location, and behavioral patterns, automatically intercepting and alerting on anomalous login behaviors. The risk engine analyzes approximately 150,000 authentication requests daily, identifies approximately 300 anomalous requests per day, and blocks approximately 50 malicious authentication attempts per day.

The system's main functions include: individual user registration and real-name authentication, legal entity user registration and electronic business license binding, unified login and Single Sign-On (SSO), Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA), session management and token refresh, user information synchronization and distribution, and authentication log auditing. The system utilizes a Redis cluster for caching session data and a MySQL master-slave architecture for storing user information, ensuring high performance and high availability of authentication services. The system has approximately 28 million registered users, including approximately 25 million individual users and approximately 3 million legal entity users. The real-name authentication pass rate is approximately 96.8%, the facial recognition pass rate is approximately 99.2%, and the average authentication time is approximately 120 milliseconds.

The system is deployed with 6 authentication nodes in an active-active architecture, achieving millisecond-level failover between primary and standby nodes. The system supports horizontal scaling, with processing capacity increased by adding node quantities. System logs are retained for 180 days, meeting security audit requirements. The system has passed Level 3 of the Classified Protection 2.0 certification, possessing comprehensive security protection capabilities.

**(2) Matter Management System**

The Matter Management System is the business core of the Government Services Hall, responsible for the unified management, dynamic adjustment, and full-process monitoring of government services matters across the entire province. Based on the *Hunan Provincial Government Services Matter Basic Catalog*, the system manages approximately 120,000 government services matters at provincial, municipal, and county levels, encompassing over 40 standardized fields including matter codes, matter names, processing conditions, application materials, processing workflows, processing time limits, and fee standards. The system employs a distributed database architecture and supports full lifecycle management of matters, including online approval processes for matter addition, modification, cancellation, and delegation.

The system has established a matter standardization review mechanism, whereby each matter must undergo a three-tier review process before entering the system: initial review by the business department, re-review by the standardization review panel, and final approval by the supervising leader. The system supports matter version management, recording the modifier, modification time, modification content, and reason for each change, ensuring traceability of matter modifications. The system also establishes a dynamic matter adjustment mechanism, promptly adjusting and updating matters in response to changes in laws and regulations, institutional reforms, and function transfers. In 2024, the system processed approximately 12,000 matter modifications, including approximately 3,000 newly added matters, approximately 6,000 modified matters, and approximately 3,000 cancelled/delegated matters.

The system's main functions include: matter standardization management, matter workflow configuration, matter permission management, matter statistical analysis, matter public disclosure, and matter supervision and assessment. The system achieves real-time data synchronization with national and provincial government services matter libraries, ensuring the accuracy and consistency of matter information. The system employs an Elasticsearch full-text search engine, supporting fuzzy search and intelligent recommendations for matters, with approximately 80,000 daily search queries. Matter data is stored at provincial, municipal, and county levels, with approximately 28,000 province-level managed matters, approximately 45,000 municipal-level matters, and approximately 47,000 county-level matters.

The system has established a matter processing time limit monitoring mechanism, providing early warnings and supervisory interventions for matters approaching or exceeding their deadlines. In 2024, the on-time completion rate was approximately 98.2%, the overdue completion rate was approximately 1.8%, and the average processing time was compressed by approximately 65% compared to the statutory time limit. The system supports matter classification management, divided into two major categories — administrative power matters and public service matters — further subdivided into 15 subcategories including administrative licensing, administrative confirmation, administrative benefits, administrative adjudication, and administrative penalties.

**(3) Unified Acceptance and Approval System**

The Unified Acceptance and Approval System is the core business processing system of the Government Services Hall, responsible for achieving unified acceptance, classified approval, full-process tracking, and result feedback for government services matters. The system employs a workflow engine (based on Activiti/Flowable) to drive approval processes, supporting over 20 approval operation modes including serial approval, parallel approval, countersignature, additional signature, return, and suspension. The system processes approximately 30,000 cases daily, with peak periods reaching up to 50,000 cases per hour.

The system implements the "Acceptance-Approval Separation" reform, separating the acceptance and approval stages, with unified acceptance by comprehensive windows and back-end approval by department approval personnel according to their authority. The system supports the "One-Window Acceptance" model, where a single comprehensive window can accept approval matters from all departments, allowing citizens to complete all applications at a single window. The system also implements the "Parallel Approval" model, enabling simultaneous initiation of approvals from multiple departments for matters involving multiple departments, significantly reducing approval time. In 2024, approximately 8,000 matters were processed through the parallel approval model, with average approval time compressed by approximately 52%.

The system's main functions include: unified document reception and material distribution, intelligent form filling assistance, electronic signatures, approval workflow engine, real-time case status tracking, overdue early warning and supervisory intervention, electronic certificate generation and delivery, and service evaluation feedback collection. The system has achieved deep integration with the electronic signature system, electronic certificate system, postal logistics system, and service evaluation system, forming a complete closed-loop approval service. The system supports approximately 1.5 million electronic signatures per year, generates approximately 600,000 electronic certificates per year, and sends approximately 1.8 million delivery notifications per year.

The system has established an approval workflow optimization mechanism, regularly reviewing and optimizing approval processes to eliminate unnecessary approval steps and materials. In 2024, approximately 2,000 approval workflows were optimized, approximately 3,000 application materials were streamlined, and approximately 1,500 approval time limits were compressed. The system supports mobile approval, enabling approval personnel to conduct approval operations via mobile terminals, improving approval efficiency. The mobile approval utilization rate is approximately 35%, with average approval efficiency improved by approximately 40%.

**(4) Electronic Certificate System**

The Electronic Certificate System is a critical support system for the Government Services Hall, responsible for the unified management, shared application, and security assurance of electronic certificates across the province. The system has collected over 680 types of electronic certificates, including business licenses, identity cards, real estate ownership certificates, and teacher qualification certificates, with approximately 280 million certificate records accumulated. The system employs blockchain technology to ensure the immutability of electronic certificate data and uses the national cryptographic SM2/SM4 algorithms for data encryption, ensuring the security of certificate data.

The system has established a full lifecycle management mechanism for electronic certificates, encompassing certificate generation, certificate collection, certificate sharing, certificate verification, certificate revocation, and certificate expiration management. The system employs blockchain technology for certificate data notarization, with each certificate record notarized on the blockchain, ensuring the authenticity and immutability of certificate data. The system supports cross-department, cross-level, and cross-region sharing of certificates, achieving a "generate once, reuse by multiple parties" certificate sharing model. The system processes approximately 450,000 certificate verification requests daily, with a verification pass rate of approximately 97.5% and a verification response time of approximately 150 milliseconds.

The system's main functions include: certificate issuance management, certificate collection and sharing, certificate verification and comparison, certificate status management (valid/revoked/expired), certificate QR code generation, certificate usage authorization, and certificate application statistics. The system has achieved interconnectivity with the national electronic certificate library and various provincial industry certificate systems, supporting the widespread application of electronic certificates in over 200 scenarios including government services, finance, education, and healthcare. The system has connected approximately 86 provincial department data sources, with approximately 500GB of daily data exchange volume.

The system has established a certificate data quality monitoring mechanism, conducting quality checks on collected certificate data, including completeness checks, accuracy checks, and consistency checks. The certificate data accuracy rate is approximately 99.5%, and the completeness rate is approximately 98.8%. The system supports batch import and export of certificates, with a single batch import capacity of approximately 100,000 records. The certificate storage capacity is approximately 280 million records × average 500KB per record ≈ 1.4PB, employing a distributed storage architecture that supports online expansion.

**(5) Service Evaluation System**

The Service Evaluation System is the quality supervision system of the Government Services Hall, responsible for collecting, compiling, and analyzing evaluation feedback from enterprises and citizens regarding government services. The system covers approximately 3,800 government service centers and 26,000 service windows at provincial, municipal, and county levels, achieving full evaluation coverage. The system collects approximately 120,000 evaluation data entries daily, with the satisfaction rate consistently maintained above 98.5%.

The system has established a closed-loop management mechanism of "Evaluation-Feedback-Rectification-Improvement." For negative evaluations, the system automatically generates negative evaluation work orders, dispatching them to the relevant responsible departments for processing, requiring completion of rectification and feedback within specified time limits. The system tracks and supervises the rectification of negative evaluations, ensuring effective handling of negative evaluation matters. The system also establishes a negative evaluation analysis mechanism, conducting classified analysis of negative evaluation data to identify weak areas in government services, providing a basis for improving government services. In 2024, the system processed approximately 85,000 negative evaluations, with a negative evaluation rectification rate of approximately 99.2% and an average rectification time of approximately 2.3 working days.

The system's main functions include: multi-channel evaluation collection (window evaluation devices, SMS evaluations, APP evaluations, website evaluations), real-time evaluation data statistics, negative evaluation early warning and rectification, evaluation data analysis and reporting, performance assessment correlation, and evaluation result disclosure. The system employs big data analytics technology to conduct multi-dimensional analysis of evaluation data, providing data support for government services improvement. The system supports real-time visualization display of evaluation data, enabling management personnel at all levels to view evaluation data in real time through large screens.

The system's evaluation data is analyzed across multiple dimensions including region, department, window, and matter type. The 2024 evaluation data indicates: provincial government service center satisfaction rate of approximately 99.1%, municipal satisfaction rate of approximately 98.5%, and county-level satisfaction rate of approximately 97.8%. The evaluation channel distribution is: window evaluation devices approximately 45%, SMS evaluations approximately 25%, APP evaluations approximately 20%, and website evaluations approximately 10%. The system has established an evaluation incentive mechanism, commending departments and individuals with excellent evaluations and conducting interviews and requiring rectification for departments with poor evaluations.

**(6) Comprehensive Monitoring System**

The Comprehensive Monitoring System is the operations management core of the Government Services Hall, responsible for real-time monitoring, alerting, and handling of the operational status of all informatization systems in the hall. The system covers various IT resources including application systems, network systems, servers, databases, middleware, and security devices, with approximately 15,000 monitoring points. The system collects approximately 200 million monitoring data entries daily, with approximately 500 alert events per day.

The system has established a tiered alerting mechanism, categorizing alerts into four levels: Critical Alerts (P1 — requiring immediate response, response time not exceeding 5 minutes), Major Alerts (P2 — requiring prompt response, response time not exceeding 15 minutes), General Alerts (P3 — requiring handling within 4 hours), and Informational Alerts (P4 — requiring handling within 24 hours). The system supports multiple alert notification methods, including SMS, email, Enterprise WeChat, and DingTalk, ensuring timely delivery of alert information to relevant personnel. In 2024, the system processed approximately 200 P1 alerts, approximately 800 P2 alerts, approximately 3,000 P3 alerts, and approximately 15,000 P4 alerts.

The system's main functions include: infrastructure monitoring (CPU/memory/disk/network), Application Performance Monitoring (APM), business transaction monitoring, centralized log analysis, intelligent alerting and event correlation, automated operations orchestration, large-screen visualization display, and operations report generation. The system employs a Zabbix + Prometheus + Grafana technology stack, achieving full-stack monitoring coverage from infrastructure to application layer. The system supports historical trend analysis of monitoring data, with a data retention period of 1 year.

The system has established a monitoring inspection mechanism, conducting comprehensive system inspections daily, covering server status, database status, network status, application status, and security status. The system inspection coverage rate is 100%, with an inspection completion rate of approximately 99.5%. The system supports automated operations orchestration, achieving automated execution of common operations tasks (such as service restart, configuration updates, and log cleanup), with an automation coverage rate of approximately 60%. Operations efficiency has improved by approximately 35%, and manual intervention frequency has decreased by approximately 40%.

**(7) Data Sharing and Exchange System**

The Data Sharing and Exchange System is the data hub of the Government Services Hall, responsible for the unified collection, cleansing, transformation, and distribution of cross-department and cross-level government data. The system has connected approximately 86 provincial department data sources, with approximately 500GB of daily data exchange volume, supporting both real-time synchronization and batch exchange modes. The system is based on the Apache Kafka message queue and Apache Flink stream processing engine, achieving efficient transmission and real-time processing of large-scale data.

The system has established a data quality monitoring mechanism, conducting quality checks on collected data, including completeness checks, accuracy checks, consistency checks, and timeliness checks. For data quality issues, the system automatically generates data quality reports and dispatches them to relevant data source units for rectification. The system has also established a data standards management mechanism, formulating unified data standards to ensure the accuracy and consistency of cross-department data exchange. In 2024, the system processed approximately 1,200 data quality issues, with a rectification rate of approximately 96.8% and an average rectification time of approximately 1.5 working days.

The system's main functions include: data source management, data collection and extraction, data cleansing and standardization, data transformation and mapping, data distribution and push, data quality monitoring, data exchange auditing, and data catalog management. The system strictly follows the *Government Data Sharing and Exchange Specification* (GB/T 38667-2020), ensuring the standardization and security of data sharing and exchange. The system supports real-time monitoring and auditing of data exchange, ensuring secure and controllable data exchange.

The system's real-time data exchange rate is approximately 85%, and the batch exchange completion rate is approximately 99.5%. The system supports resumable data transfer, ensuring data transmission reliability. The system's data cleansing rules cover approximately 2,000 business rules, with approximately 5,000 data transformation mapping relationships. The system has established a data catalog, incorporating approximately 8,600 types of data resources and approximately 120,000 data items, providing a unified data resource view for data sharing and exchange.

**(8) Hall Queue Management System**

The Hall Queue Management System is the on-site service management system of the Government Services Hall, responsible for providing fair and orderly service guidance for on-site service users. The system covers all 36 service windows of the Provincial Government Services Hall, supporting appointment ticketing, on-site ticketing, VIP priority, and extended service functions. The system serves approximately 2,000 visitors daily, with an average waiting time of approximately 15 minutes.

The system employs an intelligent queue scheduling algorithm, performing intelligent scheduling based on factors such as matter type, window function, and visitor waiting time, ensuring minimum waiting times and maximum service efficiency. The system supports multi-channel ticketing, including online appointment ticketing, on-site ticketing, and self-service terminal ticketing, accommodating different groups of service users. Online appointment ticketing accounts for approximately 35%, on-site ticketing for approximately 45%, and self-service terminal ticketing for approximately 20%.

The system's main functions include: multi-mode ticketing (online appointment, on-site ticketing, self-service terminal ticketing), intelligent queue scheduling, multimedia call display, real-time waiting count display, instant service evaluation collection, window work status management, and queue data analysis. The system achieves data linkage with the Unified Acceptance and Approval System, supporting real-time case progress queries and SMS/WeChat notifications. The system's call response time does not exceed 3 seconds, and display update latency does not exceed 1 second.

The system has established a window performance analysis mechanism, conducting statistical analysis of each window's service efficiency, waiting time, and case processing volume. 2024 data indicates: average window service time of approximately 12 minutes, maximum waiting time of approximately 45 minutes, and window utilization rate of approximately 78%. The system supports dynamic window allocation, adjusting the number of open windows in real time based on business volume changes, improving resource utilization efficiency.

**(9) Intelligent Guidance System**

The Intelligent Guidance System is the intelligent service system of the Government Services Hall, utilizing artificial intelligence technology to provide precise business guidance and service assistance for citizens. The system is based on Natural Language Processing (NLP) and knowledge graph technology, constructing an intelligent Q&A knowledge base covering 120,000 government services matters, supporting both voice and text interaction modes. The system serves approximately 5,000 consultation requests daily, with an intelligent response accuracy rate of approximately 92%.

The system employs deep learning models for intent recognition and semantic understanding, supporting multi-turn dialogue and contextual understanding. The system has established a knowledge base update mechanism, promptly updating knowledge base content for newly added and modified matters. The system also supports intelligent material pre-review functionality — after citizens upload materials, the system automatically checks whether the materials are complete and meet requirements, reducing the need for citizens to make repeated trips due to incomplete materials. In 2024, through the intelligent material pre-review function, the system reduced approximately 35,000 citizen visits and saved approximately 7,000 hours of citizen processing time.

The system's main functions include: intelligent Q&A and business guidance, material pre-review and intelligent form filling, intelligent service guide recommendations, appointment service processing, accessibility service support, multilingual service, and user profiling with personalized recommendations. The system employs deep learning models for intent recognition and semantic understanding, continuously optimizing model performance through user feedback. The system knowledge base is updated on a weekly cycle, with immediate updates for urgent matter changes.

The system has established a user profiling mechanism, recommending personalized services based on users' historical service records, search behaviors, and evaluation feedback. The system supports minority language services (Miao, Dong, Tujia, etc.) and accessibility services (voice broadcast, font enlargement, high contrast mode, etc.). The intelligent guidance satisfaction rate is approximately 88.5%, and the manual guidance satisfaction rate is approximately 92.3%, with the gap between the two gradually narrowing.

#### 1.1.1.2 Technical Architecture

The system technical architecture adopts a front-end and back-end separated microservices architecture, with the main technology selections as follows:

| Layer | Technology Selection | Description |
|------|----------|------|
| Front-end Layer | Vue 3.0 + Element Plus | Responsive web application, supporting PC and mobile |
| Gateway Layer | Spring Cloud Gateway | API gateway, unified entry, rate limiting, authentication |
| Service Layer | Spring Cloud Alibaba + Nacos | Microservices framework, service registration and discovery |
| Message Queue | Apache Kafka | Asynchronous message processing, data stream transmission |
| Cache Layer | Redis Cluster 6.0 | Distributed caching, session management |
| Database | MySQL 8.0 (Master-Slave) + TiDB | Relational database + distributed database |
| Search Engine | Elasticsearch 7.x | Full-text search, log analysis |
| Workflow Engine | Flowable 6.x | Approval process automation |
| Container Platform | Kubernetes 1.24 | Container orchestration and management |
| Image Registry | Harbor 2.x | Container image management |
| CI/CD | Jenkins + GitLab | Continuous integration and continuous deployment |
| Monitoring Stack | Zabbix + Prometheus + Grafana | Full-stack monitoring |

#### 1.1.1.3 Data Flow Architecture

The system data flow adopts a five-tier architecture of "Collection-Transmission-Processing-Storage-Application":

- **Data Collection Layer**: Collects data from various business systems, external systems, and terminal devices through API gateways, data collection agents, message queues, and other methods. Collection methods include real-time push, scheduled pull, and event-driven approaches.
- **Data Transmission Layer**: Based on Apache Kafka message queues and API gateways, achieves efficient and reliable data transmission. Supports data encrypted transmission, traffic control, resumable transfer, and other mechanisms.
- **Data Processing Layer**: Based on the Apache Flink stream processing engine and batch processing engine, performs data cleansing, transformation, aggregation, analysis, and other processing operations. Supports both real-time processing and batch processing modes.
- **Data Storage Layer**: Employs a multi-type storage architecture, including relational databases (MySQL/TiDB), distributed file systems (HDFS/MinIO), search engines (Elasticsearch), caching systems (Redis), and blockchain nodes.
- **Data Application Layer**: Provides data services to business systems and decision-making systems through data service APIs, data visualization, data reports, and other methods.

**Failure Trend Analysis:**

Based on failure data from the past five years, system failures have decreased annually, from 48 in 2020 to 30 in 2024, representing a 37.5% reduction. MTTR decreased from 35 minutes to 22 minutes, a 37.1% reduction, indicating continuous improvement in failure recovery capability. MTBF increased from 180 hours to 292 hours, a 62.2% improvement, demonstrating significant enhancement in system stability. Annual impact duration decreased from 28.8 hours to 13.2 hours, a 54.2% reduction. System availability improved from 99.67% to 99.85%, with year-over-year improvement.

Failure cause classification statistics show: hardware failures account for approximately 25% (primarily disk and memory failures), software failures account for approximately 40% (primarily memory leaks and database connection pool exhaustion), network failures account for approximately 20% (primarily link interruptions and device failures), human operation failures account for approximately 10%, and other causes account for approximately 5%.

**Satisfaction Analysis Conclusions:**

This survey collected 5,200 samples covering provincial, municipal, and county-level government service halls, including 3,640 individual user samples (70%) and 1,560 legal entity user samples (30%). The survey results indicate an overall user satisfaction score of 81.5, which is at a good level. Service stability scored highest (85.2), while response speed scored lowest (78.3), indicating that system stability is relatively good but response speed still has significant room for improvement.

Based on the summary of improvement suggestions, the top three improvement areas most valued by users are: simplifying operation workflows (32%), optimizing page loading speed (28%), and reducing system downtime (22%). These suggestions are highly consistent with the pain points identified in the system operational status analysis, providing clear direction for subsequent operations service improvement.

**Survey Methodology:**

This survey adopted a stratified random sampling method, allocating samples according to the business volume proportions of provincial, municipal, and county-level government service halls. The survey questionnaire was designed using a Likert five-point scale, encompassing 5 core dimensions: system usability, response speed, service stability, feature completeness, and data accuracy, with each dimension containing 3-5 specific evaluation indicators. The survey was conducted from October to November 2024, using three methods: on-site questionnaires, online questionnaires, and telephone callbacks.

Questionnaire reliability analysis: Cronbach's α coefficient is 0.912, indicating high internal consistency reliability. Validity analysis: KMO value is 0.887, Bartlett's test p<0.001, indicating good structural validity.

### 1.1.4 Operations and Maintenance Requirements Analysis

#### 1.1.4.1 System Stability O&M Requirements

System stability is the primary task of Government Services Hall operations and maintenance. As a public service system serving enterprises and citizens, system downtime directly impacts the government's service image and social satisfaction. O&M requirements include:

- **7×24 System Monitoring**: Round-the-clock real-time monitoring of all application systems, middleware, databases, and servers, ensuring system anomalies are detected and alerted within 5 minutes.
- **High Availability Assurance**: Core system availability requirement of 99.95% or above, meaning annual downtime shall not exceed 4.38 hours. This must be achieved through redundant deployment, automatic failover, load balancing, and other technical measures.
- **Disaster Recovery**: Establishment of a comprehensive disaster recovery system, with core system RPO (Recovery Point Objective) not exceeding 15 minutes and RTO (Recovery Time Objective) not exceeding 30 minutes.
- **Change Management**: All system changes must undergo rigorous approval and testing processes to ensure changes do not affect stable system operation.

#### 1.1.4.2 Performance Optimization O&M Requirements

With continuous business volume growth, system performance faces sustained pressure. O&M requirements include:

- **Performance Baseline Management**: Establishment of system performance baselines, with regular performance assessments and optimization to ensure system response times meet user experience requirements.
- **Capacity Planning**: Based on business growth trends, proactive capacity planning and resource expansion to avoid resource bottlenecks affecting system performance.
- **Database Optimization**: Regular database performance tuning, including index optimization, SQL optimization, table structure optimization, and database sharding.
- **Cache Strategy Optimization**: Optimization of Redis caching strategies to improve cache hit rates and reduce database access pressure.

#### 1.1.4.3 Security Assurance O&M Requirements

Government system security is the top priority of O&M work. O&M requirements include:

- **Security Monitoring**: 7×24 security monitoring, real-time detection and defense against various network attacks and intrusion activities.
- **Vulnerability Management**: Regular security vulnerability scanning and penetration testing, with timely remediation of security vulnerabilities.
- **Security Compliance**: Meeting Classified Protection 2.0 Level 3 requirements, with regular security assessments and compliance audits.
- **Emergency Response**: Establishment of a comprehensive security emergency response mechanism, ensuring security incidents receive initial handling within 15 minutes.

#### 1.1.4.4 Data Management O&M Requirements

Data is the core asset of government services. O&M requirements include:

- **Data Backup**: Establishment of a multi-tiered data backup strategy, with daily full backups and real-time incremental backups of core data, and off-site storage of backup data.
- **Data Recovery**: Regular data recovery drills to ensure the availability and integrity of backup data.
- **Data Quality**: Establishment of a data quality monitoring mechanism, with regular data cleansing and quality assessments.
- **Data Archiving**: Tiered archival management of historical data to ensure system performance and rational utilization of storage resources.

#### 1.1.4.5 Service Management O&M Requirements

O&M service management is the foundation for ensuring standardized O&M operations. O&M requirements include:

- **SLA Management**: Establishment of a comprehensive SLA indicator system, with regular SLA achievement assessments and improvements.
- **Incident Management**: Establishment of standardized incident handling processes, ensuring incidents are handled promptly and effectively.
- **Problem Management**: Establishment of root cause analysis mechanisms for problems, preventing recurrence of similar issues.
- **Knowledge Management**: Establishment of an O&M knowledge base, accumulating and sharing O&M experience and best practices.

### 1.1.5 Existing System Pain Point Analysis

#### 1.1.5.1 Technical Debt Issues

- **Legacy System Compatibility Issues**: Some earlier subsystems still employ traditional monolithic architectures with outdated technology stacks (e.g., some systems still use Struts 2, Spring MVC, and other traditional frameworks), resulting in high maintenance costs and poor scalability.
- **Inconsistent Technology Stacks**: Different subsystems were built in different periods, resulting in technology stack variations that increase the difficulty of unified O&M. Some systems use Java technology stacks while others use .NET technology stacks, leading to significant technology stack fragmentation.
- **Documentation Gaps**: Some systems lack complete technical documentation and O&M documentation, resulting in insufficient system understanding by O&M personnel and low troubleshooting efficiency.
- **Inconsistent Code Quality**: Some systems have suboptimal code quality, with issues such as hardcoding, duplicate code, and insufficient exception handling, increasing system operational risks.

#### 1.1.5.2 Performance Bottleneck Issues

- **Database Performance Bottlenecks**: Some business system database tables have exceeded tens of millions of records, lacking effective sharding strategies, resulting in significant query performance degradation.
- **Single Point of Failure Risks**: Some core services have single point of failure risks; although multiple instances are deployed, certain shared resources (such as file storage and cache nodes) still present performance bottlenecks.
- **Interface Response Latency**: Some cross-system interface call chains are too long, causing overall response times to exceed acceptable user thresholds.
- **Low Batch Processing Efficiency**: Some batch data processing tasks (such as data synchronization and report generation) have low efficiency, consuming significant system resources.

#### 1.1.5.3 Security Vulnerability Issues

- **Security Vulnerabilities**: Some systems have known security vulnerabilities (such as SQL injection, XSS cross-site scripting, CSRF cross-site request forgery, etc.) that require prompt remediation.
- **Coarse-Grained Permission Management**: Some systems have insufficiently granular permission management, posing risks of unauthorized access.
- **Insufficient Log Auditing**: Some systems have incomplete operation log recording, failing to meet security audit requirements.
- **Insufficient Encryption Measures**: Some sensitive data transmission and storage do not employ national cryptographic algorithms, not meeting government system security requirements.

#### 1.1.5.4 User Experience Issues

- **Page Loading Speed**: Some systems have slow page loading speeds, particularly during business peak periods, affecting user experience.
- **Complex Operation Workflows**: Some business system operation workflows are not sufficiently streamlined, with excessive user operation steps, increasing usage difficulty.
- **Insufficient Mobile Adaptation**: Some systems have incomplete mobile adaptation, affecting the user experience of mobile users.
- **Insufficient Accessibility Support**: Some systems lack accessibility features, failing to meet the usage needs of special groups.

#### Table 1-12 Data Traffic Growth Forecast Model (2025-2027)

| Indicator | 2024 (Baseline) | 2025 (Forecast) | 2026 (Forecast) | 2027 (Forecast) | Calculation Formula/Growth Factor |
|------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-------------|-----------------|
| Daily Avg. Cases (10K) | 3.0 | 3.4 | 3.8 | 4.2 | Baseline × (1+growth rate), growth rate decreasing annually |
| Daily Avg. Auth. (10K) | 15.0 | 17.2 | 19.5 | 21.8 | Baseline × (1+15%/13%/12%) |

| Total Data (TB) | 250 | 340 | 440 | 550 | Baseline + annual increment (90/100/110) |
| Daily Avg. Monitoring Data (100M records) | 2.0 | 2.5 | 3.1 | 3.8 | Baseline × (1+25%/24%/23%) |
| Electronic Certificate Invocations (10K/day) | 45 | 55 | 67 | 80 | Baseline × (1+22%/22%/19%) |
| Network Egress Traffic (TB/month) | 114 | 145 | 180 | 220 | Baseline × (1+27%/24%/22%) |

**Forecast Model Description:**

This forecast model is based on the following assumptions and calculation formulas:

1. **Growth Factor Calculation**: Uses a compound growth model, Annual Growth Rate = Base Growth Rate × Decay Factor. The base growth rate is determined from the past five years of historical data, with a decay factor of 0.85 (i.e., the growth rate decreases by 15% each year).
2. **Confidence Interval**: The 95% confidence interval is the forecast value ±10%, meaning the actual value has a 95% probability of falling within 90%-110% of the forecast value.
3. **Seasonal Factors**: Considering seasonal factors such as Spring Festival (February trough), National Day (October trough), and mid-year peak (June), monthly forecast values are multiplied by seasonal coefficients (0.6-1.3) on top of the annual forecast values.
4. **Contingency Factor**: Considering the impact of policy changes, system upgrades, and other contingencies, a contingency coefficient of 1.0-1.2 is applied.

**Forecast Conclusions:**

By 2027, the system's daily average case processing volume is projected to reach 42,000 (a 40% increase from 2024), total data volume is projected to reach 550TB (a 120% increase from 2024), and network egress traffic is projected to reach 220TB/month (a 93% increase from 2024). System capacity planning must be designed according to 2027 forecast values to ensure no resource bottlenecks occur during the planning period.

# Chapter 2: Overall Technical Solution


## 2.1 "Xiang Yi Ban" Super Server Integration Implementation and O&M Implementation

### 2.1.0 Overall System Architecture Design Document

#### 2.1.0.1 Logical Architecture Diagram (Text Description)

This system adopts a three-tier logical architecture design of "Access Layer – Service Layer – Data Layer", comprising six major subsystems from top to bottom: Unified Access Subsystem, Business Service Subsystem, Data Sharing Subsystem, Data Storage Subsystem, Infrastructure Support Subsystem, and Security Management and Control Subsystem. The entire architecture follows the design principles of "high cohesion and low coupling", employing Domain-Driven Design (DDD) methodology for microservice decomposition, ensuring system scalability, maintainability, and high availability.

**Unified Access Subsystem** is positioned at the topmost layer of the architecture and serves as the main entry point for the entire system's integration with external platforms. This subsystem contains four core components: API Gateway Cluster, Protocol Conversion Engine, Traffic Control Engine, and Identity Authentication Engine. The API Gateway Cluster is built on Spring Cloud Gateway, deployed on 4 dedicated servers (16 cores/64GB), responsible for receiving all requests from the "Xiang Yi Ban" Super Server and the "One-Stop Online Government Services" platform. The Protocol Conversion Engine supports automatic conversion between RESTful API and WebService, enabling seamless integration of heterogeneous systems, and supports mutual conversion among SOAP/REST/GraphQL protocols. The Traffic Control Engine employs the token bucket algorithm, configuring independent rate-limiting policies for each caller, with a global rate-limiting threshold set at 10,000 requests per second and a per-user rate limit of 100 requests per second. The Identity Authentication Engine integrates three authentication methods—OAuth 2.0, digital certificates, and API Keys—supporting flexible policy combinations. The Access Subsystem also includes a Request Routing Engine that supports weight-based, version-based, and region-based routing strategies, enabling canary release and A/B testing capabilities.

**Business Service Subsystem** is located in the middle layer of the architecture and contains 12 core business service modules: Identity Authentication Service, Item Management Service, Application Filing Service, Progress Query Service, Electronic Certificate Service, Rating and Review Service, Appointment Service, Message Notification Service, Payment Service, Logistics Service, Statistical Analysis Service, and Data Synchronization Service. Each service is independently deployed and independently scalable, communicating asynchronously through the Apache Kafka message bus and synchronously via the gRPC protocol. Service registration and discovery is implemented using Nacos, and the configuration center uniformly manages configuration items for all services. The Business Service Subsystem adopts the CQRS (Command Query Responsibility Segregation) pattern, separating read and write operations into different service instances to improve system throughput. Each service implements fault-tolerance mechanisms including circuit breaking, degradation, and retry, achieving service-level fault isolation through Hystrix/Sentinel.

**Data Sharing Subsystem** is responsible for data exchange and sharing among internal business systems, containing a Data Exchange Engine, Data Routing Engine, Data Transformation Engine, and Data Validation Engine. The Data Exchange Engine supports both publish/subscribe and point-to-point modes, processing approximately 2 million data exchange records daily, supporting data transmission of up to 10MB per single message. The Data Routing Engine automatically selects optimal data transmission paths based on data type and target system, supporting automatic failover between primary and backup paths. The Data Transformation Engine supports automatic conversion among multiple formats including JSON, XML, and CSV, with over 200 built-in data mapping rule templates. The Data Validation Engine employs a dual mechanism of CRC32 checksums and digital signatures to ensure data transmission integrity and non-repudiation. The Data Sharing Subsystem also includes a Data Version Management module that records the complete history of every data change, supporting data traceability and audit trails.

**Data Storage Subsystem** adopts a multi-type storage architecture, comprising a relational database (MySQL 8.0), cache database (Redis 7.0 Cluster), search engine (Elasticsearch 7.17), message queue (Apache Kafka 3.4), object storage (MinIO), and time-series database (InfluxDB 2.6). The relational database stores core business data, configured with master-slave replication and automatic failover, with master-slave latency controlled within 100ms. Redis Cluster caches hot data, configured as a 6-node cluster (3 masters, 3 slaves), with a cache hit rate target of no less than 90%, supporting persistent storage to prevent cache avalanche. Elasticsearch stores integration logs and audit logs, supporting full-text search and aggregation analysis, with single-node index capacity reaching up to 1 billion records. The time-series database is used for storing system monitoring metrics, supporting second-level data point writing and millisecond-level query response.

**Infrastructure Support Subsystem** provides the foundational capabilities required for system operation, comprising six major components: Service Registration and Discovery (Nacos), Distributed Configuration Center (Nacos Config), Distributed Transaction Management (Seata), Distributed Tracing (SkyWalking), Task Scheduling (XXL-JOB), and File Storage (MinIO). The Infrastructure Support Subsystem adopts a high-availability deployment mode, with all components deployed with 3 or more instances to ensure that single-point failures do not affect system operation. The Nacos cluster uses MySQL persistent storage with multi-replica backup for configuration data. SkyWalking uses Elasticsearch as its storage backend, supporting distributed tracing and performance analysis.

**Security Management and Control Subsystem** spans all layers, providing comprehensive security protection capabilities, including a WAF firewall, IDS/IPS intrusion detection system, security audit system, key management system, and permission management system. The Security Management and Control Subsystem adopts a zero-trust security architecture, performing identity verification and authorization checks on all requests, trusting no internal network traffic. The WAF firewall is configured with over 500 protection rules, covering common web threats such as SQL injection, XSS attacks, and CSRF attacks. The Key Management System uses HSM (Hardware Security Module) to store root keys, supporting key rotation and version management.

#### 2.1.0.2 Physical Architecture Diagram (Text Description)

The physical architecture of this system adopts a three-zone isolation design of "DMZ Zone – Application Zone – Data Zone", deployed in the Hunan Provincial Government Extranet environment.

**DMZ Zone (Demilitarized Zone)** serves as a buffer zone between the system and external networks, deployed on the DMZ port of the firewall. The DMZ Zone deploys the following equipment: 2 firewalls (active-standby mode, Huawei USG6600 series, throughput ≥40Gbps), 2 load balancers (active-standby mode, F5 BIG-IP 4200v, supporting SSL offloading), 2 WAF firewalls (active-standby mode, NSFOCUS WAF, throughput ≥10Gbps), 1 VPN gateway (for remote O&M access), and 2 DNS servers (active-standby mode). The DMZ Zone is isolated from external networks through a firewall, allowing only HTTPS (port 443) and national cryptographic SSL traffic to pass through. The DMZ Zone is isolated from the internal network through a second-layer firewall, allowing only traffic on specific ports to pass through.

**Application Zone** is the deployment area for the system's core business, deployed on the internal port of the firewall. The Application Zone is divided into three sub-areas:

- **Access Service Area**: Deploys the API Gateway Cluster (4 servers, 16 cores/64GB/500GB SSD) and Protocol Conversion Service (2 servers, 8 cores/32GB). The Access Service Area uses dual uplink connections to the core switch to ensure network redundancy.
- **Business Service Area**: Deploys the microservice cluster, comprising 20 servers in total (32 cores/128GB/1TB SSD), distributed across 4 server cabinets with 5 servers per cabinet. The Business Service Area connects to the core switch via 10-Gigabit fiber, with servers interconnected via 25GE networking to ensure internal communication bandwidth.
- **Security Service Area**: Deploys security-related services, including 2 bastion hosts (active-standby mode), 1 vulnerability scanner, 2 log audit systems, 2 IDS/IPS systems (active-standby mode), and 1 key management system (including HSM hardware security module).

**Data Zone** is the storage area for system data, deployed on the internal port of the firewall, isolated from the Application Zone through an internal firewall. The Data Zone is divided into two sub-areas:

- **Database Area**: Deploys the MySQL database cluster (4 nodes, 32 cores/256GB/2TB NVMe SSD, 1 master, 3 slaves), Redis Cluster (6 nodes, 16 cores/64GB/500GB SSD, 3 masters, 3 slaves), Elasticsearch cluster (6 nodes, 16 cores/128GB/2TB SSD, 3 masters, 3 slaves), and Kafka cluster (4 nodes, 16 cores/64GB/2TB SSD).
- **Storage Area**: Deploys the MinIO object storage cluster (4 nodes, 16 cores/64GB/10TB HDD), backup storage system (20TB usable capacity), and SAN storage system (50TB usable capacity, used for database shared storage).

**Network Architecture**: The overall network adopts a three-tier architecture (Core Layer – Aggregation Layer – Access Layer). Core switches use active-active hot standby, with 10GE links from the Core Layer to the Aggregation Layer and GE links from the Aggregation Layer to the Access Layer. All critical links employ redundant design to ensure that single-point failures do not affect system operation.

**Data Center Environment**: The system is deployed in the Hunan Provincial Government Extranet Data Center, compliant with Class B standards (GB 50174-2017), equipped with UPS uninterruptible power supplies (dual power feed, backup time ≥30 minutes), precision air conditioning (N+1 redundancy), fire suppression system (gas-based fire suppression), and access control system (fingerprint + IC card dual-factor authentication).

#### 2.1.0.3 Deployment Architecture Diagram (Text Description)

This system adopts a Kubernetes containerized deployment architecture, combined with traditional virtual machine deployment methods, to achieve flexible and efficient system deployment.

**Kubernetes Cluster Architecture**:

- **Master Nodes**: 3 nodes deployed (8 cores/32GB), each running API Server, Controller Manager, Scheduler, and etcd components. The 3 Master nodes provide external services through a load balancer for high availability. The etcd cluster uses 3-node deployment to ensure consistency and reliability of cluster state data.
- **Worker Nodes**: 16 nodes deployed (32 cores/128GB/1TB SSD), running business microservice Pods. Worker nodes are divided into three groups: Access Service Group (4 nodes), Core Business Group (8 nodes), and Data Processing Group (4 nodes). Each group of nodes has independent resource pools and scheduling policies.
- **Ingress Controller**: Nginx Ingress Controller deployed (3 replicas), responsible for external traffic routing and load balancing. The Ingress Controller is configured with SSL termination and supports HTTP/2 and gRPC protocol proxying.
- **Service Mesh**: Istio is adopted as the service mesh, deploying Sidecar proxies (Envoy) to achieve inter-service traffic management, secure communication, and observability. The Istio control plane is deployed with 3 replicas to ensure high availability.

**Namespace Planning**:

- `xiangyiban-access`: Access layer namespace, deploying API Gateway, Protocol Conversion Service, and other components, with independent network policies configured.
- `xiangyiban-service`: Business service namespace, deploying all business microservices, with resource quotas configured (CPU: 40 cores, Memory: 160GB).
- `xiangyiban-data`: Data layer namespace, deploying databases, caches, message queues, and other data services, with persistent storage configured.
- `xiangyiban-monitor`: Monitoring namespace, deploying Prometheus, Grafana, SkyWalking, and other monitoring components.
- `xiangyiban-security`: Security namespace, deploying WAF, IDS/IPS, log audit, and other security components.
- `xiangyiban-cicd`: CI/CD namespace, deploying GitLab, Jenkins, Harbor, and other DevOps tools.

**Pod Resource Allocation**:

- API Gateway Pod: Each Pod allocated 4 CPU cores/8GB memory, minimum replicas 4, maximum replicas 12, HPA target CPU utilization 60%.
- Business Microservice Pod: Each Pod allocated 2 CPU cores/4GB memory, minimum replicas 3, maximum replicas 20, HPA target CPU utilization 70%.
- Database Pod: Each Pod allocated 8 CPU cores/32GB memory, fixed replica count (MySQL 1 master, 3 slaves; Redis 3 masters, 3 slaves), no HPA used.
- Elasticsearch Pod: Each Pod allocated 8 CPU cores/32GB memory, fixed replica count (3 masters, 3 slaves), no HPA used.
- Kafka Pod: Each Pod allocated 4 CPU cores/16GB memory, fixed replica count (4 nodes), no HPA used.

**Network Policies**:

- Access layer namespace only allows inbound traffic from the Ingress Controller and is permitted to access the business service namespace.
- Business service namespace allows inbound traffic from the access layer namespace and is permitted to access the data layer namespace; direct access to external networks is prohibited.
- Data layer namespace only allows inbound traffic from the business service namespace; all outbound traffic is prohibited.
- Monitoring namespace is permitted to access monitoring ports of all namespaces; other namespaces are prohibited from accessing the monitoring namespace.

**Storage Solutions**:

- Database Storage: Uses Ceph RBD as the persistent storage backend, configured with an SSD storage pool, IOPS ≥5000, throughput ≥500MB/s.
- Log Storage: Uses Ceph RBD, configured with an HDD storage pool, capacity ≥10TB.
- File Storage: Uses MinIO object storage, configured with erasure coding mode (8+2), usable capacity ≥50TB.
- Backup Storage: Uses Ceph RBD, configured with an HDD storage pool, capacity ≥20TB.

### 2.1.0.5 Database Design Plan

#### 2.1.0.5.1 ER Diagram Text Description

The database ER diagram of this system contains 18 major entities, covering core business domains including users, items, applications, certificates, reviews, appointments, notifications, payments, logistics, and files.

**Core Entities and Relationship Descriptions:**

1. **User Entity (sys_user)**: Is the core entity of the system, containing attributes such as user ID, username, password, ID card number, mobile phone number, email, user type (individual/legal entity), user status, registration time, and last login time. The User Entity has a one-to-many relationship with the Application Entity (one user can submit multiple applications), a one-to-many relationship with the Evaluation Entity (one user can submit multiple reviews), a one-to-many relationship with the Appointment Entity (one user can create multiple appointments), a one-to-many relationship with the Payment Order Entity (one user can create multiple payment orders), and a one-to-many relationship with the Certificate Entity (one user can hold multiple certificates).

2. **Item Entity (biz_item)**: Is the core entity of government service items, containing attributes such as item code, item name, item type, handling department, handling conditions, application materials, handling process, handling time limit, fee standards, and legal basis. The Item Entity has a one-to-many relationship with the Application Entity (one item corresponds to multiple applications), a one-to-one relationship with the Form Configuration Entity (each item corresponds to one form configuration), and a one-to-many relationship with the Material Entity (one item requires multiple materials).

3. **Application Entity (biz_application)**: Is the core entity of application filing, containing attributes such as application number, associated item ID, applicant ID, filing time, application status (pending acceptance/accepted/under review/completed/rejected/withdrawn), review result, and completion time. The Application Entity has a one-to-many relationship with the Approval Record Entity (one application contains multiple approval records), a one-to-many relationship with the Application Material Entity (one application contains multiple materials), and a one-to-one relationship with the Evaluation Entity (one application corresponds to one review).

4. **Approval Record Entity (biz_approval_record)**: Records each step in the application review process, containing attributes such as record ID, associated application ID, approval step name, approver ID, approval opinion, approval time, and approval status.

5. **Application Material Entity (biz_application_material)**: Records material information submitted during application filing, containing attributes such as material ID, associated application ID, material type, file path, file size, upload time, and material status.

6. **Electronic Certificate Entity (biz_certificate)**: Stores electronic certificate information, containing attributes such as certificate ID, certificate type, certificate number, holder ID, issuing authority, issue date, validity period, certificate status, and file path.

7. **Evaluation Entity (biz_evaluation)**: Records user reviews of government services, containing attributes such as evaluation ID, associated application ID, reviewer ID, rating level (1-5 stars), review content, and review time.

8. **Appointment Entity (biz_appointment)**: Records user appointment information for government services, containing attributes such as appointment ID, appointee ID, associated item ID, appointment date, appointment time slot, appointment window, and appointment status.

9. **Notification Entity (biz_notification)**: Records system-sent message notifications, containing attributes such as notification ID, recipient ID, notification type, notification title, notification content, send time, delivery time, and read status.

10. **Payment Order Entity (biz_payment_order)**: Records online payment information, containing attributes such as order ID, associated application ID, payment amount, payment method, payment status, payment time, and transaction number.

11. **Logistics Order Entity (biz_logistics_order)**: Records logistics delivery information, containing attributes such as order ID, associated application ID, courier company, tracking number, delivery address, shipping status, and delivery time.

12. **Form Configuration Entity (biz_form_config)**: Stores application form configuration information, containing attributes such as configuration ID, associated item ID, form Schema (JSON format), form version, and creation time.

13. **Material Entity (biz_material)**: Records required materials for items, containing attributes such as material ID, associated item ID, material name, material type, whether mandatory, and material description.

14. **Department Entity (sys_department)**: Stores government department information, containing attributes such as department ID, department name, department code, parent department ID, and department status.

15. **Role Entity (sys_role)**: Stores system role information, containing attributes such as role ID, role name, role code, and role description.

16. **Permission Entity (sys_permission)**: Stores system permission information, containing attributes such as permission ID, permission name, permission type, resource path, and operation type.

17. **Operation Log Entity (sys_operation_log)**: Records system operation logs, containing attributes such as log ID, operator ID, operation type, operation content, operation time, and IP address.

18. **Data Dictionary Entity (sys_dict_data)**: Stores system data dictionary information, containing attributes such as dictionary ID, dictionary type, dictionary code, dictionary value, and sort order.

| biz_certificate | idx_composite_1 | Composite Index | cert_type, status | Certificate type + status combined query |

#### 2.1.0.5.4 Database Sharding Plan

#### Table 2-1-6: Database Sharding Strategy

| Table Name | Sharding Strategy | Sharding Key | Shard Count | Sharding Algorithm | Description |
|-----------|-------------------|-------------|-------------|-------------------|-------------|
| biz_application | Time-based sharding | create_time | Monthly sharding (36 tables) | Modulo algorithm | One table per month, historical data archiving |
| biz_approval_record | Time-based sharding | create_time | Monthly sharding (36 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Aligned with application table |
| biz_application_material | Time-based sharding | create_time | Monthly sharding (36 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Aligned with application table |
| biz_interface_log | Time-based sharding | create_time | Daily sharding (90 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Retain 90 days of online data |
| biz_audit_log | Time-based sharding | create_time | Daily sharding (90 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Retain 90 days of online data |
| biz_operation_log | Time-based sharding | create_time | Daily sharding (90 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Retain 90 days of online data |
| biz_notification | User-based sharding | receiver_id | 16 tables | Hash modulo | Hash sharding by user ID |
| biz_data_sync | Time-based sharding | create_time | Monthly sharding (12 tables) | Modulo algorithm | Retain 12 months of online data |
| biz_statistics_daily | No sharding | / | / | / | Small data volume, no sharding required |
| sys_user | No sharding | / | / | / | Moderate data volume, no sharding required |

**Database Sharding Middleware**: ShardingSphere 5.3 is adopted as the database sharding middleware, configured as follows:
- Read-write separation: All tables configured with master-slave read-write separation; write operations routed to master, read operations routed to slaves
- Sharding algorithm: Time-based tables use standard hash modulo algorithm; user-based tables use consistent hashing algorithm
- Data migration: Online data migration plan configured, supporting scale-out without downtime
- Distributed ID: Snowflake algorithm used to generate globally unique IDs, avoiding ID conflicts in sharded environments

| Connection Pool Optimization | Adjust database connection pool parameters | Connection reuse rate >90% | HikariCP tuning | 80% reduction in connection wait time |
| Read-Write Separation | Configure master-slave read-write separation | 200% improvement in read performance | ShardingSphere read-write separation | 200% improvement in read throughput |
| Cache Optimization | Hot data caching | Cache hit rate >90% | Redis multi-level cache | 80% reduction in database queries |
| Archival Strategy | Historical data archiving | Controllable online data volume | Scheduled archival tasks | 60% reduction in online table size |
| Statistics Update | Periodically update table statistics | Execution plan accuracy | ANALYZE TABLE scheduled tasks | Optimal query plans |

| Full System Disaster Recovery | Semi-annually | Restore entire system from backup | Disaster recovery environment | System functions normally, recovery time <4 hours | O&M Lead |
| Database Master-Slave Failover | Monthly | Simulate master failure, verify slave failover | Test environment | Failover time <30 seconds, no data loss | DBA |

### 2.1.0.12 Security Architecture Design

#### 2.1.0.12.1 Zero Trust Architecture Design

This system adopts a zero-trust security architecture, following the principle of "never trust, always verify," performing strict identity verification and authorization checks on all requests.

**Zero Trust Architecture Core Components:**

1. **Identity Authentication Plane**: Employs multi-factor authentication (MFA) mechanism, combining password, digital certificate, and biometric authentication factors. All user logins must pass at least two-factor authentication. Inter-service communication uses mTLS (mutual TLS) authentication, with each service holding a unique client certificate issued by an internal CA, valid for 90 days with automatic rotation.

2. **Policy Decision Point (PDP)**: Deploys an OPA (Open Policy Agent)-based policy engine for real-time authorization decisions on all API requests. Policy rules are written in the Rego language, supporting multi-dimensional access control based on user roles, resource attributes, time, location, and other factors. Policy decision response time <10ms.

3. **Policy Enforcement Point (PEP)**: Deploys policy enforcement points in the API Gateway and service mesh, intercepting all requests and forwarding them to the PDP for authorization decisions. Unauthorized requests directly return 403 Forbidden, and security audit logs are recorded.

4. **Trust Evaluation Engine**: Real-time evaluation of trust scores for each request, with scoring factors including device fingerprint, network location, access time, and historical behavior. Requests with trust scores below the threshold trigger additional security verification (such as captcha, secondary authentication).

| Convergence Type | Convergence Rule | Convergence Window | Max Alert Count | Description |
|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------|----------------|-------------|

| Layer Convergence | When parent service alert triggers, suppress child service alerts | 30 minutes | 1 | Avoid cascading alerts |

| Topology Convergence | Alerts from the same cabinet/region merged into one | 10 minutes | 1 | Rapid fault domain identification |
| Root Cause Convergence | Identify root cause alert, suppress derived alerts | 30 minutes | 1 | Focus on root cause handling |

#### 2.1.0.15.2 CI Relationship Diagram Text Description

CI relationships in the CMDB are classified into the following types:

1. **Deployment Relationship (deployed_on)**: Application services are deployed on servers, and servers are deployed in cabinets. For example: auth-service is deployed on app-server-01, and app-server-01 is deployed in Cabinet A-01.

2. **Dependency Relationship (depends_on)**: Dependency relationships between services. For example: gateway-service depends on auth-service and redis-service.

3. **Association Relationship (associated_with)**: Association relationships between configuration items. For example: SSL certificate is associated with a domain name, and the domain name is associated with an application service.

4. **Inheritance Relationship (inherits_from)**: Inheritance relationships between CI types. For example: Cloud server inherits from Server, MySQL inherits from Relational Database.

5. **Composition Relationship (composed_of)**: Whole-part relationships. For example: K8s cluster is composed of multiple K8s nodes, Redis cluster is composed of multiple Redis nodes.

6. **Connection Relationship (connected_to)**: Network connection relationships. For example: Switch is connected to Server, Router is connected to Switch.

### 2.1.0.16 Version Management Process

#### 2.1.0.16.1 Semantic Versioning Specification

This system adopts Semantic Versioning (Semantic Versioning 2.0.0) specification, with version number format: MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH.

**Version Number Increment Rules:**

- **MAJOR**: Incremented when making incompatible API changes, resetting MINOR and PATCH to 0. For example: upgrading from 1.x.x to 2.0.0.
- **MINOR**: Incremented when adding new functionality in a backward-compatible manner, resetting PATCH to 0. For example: upgrading from 1.1.x to 1.2.0.
- **PATCH**: Incremented when making backward-compatible bug fixes. For example: upgrading from 1.1.1 to 1.1.2.

**Pre-release Version Identifiers:**

- alpha: Internal testing version, e.g., 1.0.0-alpha.1
- beta: Public testing version, e.g., 1.0.0-beta.1
- rc: Release candidate version, e.g., 1.0.0-rc.1

**Version Tag Management:**

- Each release version creates a corresponding Tag in Git, with naming convention v{MAJOR}.{MINOR}.{PATCH}
- Tags must be associated with corresponding Release notes, including four sections: new features, changes, fixes, and known issues
- Each Release must include a changelog (CHANGELOG) recording all changes

#### 2.1.0.16.2 Branch Strategy (Git Flow)

#### Table 2-1-36: Git Branch Strategy

| Branch Name | Branch Type | Naming Convention | Lifecycle | Merge Target | Description |
|------------|-----------|------------------|-----------|-------------|-------------|
| main | Main branch | main | Permanent | / | Production environment code, only accepts release and hotfix merges |
| develop | Development branch | develop | Permanent | / | Development environment code, the main trunk branch for daily development |
| feature/* | Feature branch | feature/{ticket-id}-{desc} | Temporary | develop | New feature development branch |
| release/* | Release branch | release/v{major}.{minor}.{patch} | Temporary | main+develop | Release preparation branch, bug fixes only |
| hotfix/* | Hotfix branch | hotfix/{ticket-id}-{desc} | Temporary | main+develop | Production environment emergency fix branch |
| bugfix/* | Bugfix branch | bugfix/{ticket-id}-{desc} | Temporary | develop | Daily bugfix branch |

**Branch Operation Process:**

1. **Feature Development**: Create feature branch from develop branch, submit Pull Request (PR) to develop branch upon completion, merge after code review.
2. **Release Preparation**: Create release branch from develop branch, perform integration testing and bug fixing, PR to main branch and create Tag after testing passes, simultaneously merge back to develop branch.
3. **Hotfix**: Create hotfix branch from main branch, PR to main and develop branches after fix, and create new Patch version Tag.
4. **Code Merging**: All merges must be done through PRs, requiring at least 2 reviewers to approve. Direct push to main and develop branches is not allowed.

#### 2.1.0.20.2 Technical Debt Assessment Criteria

#### Table 2-1-45: Technical Debt Assessment Criteria

| Assessment Dimension | Weight | Scoring Criteria (1-5 points) | Assessment Method | Threshold |
|---------------------|--------|----------------------------|------------------|-----------|
| Impact Scope | 30% | 1=Single module, 3=Multiple modules, 5=Global impact | Impact analysis | ≥3 points requires priority handling |
| Remediation Cost | 25% | 1=<1 person-day, 3=1-5 person-days, 5=>5 person-days | Workload assessment | ≥4 points requires scheduled handling |
| Business Risk | 25% | 1=No impact, 3=Potential impact, 5=Direct business impact | Risk analysis | ≥3 points requires priority handling |
| Technical Complexity | 20% | 1=Simple fix, 3=Medium complexity, 5=Architecture overhaul | Technical analysis | ≥4 points requires dedicated handling |

#### 2.1.0.20.3 Repayment Priority Ranking Rules

Technical debt priority calculation formula: Priority Score = Impact Scope × 0.3 + Business Risk × 0.25 + (6 - Remediation Cost) × 0.25 + Technical Complexity × 0.2

| Priority | Score Range | Handling Deadline | Handling Method | Approver |
|---------|-----------|------------------|----------------|---------|
| P0 - Critical | ≥4.0 | Within this week | Immediate fix, suspend new feature development | Technical Director |
| P1 - High | 3.0-3.9 | Within this iteration | Include in iteration plan, assign dedicated personnel | Technical Lead |
| P2 - Medium | 2.0-2.9 | Within next iteration | Add to backlog, handle during idle time | Development Lead |
| P3 - Low | 1.0-1.9 | Within 6 months | Track and record, handle when opportunity arises | Development team |

#### 3.1.1.1 Window Interactive Terminal

**I. Equipment Overview**

Window interactive terminals are deployed at all 148 service windows in the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall, serving as the core interactive equipment for the public. The equipment adopts the EVOC EC-2121 industrial-grade touch display all-in-one, with a screen size of 21.5 inches, resolution no less than 1920×1080, and capacitive multi-point touch support. The equipment performs functions including service process guidance, service information display, service evaluation collection, and policy promotion display, with daily continuous operation time of no less than 10 hours and annual operating time of approximately 3,650 hours.

The equipment has been in operation since March 2022, approximately 2 years and 9 months to date, with overall good operating conditions. Based on preliminary inspection and evaluation, the equipment integrity rate is approximately 96.5%, with main faults concentrated in touchscreen drift, intermittent network interface disconnection, and power adapter aging.

**II. Standard Operating Procedures (SOP)**

**SOP-WT-001: Window Interactive Terminal Daily Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure**

**Purpose:** Ensure window interactive terminals are in optimal working condition daily and guarantee continuity of service.

**Scope:** All 148 window interactive terminals in the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall.

**Responsibilities:**
- O&M Engineer: Responsible for executing daily maintenance operations and completing maintenance records
- O&M Supervisor: Responsible for supervising maintenance quality, reviewing maintenance records, and handling exceptions
- On-duty Personnel: Responsible for visual inspection of equipment status during inspection rounds

**Maintenance Frequency:** Once daily, completed before opening (08:00-08:30)

**Operating Steps:**

| Step | Operation Item | Operation Method | Notes | Acceptance Criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Visual Inspection | Visually inspect equipment casing, base, screen bezel | Check for deformation, damage, looseness | Appearance intact and undamaged |
| 2 | Screen Cleaning | Use lint-free cloth with specialized cleaning solution, wipe from center outward | Do not use alcohol or ammonia-based cleaners; avoid scratching screen | No dust, stains, or watermarks |
| 3 | Touchscreen Function Test | Launch touch test software, tap each area of the screen point by point | Must cover four corners and center area of screen | Touch response accurate, no drift |
| 4 | Network Connectivity Test | Open command line tool, ping gateway and server addresses | Continuous ping test 30 times, record latency and packet loss | Latency ≤10ms, packet loss = 0% |
| 5 | Application Launch | Launch service application | Record application startup time | Startup time ≤15 seconds |
| 6 | Service Evaluation Function Test | Simulate public operation of evaluator | Confirm evaluation data can be submitted normally | Evaluation data uploaded in real-time successfully |
| 7 | Power Adapter Check | Use multimeter to measure power adapter output voltage | Measure while equipment is in working state | Voltage deviation ≤±5% |
| 8 | Heat Dissipation Check | Use infrared thermometer to measure equipment casing temperature | Measure rear ventilation area of equipment | Casing temperature ≤45℃ |

**Maintenance Record Template:**

| Date | Window No. | Maintenance Personnel | Inspection Result | Abnormal Situation | Handling Result | Acceptance Signature |
|------|-----------|----------------------|-------------------|-------------------|----------------|---------------------|
| | | | Normal/Abnormal | Description | Description | |
