**SOP-WT-002: Window Interactive Terminal Weekly Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure**

**Maintenance Frequency:** Once weekly (Friday 17:00-18:00)

**Operating Steps:**

| Step | Operation Item | Operation Method | Notes | Acceptance Criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Deep Cleaning | Disassemble equipment casing, use anti-static brush to clean internal dust | Disconnect power before disassembly; wear anti-static wristband | No significant internal dust accumulation |
| 2 | Ventilation Cleaning | Use compressed air can to clean ventilation holes and fans | Keep compressed air can upright, 15-20cm from ventilation holes | Ventilation holes unobstructed |
| 3 | Cable Inspection | Check power cable, network cable, USB cable connection status | Check for cable aging, damage, bending | Cables undamaged, connectors not loose |
| 4 | System Update | Check OS patch updates | Back up system before updates | Patch installation rate 100% |
| 5 | Disk Cleanup | Clean temporary files, log files, and cache files | Confirm important data backed up before cleanup | Disk free space ≥30% |
| 6 | Touch Calibration | Execute touchscreen calibration procedure | Use standard calibration tool during calibration | Touch positioning accuracy ≤2mm |
| 7 | Brightness Detection | Use luminance meter to measure screen center brightness | Display full white screen during measurement | Brightness ≥250cd/m² |

**SOP-WT-003: Window Interactive Terminal Monthly Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure**

**Maintenance Frequency:** Once monthly (last working day of each month)

**Operating Steps:**

| Step | Operation Item | Operation Method | Notes | Acceptance Criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Hardware Diagnostics | Run equipment hardware diagnostics (CPU, memory, hard drive, graphics card, etc.) | Diagnostics take approximately 30 minutes; equipment unavailable during this time | All modules pass diagnostics |
| 2 | Power Supply Detection | Use multimeter to detect power adapter output voltage and current | Measure under full load conditions | Voltage deviation ≤±5% |
| 3 | Heat Dissipation Detection | Use infrared thermometer to detect temperatures at key equipment points | Measure CPU heatsink, power module, screen backplane | All points within normal temperature range |
| 4 | Network Performance Test | Use network tester to test network throughput | Test duration no less than 10 minutes | Throughput ≥90Mbps |
| 5 | Configuration Backup | Backup equipment configuration files and system images | Backup to local and remote storage | Backup completion rate 100% |
| 6 | Wear Parts Inspection | Check fans, buttons, touchscreen bezel and other wear parts | Record wear status, provide early replacement warning | All components operating normally |

**SOP-WT-004: Window Interactive Terminal Quarterly Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure**

**Maintenance Frequency:** Once quarterly (last week of each quarter)

**Operating Steps:**

| Step | Operation Item | Operation Method | Notes | Acceptance Criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Full Disassembly Cleaning | Completely disassemble equipment, clean all internal components | Photograph disassembly process, ensure correct reassembly | All components clean and dust-free |
| 2 | Heat Dissipation System Maintenance | Replace CPU thermal paste, clean cooling fans | Use high-quality thermal paste (thermal conductivity ≥4W/m·K) | Heat dissipation efficiency restored ≥95% |
| 3 | Cable Replacement | Inspect and replace aging cables | Prioritize replacement of cables in use for over 2 years | All cables transmitting normally |
| 4 | Display Detection | Use color analyzer to detect display performance | Detect brightness, contrast, color gamut, color deviation | Color deviation ΔE≤3 |
| 5 | Overall Performance Evaluation | Comprehensive evaluation of equipment performance (hardware + software) | Use professional scoring tools | Performance score ≥80 points |
| 6 | Asset Inventory | Verify equipment asset information and location | Update asset ledger | 100% ledger-physical match rate |

**SOP-WT-005: Window Interactive Terminal Annual Maintenance Standard Operating Procedure**

**Purpose:** Conduct comprehensive deep maintenance of equipment, evaluate equipment health status, and formulate next year's maintenance plan.

**Maintenance Frequency:** Once annually (December each year)

**Operating Steps:**

| Step | Operation Item | Operation Method | Notes | Acceptance Criteria |
|------|---------------|-----------------|-------|-------------------|
| 1 | Comprehensive Hardware Detection | Use professional testing equipment to conduct detailed testing of all hardware modules | Test CPU, memory, hard drive, motherboard, graphics card, power supply, etc. | All modules meet performance standards |
| 2 | Hard Drive Health Assessment | Use SMART tools to detect hard drive health status | Focus on reallocated sector count, pending sector count, uncorrectable sector count | SMART status "Good" |

| 4 | Comprehensive Power Supply Detection | Use power supply tester to detect output voltage and ripple on all rails | Measure under both full load and light load conditions | Voltage deviation ≤±3%, ripple ≤50mV |
| 5 | Display Panel Aging Assessment | Use professional equipment to evaluate display panel brightness decay and color drift | Compare with factory parameters | Brightness decay ≤20%, color deviation ΔE≤5 |
| 6 | Heat Dissipation System Full Maintenance | Replace thermal paste, clean heatsinks, detect fan speeds | Use thermal paste with conductivity ≥4W/m·K | CPU full load temperature ≤75℃ |
| 7 | System Reinstallation and Optimization | Reinstall operating system and perform comprehensive optimization | Install latest patches and drivers | System boot time ≤30 seconds |
| 8 | Equipment Asset Status Assessment | Evaluate overall equipment status, determine need for upgrade or replacement | Comprehensively consider equipment age, failure rate, repair cost | Assessment report complete |

**Common Fault Handling Measures:**

| Fault Symptom | Possible Cause | Handling Measure | Estimated Time |
|--------------|---------------|-----------------|---------------|
| Touchscreen unresponsive | Driver abnormal/hardware fault | Restart device→reinstall driver→replace touchscreen | 30-60 minutes |
| Screen display abnormal | Display cable loose/graphics card fault | Check cable→replace cable→replace graphics card | 45-90 minutes |
| Network connection interrupted | Network cable fault/switch port abnormal | Replace cable→check switch→replace port | 15-30 minutes |
| Device cannot start | Power supply fault/motherboard fault | Replace power adapter→check motherboard→replace motherboard | 30-120 minutes |
| Touch drift | Calibration data lost/screen fault | Recalibrate→replace touchscreen | 20-40 minutes |
| Application crash | System abnormal/insufficient storage | Restart app→clean storage→reinstall app | 10-30 minutes |

**Table 3-8 Window Interactive Terminal Common Fault Handling Measures Table**

**V. Fault Diagnosis Decision Tree**

```
Window Interactive Terminal Fault Diagnosis Decision Tree
├── Cannot Power On
│   ├── Power indicator light off
│   │   ├── Check power outlet for power → No power: Repair power line or replace outlet
│   │   ├── Check power adapter output voltage → No output: Replace with same model adapter
│   │   ├── Check power connection cable → Damaged/broken: Replace power cable
│   │   └── Check motherboard power indicator → Off: Replace motherboard or send for repair
│   └── Power indicator on but no display
│       ├── Check display cable → Loose/oxidized: Reseat or replace cable
│       ├── External display test → External normal: Replace cable/screen module
│       ├── External also no display → Check graphics card/memory: Reseat memory modules
│       └── All above ineffective → Replace graphics card/motherboard
├── Blue Screen/Freeze After Boot
│   ├── Check recent system changes → Changes made: Rollback changes (uninstall updates/restore system)
│   ├── Run memory diagnostics (MemTest86) → Errors found: Replace faulty memory module
│   ├── Check CPU temperature (BIOS/monitoring software) → Overheating (>80℃): Clean cooling system
│   ├── System log analysis → Driver fault: Reinstall or rollback driver
│   └── All above ineffective → Reinstall operating system
├── Touchscreen Abnormal
│   ├── Completely unresponsive
│   │   ├── Check USB connection → Loose/disconnected: Reseat USB cable
│   │   ├── Check Device Manager → Driver abnormal: Reinstall touch driver
│   │   ├── Reinstall touch driver → Ineffective: Check touch controller
│   │   └── Check touch controller → Fault: Replace touch control board
│   ├── Touch drift
│   │   ├── Execute touch calibration → Effective: Complete calibration
│   │   ├── Execute touch calibration → Ineffective: Check electromagnetic interference source
│   │   ├── Check electromagnetic interference → Interference found: Shield/remove interference source
│   │   └── All above ineffective → Replace touchscreen
│   ├── Partial area unresponsive
│   │   ├── Check touchscreen surface → Damage/scratches: Replace touchscreen
│   │   ├── Check touch controller → Fault: Replace control board
│   │   └── Check firmware version → Outdated: Update firmware
│   └── False touch triggers
│       ├── Check screen surface → Water stains/smudges: Clean screen
│       ├── Check ambient humidity → Too high: Dehumidify
│       └── All above ineffective → Replace touchscreen
├── Network Abnormal
│   ├── Complete network disconnection
│   │   ├── Check network cable connection → Loose/disconnected: Reseat or replace cable
│   │   ├── Check switch port indicator → Off: Replace switch port
│   │   ├── Check NIC driver → Abnormal (yellow exclamation): Reinstall driver
│   │   ├── Check NIC hardware → Fault: Replace NIC (USB/PCIe)
│   │   └── Check network configuration → IP conflict: Reconfigure IP address
│   └── Network unstable (intermittent disconnection)
│       ├── Check network bandwidth utilization → Congestion (>80%): Optimize network/increase bandwidth
│       ├── Check network configuration (DNS/gateway) → Error: Correct configuration
│       ├── Check network cable quality (tester) → Crosstalk/attenuation too high: Replace cable
│       ├── Check electromagnetic interference → Interference found: Shield/remove interference source
│       └── Check switch configuration → Port rate limiting/QoS: Adjust configuration
├── Application Abnormal
│   ├── Application cannot start
│   │   ├── Check system resources (CPU/memory) → Insufficient: Release resources/close unrelated processes
│   │   ├── Check application dependencies → Missing: Install dependencies (.NET/VC++ runtime)
│   │   ├── Check application configuration → Corrupted: Restore default configuration
│   │   └── Reinstall application → Ineffective: Reinstall operating system
│   ├── Application crash
│   │   ├── Clean disk space → Space insufficient (<10%): Clean/expand
│   │   ├── Check system compatibility → Incompatible: Update system/install compatible version
│   │   ├── Check application logs → Analyze cause and fix
│   │   └── Check for viruses → Virus found: Disinfect and reinstall
│   └── Application running slowly
│       ├── Check CPU usage → Too high: Optimize application/upgrade hardware
│       ├── Check memory usage → Too high: Add memory
│       └── Check disk I/O → Too high: Optimize disk/replace SSD
└── Peripheral Abnormal
    ├── Card reader not recognized
│   ├── Check USB connection → Loose: Reseat
│   ├── Check driver → Abnormal: Reinstall driver
│   └── All above ineffective → Replace card reader
    ├── Printer not working
    │   ├── Check printer connection → Disconnected: Reconnect
    │   ├── Check print queue → Stuck: Clear queue
    │   └── All above ineffective → Replace printer
    └── Evaluator not responding
        ├── Check connection → Disconnected: Reconnect
        └── All above ineffective → Replace evaluator
```

**VI. Spare Parts Management**

**Spare parts management adopts the ABC classification method:**

- **Class A Spare Parts** (Critical): Touchscreens, motherboards, display modules and other core components, accounting for 60% of total value. Strict inventory control with regular inventory checks.
- **Class B Spare Parts** (Important): Power adapters, network modules, cooling fans, etc., accounting for 25% of total value. Moderate inventory, replenished as needed.
- **Class C Spare Parts** (General): Cables, buttons, casing parts, etc., accounting for 15% of total value. Simplified management, bulk procurement.

**Spare Parts Inventory Management Process:**

```
Procurement Request → Approval → Procurement → Receiving Inspection → Registration → Storage Management → Issue for Use → Usage Record → Inventory Check
```

**Spare Parts List (Including Safety Stock Calculation Formula):**

| Spare Part Name | Specification/Model | Safety Stock | Maximum Stock | Procurement Cycle | Storage Location | Unit Price (CNY) | Safety Stock Calculation |
|----------------|--------------------|--------------|--------------|--------------------|-----------------|-----------------|-------------------------|
| Touchscreen | EC-2121-TP | 10 units | 20 units | 7 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 1,200 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×3.2×√5≈12 |
| Power Adapter | EC-2121-PWR | 15 units | 30 units | 5 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 180 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×2.8×√5≈10 |
| Network Module | EC-2121-NIC | 10 units | 20 units | 7 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 350 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×2.0×√7≈9 |
| Cooling Fan | EC-2121-FAN | 10 units | 20 units | 5 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 85 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×2.5×√5≈9 |
| Motherboard | EC-2121-MB | 5 units | 10 units | 15 working days | Central spare parts warehouse | 2,800 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×1.2×√15≈8 |

| Hard Drive (SSD) | 128GB SATA | 8 units | 16 units | 5 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 220 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×2.0×√5≈7 |
| Memory Module | 4GB DDR3 | 10 units | 20 units | 5 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 120 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×2.5×√5≈9 |
| Touch Control Board | EC-2121-TC | 5 units | 10 units | 10 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 450 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×1.5×√10≈8 |
| Power Board | EC-2121-PB | 5 units | 10 units | 7 working days | Hall spare parts warehouse | 380 | SS=Z×σd×√L=1.65×1.8×√7≈8 |

**Safety Stock Calculation Formula Explanation:**
- SS = Safety Stock Quantity
- Z = Service level coefficient (95% service level corresponds to Z=1.65)
- σd = Standard deviation of daily consumption
- L = Procurement lead time (working days)
- Formula: SS = Z × σd × √L

```
High-Speed Document Camera Abnormal
├── Cannot Capture Image
│   ├── Check USB connection → Loose: Reseat
│   ├── Check USB port → Fault: Change port
│   ├── Reinstall driver → Ineffective: Replace device
│   └── Check camera hardware → Fault: Replace camera module
├── Blurry Image
│   ├── Check lens → Contaminated: Clean lens
│   ├── Test auto focus → Stuck: Repair focus mechanism
│   ├── Check focus motor → Fault: Replace motor
│   └── All above ineffective → Replace camera module
├── Image Distortion
│   ├── Check calibration data → Lost: Recalibrate
│   ├── Check lens → Damaged: Replace lens
│   └── All above ineffective → Replace camera module
├── Uneven Fill Light
│   ├── Check LED light strip → Partial bead decay: Replace light strip
│   └── Check driver board → Fault: Replace driver board
└── Color Deviation
    ├── Execute white balance calibration → Ineffective: Recalibrate
    ├── Check color parameters → Lost: Recalibrate
    └── All above ineffective → Replace camera module
```

```
Safety Stock = (Maximum Daily Consumption × Maximum Replenishment Cycle) - (Average Daily Consumption × Average Replenishment Cycle)
```

## 4.1 O&M Plan for Hall Queue Ticket Dispensing, Calling, and Window Configuration Functions

### 4.1.1 Function Overview

The queue ticket dispensing and calling system is the core functional module of the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall informatization system, serving as the first point of contact for providing queuing services to the public. The system adopts a distributed architecture design, with multiple subsystems—including ticket dispensing terminals, calling control, display terminals, and voice announcements—working collaboratively.

**System Architecture:**

```
┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐    ┌─────────────┐
│  Ticket      │───→│  Application │───→│  Database    │    │  Display     │
│  Dispensing  │    │  Server      │    │  Server      │    │  Terminal    │
│  Terminal    │    │  (Business   │    │  (Data       │    │ (LED/LCD)   │
│ (Standing/   │    │   Logic)     │    │  Storage)    │    │             │
│  Desktop)    │    │              │    │              │    │             │
└─────────────┘    └──────┬──────┘    └─────────────┘    └─────────────┘
                          │
                   ┌──────┴──────┐
                   │  Voice       │
                   │  Announcement│
                   │  System      │
                   │ (Power Amp/  │
                   │  Speakers)   │
                   └─────────────┘
```

**Figure 4-1 Queue Ticket Dispensing and Calling System Architecture Diagram**

**Business Process:**

After arriving at the hall, members of the public select the service category at the ticket dispensing terminal. The system automatically assigns a queue number and prints a ticket receipt. Based on the service capacity of each window, the system intelligently assigns service windows and notifies the public via display screens and voice announcements to proceed to the designated window. Window staff complete the calling operation through the call station keyboard.

**Daily Service Volume:**

| Metric | Data |
|--------|------|
| Daily Ticket Dispensing Volume | 800–1,200 person-times |
| Daily Calling Volume | 750–1,150 person-times |
| Peak Hour Ticket Dispensing Volume | 300–400 person-times/hour |
| Average Waiting Time | 15–25 minutes |
| Average Processing Time | 8–15 minutes |

**Table 4-1 Daily Service Volume Statistics of the Queue Ticket Dispensing and Calling System**

### 4.1.4 Function Optimization Measures

**1. Queuing Algorithm Optimization**

- **Intelligent Load Balancing**: Intelligently recommend the optimal window based on the current waiting count and average processing time at each window
- **Priority Management**: Establish priority calling mechanisms for special groups such as the elderly and persons with disabilities
- **Appointment Integration**: Integrate appointment users and on-site ticket dispensing users into a unified queue, with rational allocation based on appointment time slots
- **Dynamic Adjustment**: Dynamically adjust calling weights for various service categories based on real-time business volume

**2. Display Optimization**

- **Multi-Screen Synchronization**: Enable coordinated display across display terminals in different areas to avoid information silos
- **Adaptive Layout**: Automatically adjust interface layout based on display terminal dimensions
- **Real-Time Refresh**: Refresh display content in real-time with latency ≤1 second
- **Emergency Broadcast**: Support instant insertion of emergency notifications

**3. Voice Optimization**

- **Multi-Zone Audio Control**: Enable independent volume control for different zones
- **Speed Adjustment**: Support flexible adjustment of announcement speech speed
- **Multi-Language Support**: Support announcements in Mandarin and local dialects
- **Anti-Feedback Processing**: Employ digital audio processing technology to prevent acoustic feedback

## 4.2 O&M Plan for Appointment-Based Ticket Dispensing and Wait Time Inquiry Functions

### 4.2.1 Function Overview

The appointment-based ticket dispensing and wait time inquiry functions are important extensions of the queue ticket dispensing and calling system, enabling the public to pre-book service appointments through multiple channels and inquire about real-time wait status, effectively reducing on-site waiting time.

**Appointment Channels:**

| Channel | Description | Daily Appointment Volume |
|---------|-------------|--------------------------|
| "Xiang Yi Ban" APP | Hunan Provincial Government Service Platform mobile application | 200–300 person-times |
| "Xiang Yi Ban" Mini Program | WeChat Mini Program | 150–250 person-times |
| Hall Self-Service Terminals | On-site self-service appointment | 50–100 person-times |
| Online Service Hall | Web-based appointment | 100–150 person-times |

**Table 4-4 Appointment Channels and Daily Appointment Volume**

**Appointment Process:**

```
User selects service category → Selects date and time slot → Fills in basic information → Confirms appointment → Generates appointment code
                                                          │
Arrives at hall ← Appointment reminder ← System sends SMS reminder ← 30-minute advance reminder ←┘
    │
    ↓
Scans code at self-service terminal to check in → Automatically enters queue → Waits for calling → Processes business
```

### 4.2.5 System Optimization Measures

**1. Appointment Algorithm Optimization**

- **Intelligent Time Slot Recommendation**: Recommend less crowded time slots based on historical data
- **Dynamic Capacity Control**: Dynamically adjust appointment capacity for each time slot based on actual business volume
- **No-Show Prediction**: Predict no-show probability based on user profiles, and rationally release no-show slots
- **Standby Mechanism**: Automatically notify standby users upon no-shows

**2. Wait Time Prediction Model**

- **Multi-Dimensional Prediction**: Comprehensively consider factors such as service category, number of windows, and current queue length
- **Machine Learning Optimization**: Employ machine learning algorithms to continuously optimize the prediction model
- **Real-Time Correction**: Correct prediction values in real-time based on actual processing situations
- **Confidence Interval**: Provide confidence intervals for prediction results

# Chapter 5: Fault Handling Process


## 5.1 Hotline Service Flowchart

### 5.1.1 Process Overview

The hotline service is the primary access channel for the operation and maintenance services of this project, serving as the unified reception and dispatch hub for fault reporting, information consultation, service requests, complaints, and suggestions. The service hotline operates on a 7×24-hour on-duty system, ensuring timely response to the Procuring Entity's needs at all times.

This process aims to standardize the full-process operations of the hotline service, ensuring that every incoming call is handled promptly, accurately, and efficiently, achieving the service goals of "unified reception, classified handling, unified follow-up, and closed-loop management." The hotline service process covers the entire workflow from incoming call reception to work order closure, through standardized operating procedures and rigorous quality control, to ensure that service levels meet all indicators specified in the SLA agreement.

The hotline service adheres to the following basic principles:
- **First-Contact Responsibility**: The first on-duty personnel to answer the call is the primary responsible person, accountable for end-to-end tracking until the issue is resolved or a handover is completed;
- **Time-Limited Completion**: All matters must be handled within specified time limits without unjustified delays;
- **Closed-Loop Management**: Every service record forms a complete closed loop from reception to completion, ensuring every matter receives a response and every item is properly addressed;
- **Full Traceability**: All call records, work order information, and handling processes are fully documented, supporting post-incident tracing and auditing;
- **Service Standardization**: All service scripts, handling procedures, and quality standards are uniformly regulated to ensure service consistency;
- **Information Confidentiality**: Sensitive information involving the Procuring Entity's business data, system configurations, etc., must be kept strictly confidential and shall not be disclosed;
- **Continuous Improvement**: Service data is regularly analyzed to identify improvement opportunities and continuously optimize service processes and quality;
- **Customer Orientation**: Customer needs are central, proactively providing service experiences that exceed expectations.

The hotline service team is composed of the following personnel:
- **Hotline Supervisor**: 1 person, responsible for daily management, quality monitoring, and performance evaluation of the hotline team;
- **On-Duty Engineers**: 2 persons per shift, responsible for 7×24-hour hotline answering, problem diagnosis, and work order processing;
- **Technical Support Engineers**: 3 persons, responsible for remote technical support and escalation handling of complex issues;
- **Quality Monitor**: 1 person, responsible for service quality spot checks, work order quality inspection, and satisfaction analysis;
- **Training Specialist**: 1 person, responsible for new employee training, script updates, and skill enhancement;
- **Data Analyst**: 1 person, responsible for hotline data statistics, trend analysis, and report compilation.

The technical support infrastructure for the hotline service includes:
- **Operation and Maintenance Management System**: Provides core functions such as work order management, knowledge base query, and statistical analysis;
- **Call Center System**: Supports incoming call pop-up, call recording, queue management, call traffic statistics, and other functions;
- **Remote Assistance Tools**: Supports remote desktop, file transfer, screen sharing, and other remote support functions;
- **Mobile O&M APP**: Supports mobile work order acceptance, on-site photo capture, electronic check-in, and other mobile functions;
- **SMS/WeChat Notification Platform**: Supports work order notifications, progress reminders, satisfaction surveys, and other message push functions;
- **Intelligent Voice Analysis System**: Supports speech-to-text, emotion recognition, keyword extraction, and other intelligent analysis functions;
- **Large-Screen Display System**: Real-time display of hotline answering status, work order processing status, SLA compliance status, and other key indicators.

### 5.1.2 Detailed Process Description

**Step 1: Incoming Call Reception and Greeting (Response Time ≤10 seconds)**

On-duty personnel answer the phone within 10 seconds of the ring, using the standard greeting: "Hello, this is the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall Informatization Project O&M Service Hotline. I am on-duty engineer XX. How may I assist you?"

Upon answering, the on-duty personnel immediately creates a new service work order in the O&M management system, recording basic information such as incoming call time and caller number. For calls during business hours (8:30-12:00, 14:00-17:30), the call must be answered within 3 rings; for calls during non-business hours, on-duty personnel must answer within 10 seconds, ensuring no gaps in nighttime duty coverage.

On-duty personnel should maintain a friendly tone, moderate speech speed, clear articulation, and provide service in Mandarin. During the greeting, actively listen to the caller's expression, do not interrupt, and preliminarily determine the type and urgency of the call. For callers using dialects or foreign languages, on-duty personnel should attempt to communicate in the corresponding language and, if necessary, transfer to multilingual support personnel.

Quality standards for incoming call reception:
- Hotline answer rate ≥99%, meaning no more than 1% of total incoming calls go unanswered per month;
- Answer rate within 3 rings ≥95%, ensuring the vast majority of calls are answered within 3 rings;
- Greeting script usage rate 100%, using the standard greeting for every incoming call;
- Work order creation timeliness rate 100%, creating work orders immediately after call reception.

Notes for incoming call reception:
- In case of call queuing, play the standard waiting prompt: "Hello, your call is being connected. Please wait. Thank you for your patience."
- If the system fails and work orders cannot be created, use paper work orders for temporary recording, with system entry within 24 hours after system recovery;
- For special numbers such as "110," "119," "120," immediately initiate the special handling process;
- For callers who are emotionally agitated or unclear in expression, on-duty personnel should remain patient and use guided questioning to help callers accurately describe issues;
- For callers using dialects, on-duty personnel should attempt bilingual communication in both Mandarin and the dialect;
- For callers using foreign languages, on-duty personnel should transfer to multilingual support personnel or use translation tools to assist communication.

**Step 2: Information Registration and Requirement Confirmation (Recording Time ≤3 minutes)**

After confirming the type of incoming call matter, the on-duty personnel registers the following information completely according to the work order template:
- **Basic Information**: Caller's name, affiliated department, contact phone number, incoming call time;
- **Matter Category**: Fault reporting (hardware fault, software fault, network fault), information consultation, service request, complaint or suggestion;
- **Matter Description**: Fault symptoms, impact scope, occurrence time, whether it has occurred for the first time;
- **Urgency Level**: Preliminarily classified as urgent, important, or general based on the impact of the fault on Government Service Hall operations;
- **Associated Information**: Involved equipment numbers, system modules, location areas, etc.;
- **Historical Association**: Query whether the caller/department/equipment has similar recent service records.

After information registration is complete, the on-duty personnel recites the key information to the caller for confirmation: "Hello, let me confirm with you: you are reporting that the XX system in the XX area is experiencing XX issue, is that correct?" Ensure the information recorded is accurate. For unclear descriptions or incomplete information, on-duty personnel should politely guide the caller to provide necessary details.

The accuracy rate of recording must reach 98% or above, meaning no fewer than 98 out of every 100 work orders contain complete and accurate information. The on-duty supervisor randomly inspects 10% of work order records daily for quality verification.

Notes for information registration:
- For calls involving sensitive information (such as passwords, account numbers, etc.), do not record them over the phone; guide the caller to reset through secure means;
- For cases where multiple people report the same issue, record subsequent caller information in the first work order to avoid duplicate work order creation;
- When the caller's self-reported fault level does not match the actual situation, on-duty personnel should use professional knowledge to judge and correct;
- After work order creation, the system automatically generates a unique work order number in the format "YYMMDD-XXXX" for subsequent tracking;
- When caller-provided information contains contradictions or questionable points, on-duty personnel should clarify information by asking the 5W1H questions (When, Where, Who, What, Why, How).

**Step 3: Problem Diagnosis and Classified Processing (Diagnosis Time ≤5 minutes)**

Based on the problem symptoms described by the caller and combined with historical cases and solutions in the knowledge base, on-duty personnel perform preliminary problem diagnosis. Based on the diagnosis results, classified processing is carried out according to the following standards:

- **Remotely Resolvable Issues**: Such as software operation guidance, password resets, simple configuration adjustments, etc. On-duty personnel immediately guide the caller to resolve the issue via phone or remote assistance tools, and records the solution and handling result in the work order;
- **Issues Requiring Work Order Dispatch**: Such as hardware faults, system downtime, network interruptions, and other faults requiring on-site handling. On-duty personnel creates a formal maintenance work order through the O&M management system, filling in complete fault descriptions, preliminary diagnosis results, suggested handling plans, and urgency level, and dispatches it to the corresponding O&M team;
- **Matters Requiring Escalation**: Such as issues involving system architecture, matters requiring vendor support, major fault incidents, etc. On-duty personnel immediately reports to the on-duty supervisor for coordinated handling;
- **Matters Requiring Transfer**: Such as issues falling within the responsibility scope of other departments (e.g., property management, renovation and construction, etc.). On-duty personnel records relevant information and transfers to the corresponding department, then tracks the transfer result.

During the diagnosis process, on-duty personnel should fully utilize the knowledge base function of the O&M management system, searching historical fault cases and solutions to improve the first-call resolution rate. For new types of faults without matching records in the knowledge base, on-duty personnel should document fault symptoms and handling processes in detail, creating new knowledge entries for the knowledge base.

The dispatch accuracy rate must reach 95% or above, meaning no fewer than 95 out of every 100 dispatched work orders have the correct dispatch target and handling plan.

Notes for problem diagnosis:
- For issues with vague descriptions or incomplete information, on-duty personnel should clarify fault symptoms by asking key questions (5W1H: When, Where, Who, What, Why, How);
- For faults that may involve security incidents (such as system intrusion, data tampering, etc.), immediately initiate the security incident handling process and notify the information security department;
- When the problem described by the caller does not match the actual system monitoring status, on-duty personnel should prioritize system monitoring data while recording the caller's description as reference;
- If the knowledge base system is unavailable during diagnosis, on-duty personnel may use offline knowledge base documents or contact technical support engineers for assistance;
- For complex issues involving multiple systems or specialties, on-duty personnel should identify the primary responsible specialty and assisting specialties during the diagnosis stage to avoid work order buck-passing after dispatch.

**Step 4: Work Order Dispatch and Task Assignment (Dispatch Time ≤3 minutes)**

For faults requiring on-site handling, on-duty personnel complete work order dispatch in the O&M management system. The following rules are followed during dispatch:

- **Proximity Principle**: Prioritize dispatching O&M engineers closest to the fault location to reduce arrival time;
- **Professional Matching Principle**: Dispatch engineers with corresponding professional skills based on fault type—hardware faults to hardware engineers, network faults to network engineers, software faults to software engineers;
- **Load Balancing Principle**: Under the premise of professional matching, consider the current task load of each engineer to avoid overloading individual engineers;
- **Primary-Backup Complement Principle**: Each professional position has a primary (A) and backup (B) person, with A as the first responsible person and B as substitute when A cannot respond;
- **Skill Level Principle**: Complex or difficult faults are prioritized for senior engineers, while simple faults can be handled by junior engineers, enabling talent development and resource optimization.

After work order dispatch, the system automatically notifies the corresponding O&M engineer via SMS, APP push notification, etc. Upon receiving the dispatch notification, the O&M engineer must confirm acceptance within 5 minutes. If no one confirms within 5 minutes, the system automatically escalates the notification to the team leader for manual assignment. If the team leader still has not assigned within 3 minutes, the system further escalates the notification to the O&M project manager.

Notes for work order dispatch:
- For P1-level urgent faults, the system simultaneously broadcasts notifications to all relevant engineers to ensure the fastest possible response;
- For faults requiring special skills or special permissions, the system automatically matches engineers with corresponding qualifications;
- For complex faults involving multiple specialties, the system automatically creates linked work orders, dispatching them to the corresponding specialty engineers and designating a primary responsible engineer for coordination;
- After work order dispatch, the system records key time nodes such as dispatch time, dispatch target, and confirmation time for subsequent SLA assessment;
- For P1 and P2 level faults, the system automatically sends notifications to the handling engineer's supervisor after work order dispatch to ensure management is informed of important fault handling progress.

**Step 5: Process Tracking and Progress Feedback (Tracking Interval ≤30 minutes)**

After work order dispatch, on-duty personnel are responsible for tracking the work order processing progress to ensure faults are handled promptly. The tracking mechanism is as follows:

- **Routine Work Orders**: On-duty personnel check work order status updates every 30 minutes to confirm whether the engineer has arrived on-site and whether fault handling has begun;
- **Urgent Work Orders**: On-duty personnel track every 15 minutes and provide timely progress feedback to the caller;
- **Timeout Warning**: When work order processing time approaches the response time limit specified in the SLA, the system automatically issues a warning. On-duty personnel immediately contacts the handling engineer to confirm progress and, if necessary, coordinates reinforcement.

On-duty personnel proactively provide progress feedback to the caller at the following time points:
- Within 10 minutes after work order dispatch: Inform the caller that an engineer has been assigned with estimated arrival time;
- After the engineer arrives on-site: Inform the caller of arrival and that processing is underway;
- After fault handling is complete: Inform the caller that the issue has been repaired and ask to confirm service status;
- If processing time needs to be extended: Proactively inform the caller of the reason and estimated extension time, obtaining understanding and consent.

Notes for process tracking:
- If during tracking the engineer's handling plan is found to be inconsistent with the work order description, on-duty personnel should promptly communicate with the engineer for confirmation and, if necessary, adjust the handling plan;
- For work orders where processing time exceeds 50% of the SLA time limit, on-duty personnel should proactively contact the engineer to understand the reason and assess whether reinforcement is needed;
- For work orders where the caller has called multiple times to follow up, on-duty personnel should increase tracking frequency to every 10 minutes and provide timely feedback on the latest progress;
- Tracking records should be fully documented in the work order system, including tracking time, tracking content, tracked person, feedback results, etc.;
- For P1-level faults, on-duty personnel should report handling progress to the supervisor every 5 minutes to ensure management has real-time situational awareness.

**Step 6: Result Confirmation and Work Order Review (Confirmation Time ≤15 minutes after completion)**

After fault handling is complete, the O&M engineer fills in the handling result report in the O&M management system, including:
- Fault cause analysis;
- Handling measures and solutions;
- List of replaced spare parts (if applicable);
- Before-and-after comparison test results;
- Preventive recommendations (if applicable);
- On-site handling photos (if applicable);
- Issues encountered during handling and outstanding matters.

After receiving the handling result report, on-duty personnel calls the caller within 15 minutes to confirm whether the fault has been completely resolved and whether the service is satisfactory. After confirmation is complete, on-duty personnel reviews the work order, checking the following:
- Work order information is complete and accurate;
- Handling process records are detailed with clear logic;
- Handling results are consistent with the fault description;
- Caller satisfaction feedback has been recorded;
- Spare parts usage records are consistent with inventory changes;
- Linked work order statuses have been synchronized and updated.

After review approval, on-duty personnel updates the work order status to "Closed." If incomplete work order information or issues with handling results are found, the work order is returned to the handling engineer for supplementation.

Notes for work order review:
- If handling results are found to be inconsistent with the fault description during review, on-duty personnel should confirm with the handling engineer by phone and, if necessary, arrange a second on-site visit;
- For work orders where the caller reports dissatisfaction, on-duty personnel should record the reasons for dissatisfaction in detail and arrange a follow-up or secondary handling within 24 hours;
- Spare parts usage records should be reconciled with the inventory management system to ensure consistency between records and actual inventory;
- After work order closure, the system automatically sends a satisfaction survey SMS to the caller, inviting them to evaluate the service;
- For P1 and P2 level fault work orders, review must be jointly confirmed by the on-duty supervisor to ensure handling quality.

**Step 7: Follow-Up Summary and Knowledge Crystallization (Follow-Up Time ≤24 hours after work order closure)**

After work order closure, on-duty personnel conducts a follow-up within 24 hours, covering:
- Confirming the fault has not recurred and the system is operating stably;
- Understanding the engineer's service attitude, professional level, and other evaluations;
- Collecting the caller's improvement suggestions for O&M services;
- Recording the caller's other needs.

After the follow-up is complete, on-duty personnel supplements the follow-up records in the work order system. For issues discovered during the follow-up, secondary handling is arranged promptly.

Each week, the service hotline team leader compiles the week's work order data, analyzing fault type distribution, high-frequency issues, handling timeliness, and other indicators to form a weekly report. For repeatedly occurring typical faults, the technical team is organized to analyze root causes, develop preventive measures, and update the knowledge base.

Notes for follow-up summary:
- Standard follow-up scripts should be used during follow-up to ensure consistency of follow-up content;
- For new issues reported by callers during follow-up, new service work orders should be created in the O&M management system;
- Improvement suggestions raised by callers during follow-up should be recorded in the "Service Improvement Suggestions Summary Table" and periodically organized for review and implementation;
- Follow-up records should contain complete information including follow-up time, follow-up method, follow-up content, caller feedback, handling measures, etc.;
- For P1-level faults, follow-up should be conducted within 4 hours after work order closure to ensure the fault is completely resolved.

### 5.1.5 Script Specifications

**Standard Greeting:**
> "Hello, this is the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall Informatization Project O&M Service Hotline. I am on-duty engineer XX. How may I assist you?"

**Information Confirmation Script:**
> "Hello, let me confirm with you: you are reporting that the [specific area]'s [specific system/equipment] is experiencing [specific issue], is that correct?"

**Waiting Script:**
> "Please wait a moment while I query the relevant information for you. This is expected to take approximately X minutes. Thank you for your patience."

**Dispatch Notification Script:**
> "Hello, we have arranged a [professional category] engineer for you, estimated to arrive on-site within [X] minutes. Please keep your phone accessible. We will contact you promptly if there are any changes."

**Progress Feedback Script:**
> "Hello, I would like to provide you with the latest update: our engineer has [arrived on-site / is currently processing / has completed handling]. The current status is [specific progress], and normal operation is expected to be restored within [time]."

**Closing Script:**
> "Thank you for calling. If you have any further questions, please feel free to call our service hotline at any time. Wishing you a productive day. Goodbye!"

**Complaint Handling Script:**
> "We sincerely apologize for the inconvenience. I will immediately escalate the issue you have reported to the relevant responsible person, who will respond to you within [time]. Thank you for your understanding and support."

**Escalation Notification Script:**
> "Hello, the issue you reported has been transferred to our [supervisor / technical expert] for handling. They will proactively contact you within [time]. Please rest assured."

**Follow-Up Script:**
> "Hello, this is the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall Informatization Project O&M Service Hotline. We would like to conduct a follow-up regarding the [specific issue] you previously reported. Is the equipment currently operating normally? Are you satisfied with our service?"

### 5.1.6 Emergency Escalation Mechanism

The hotline service establishes a three-level emergency escalation mechanism:

- **Level 1 Escalation (On-Duty Engineer → On-Duty Supervisor)**: On-duty engineers immediately report to the on-duty supervisor when encountering the following situations: the same fault affects more than 3 windows or business departments; the caller is emotionally agitated or files a complaint; the fault involves core business functions of the system; the on-duty engineer cannot determine the handling plan.
- **Level 2 Escalation (On-Duty Supervisor → O&M Project Manager)**: On-duty supervisors immediately report to the O&M project manager when encountering the following situations: the fault is expected to exceed 2 hours without recovery; the fault involves multi-system coordinated failures; coordination with external vendors or resource support is required; the Procuring Entity's leadership is concerned or inquiring about the matter.
- **Level 3 Escalation (O&M Project Manager → Company Senior Management)**: O&M project managers immediately report to company senior management when encountering the following situations: the fault causes widespread business interruption at the Government Service Hall; data security incidents are involved; the Procuring Entity issues written complaints or rectification requirements; major resources need to be mobilized at the company level.

All escalation levels must complete telephone notification within 5 minutes and written situation reports within 10 minutes. After escalation, the responsible person at the upper level must respond and provide handling instructions within 15 minutes.

## 5.2 On-Site Service Flowchart

### 5.2.1 Process Overview

On-site service refers to the process where O&M engineers, based on work order assignments, visit the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall to perform equipment maintenance, fault repair, system debugging, and other O&M services. On-site service is a core component of the O&M service system, directly affecting fault recovery speed and service quality.

This process aims to standardize the full-process operations of on-site service, establishing a standardized workflow from work order reception to service completion, ensuring that every on-site service can be completed efficiently, professionally, and in compliance with regulations. On-site service follows the basic requirements of "thorough preparation, standardized operations, courteous service, and complete documentation."

On-site service team configuration:
- **Hardware O&M Engineers**: 3 persons, responsible for maintenance and fault repair of servers, storage devices, terminal equipment, and other hardware;
- **Network O&M Engineers**: 2 persons, responsible for maintenance and fault repair of network equipment, structured cabling, network security, and other network-related items;
- **Software O&M Engineers**: 2 persons, responsible for maintenance and fault repair of operating systems, application software, databases, and other software-related items;
- **Comprehensive O&M Engineers**: 2 persons, responsible for maintenance and fault repair of UPS, air conditioning, fire suppression, and other data center infrastructure.

### 5.2.2 Detailed Process Description

**Step 1: Work Order Reception and Task Confirmation (Response Time ≤5 minutes)**

After receiving work order notifications via mobile APP or O&M management system, O&M engineers must confirm acceptance within 5 minutes. When confirming acceptance, the engineer should carefully read the work order information, including:
- Fault location (floor, area, window number);
- Fault type (hardware/software/network);
- Fault description and preliminary diagnosis results;
- Urgency level and response time requirements;
- Reporter's contact information.

If the engineer is unable to respond promptly due to handling other urgent work orders, they must apply for reassignment through the system within 3 minutes, and the service hotline will reassign. After confirming acceptance, the engineer should immediately contact the reporter by phone to confirm whether the fault symptom still exists and inform the estimated arrival time.

**Step 2: Service Preparation (Preparation Time ≤15 minutes)**

After accepting the work order, the engineer performs thorough service preparation based on the fault type:
- **Tool Preparation**: Prepare corresponding maintenance tools based on fault type, including laptop, multimeter, network cable tester, screwdriver set, anti-static wristband, spare network cables, USB adapters, etc.;
- **Spare Parts Preparation**: Carry commonly needed spare parts, including memory modules, hard drives, network cards, keyboards and mice, network cables, power modules, etc.;
- **Documentation Preparation**: Review technical documentation, historical maintenance records, and emergency response plans for the equipment type;
- **Protective Equipment Preparation**: Prepare anti-static gloves, shoe covers, workbench covers, and other protective supplies.

Before departure, the engineer should re-verify that all tools and spare parts are complete, ensuring that handling work can begin immediately upon arrival at the site, avoiding second trips due to insufficient preparation.

**Step 3: On-Site Arrival and Check-In (Arrival Time per SLA Specifications)**

The engineer arrives at the service hall on-site within the time limit specified by the SLA. Post-arrival operating procedures are as follows:
- Perform electronic check-in at the designated O&M check-in point, recording arrival time;
- Proactively present work credentials and wear the company-issued ID badge;
- Contact the reporter to confirm the fault location and politely request guidance to the faulty equipment;
- While proceeding to the fault location, maintain professional demeanor and refrain from loud conversations in public areas.

**Step 4: Fault Diagnosis and Handling Plan Confirmation (Diagnosis Time ≤15 minutes)**

After reaching the faulty equipment, the engineer performs diagnosis following these steps:
- Observe the equipment's operating status, checking indicator lights, screen displays, connection cables, etc.;
- Inquire with the reporter about the specific circumstances of the fault occurrence, including occurrence time, triggering operations, impact scope, etc.;
- Use professional tools for testing, such as network connectivity tests, hardware diagnostic tools, system log analysis, etc.;
- Perform comprehensive analysis to determine the fault cause and location.

After diagnosis is complete, the engineer explains the fault cause and handling plan to the reporter, informing the estimated handling time. If equipment replacement or extended maintenance is required, the reporter's consent should be obtained, and temporary alternatives should be provided (such as deploying backup equipment) to ensure government service operations are not interrupted.

**Step 5: Fault Handling and Repair (Handling Time per SLA Specifications)**

After the handling plan is confirmed, the engineer performs fault handling according to standard operating procedures:
- Back up relevant data before handling (where applicable);
- Operate according to equipment maintenance manuals or technical plans;
- During operations, observe anti-static and damage prevention precautions, handling items with care;
- When replacing spare parts, record the old spare part's model, serial number, and fault symptoms;
- Maintain communication with the reporter during handling, providing timely progress updates.

For software faults, the engineer should confirm the system version and patch status before handling and perform functional testing after completion to ensure the issue is completely resolved. For hardware faults, complete hardware self-tests and functional tests should be performed after spare part replacement. For network faults, network connectivity tests and bandwidth tests should be performed after repair to confirm the network has returned to normal.

**Step 6: Result Verification and On-Site Cleanup (Verification Time ≤10 minutes)**

After fault handling is complete, the engineer performs the following verification and cleanup work:
- **Functional Verification**: Start the equipment, test related functions item by item, and confirm the fault has been completely resolved;
- **Performance Check**: Verify that the equipment's operating status is within normal parameters;
- **Associated Check**: Check whether other equipment and systems related to this equipment are operating normally;
- **On-Site Cleanup**: Collect tools, clean up removed old spare parts and packaging materials, and restore on-site cleanliness;
- **Equipment Restoration**: Return equipment and cables to their original positions, ensuring the site is clean and orderly.

After verification is complete, request the reporter to confirm on-site that the equipment is operating normally and sign the work order for confirmation.

**Step 7: Work Order Completion and Service Report (Completion Time ≤30 minutes after handling)**

After on-site service is complete, the engineer fills in a complete service report in the O&M management system:
- Detailed fault cause analysis;
- Handling process and specific operating steps;
- List of spare parts used (model, quantity, source);
- Before-and-after comparison test data;
- Preventive recommendations and follow-up precautions;
- On-site service photos (where applicable).

After the service report is submitted, the service hotline on-duty personnel conducts a quality follow-up to confirm the reporter's satisfaction with the service result. The work order is formally closed, and relevant materials are archived.

### 5.2.4 SLA Indicators

| SLA Indicator Name | Target Value | Calculation Method | Assessment Period |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Urgent Fault Arrival Time | ≤15 minutes | Time from work order acceptance to on-site arrival | Per incident |
| Important Fault Arrival Time | ≤30 minutes | Time from work order acceptance to on-site arrival | Per incident |
| General Fault Arrival Time | ≤60 minutes | Time from work order acceptance to on-site arrival | Per incident |
| First-Visit Fix Rate | ≥85% | Work orders fixed on first visit ÷ Total on-site work orders × 100% | Monthly |
| Fault Repair Rate | ≥99% | Successfully repaired work orders ÷ Total work orders × 100% | Monthly |
| On-Time Arrival Rate | ≥95% | Arrivals within specified time limit ÷ Total on-site visits × 100% | Monthly |
| Customer Satisfaction | ≥92% | Satisfactory evaluations ÷ Total follow-ups × 100% | Monthly |
| Work Order Report Completeness | 100% | Work orders with complete reports ÷ Total work orders × 100% | Monthly |

### 5.2.5 Service Standards

**Dress Code:**
- Wear company-issued uniforms, kept clean and undamaged;
- Wear ID badge with clearly visible information;
- Wear anti-static work clothes and shoe covers when entering data centers and other critical areas;
- Wearing slippers, vests, shorts, or other inappropriate clothing is prohibited.

**Tool Standards:**
- Use company-issued standard toolboxes with complete tools in good condition;
- Carry a laptop with pre-installed necessary O&M tools and software;
- Carry commonly used spare parts, stored in categorized order with clear labels;
- Return tools to their proper places after use, keeping the toolbox clean.

**Etiquette Standards:**
- Proactively present credentials when entering the hall, cooperating with security inspections;
- Communicate with reporters with a polite attitude and calm tone, using civilized language;
- No smoking, eating, or loud conversations at the service site;
- Do not touch equipment unrelated to the fault;
- If items need to be moved during handling, obtain consent first and handle with care;
- Proactively clean up the site after service completion, restoring original conditions;
- Do not linger in the hall for extended periods; leave promptly after handling is complete.

**Operating Standards:**
- Operate strictly according to equipment maintenance manuals and technical plans; do not unilaterally change handling plans;
- Changes involving system configuration must be approved by the O&M project manager before execution;
- Perform data backup before operations to ensure no data loss due to maintenance activities;
- All removed waste spare parts must be collected uniformly and shall not be left on-site;
- For faults beyond one's capability scope, report promptly and do not attempt blind operations.

## 5.3 On-Site Service Process

### 5.3.1 Process Overview

On-site service refers to the daily O&M activities conducted by the O&M team at the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall, including equipment inspection, preventive maintenance, system monitoring, performance optimization, technical support, etc. On-site service is the foundational work for ensuring the stable operation of informatization systems, reducing fault occurrence rates through proactive identification and elimination of potential hazards, and ensuring business continuity of the Government Service Hall.

This process aims to standardize the full-process operations of on-site service, establishing a scientific and systematic inspection and maintenance system to ensure that every O&M activity has standards to follow, records to reference, and evaluations to rely on. On-site service follows the principle of "prevention first, combination of prevention and treatment, refined management, and continuous improvement."

### 5.3.2 Detailed Process Description

**Step 1: Work Plan Preparation and Approval**

Every Friday, the O&M project manager organizes the preparation of the following week's on-site service work plan, including:
- Inspection routes and inspection points;
- Key maintenance equipment and system lists;
- Preventive maintenance items and operational plans;
- Personnel assignment and time arrangements;
- Required tools, spare parts, and materials lists.

After the work plan is prepared, it is submitted to the Procuring Entity's O&M management responsible person for review and approval. For maintenance projects involving system downtime or business interruption, maintenance applications must be submitted 3 working days in advance and can only be executed after approval by the Procuring Entity.

**Step 2: Pre-Shift Preparation and Task Assignment**

Before the start of daily work (8:00), the O&M team holds a pre-shift meeting (10 minutes), covering:
- Briefing on the previous day's work completion and system operating status;
- Assignment of the day's work tasks, clarifying each person's responsibilities;
- Emphasis on safety precautions and operating standards;
- Verification of tools, spare parts, and protective equipment completeness.

After the pre-shift meeting, each engineer collects the corresponding work orders and inspection record forms according to task assignments, completing pre-departure preparations.

**Step 3: On-Site Inspection Execution**

O&M engineers conduct on-site inspections point by point according to established inspection routes and plans. The following operations are strictly enforced during the inspection process:
- At each inspection point, first perform electronic check-in in the inspection system, recording arrival time;
- Inspect item by item according to the inspection checklist, not omitting any inspection item;
- Use professional tools for measurement and testing, recording actual values;
- Photograph equipment operating status and abnormal conditions;
- Report abnormal conditions immediately upon discovery and record detailed information.

**Step 4: Preventive Maintenance Execution**

According to the maintenance plan, O&M engineers perform preventive maintenance operations on designated equipment:
- Equipment Cleaning: Remove surface and internal dust from equipment, clean cooling fans and ventilation ports;
- Cable Management: Inspect and organize equipment cable connections, ensuring secure connections and clear labels;
- System Optimization: Clean temporary system files, check disk space, and update security patches;
- Hardware Testing: Run hardware diagnostic tools, check hard drive health status, memory errors, etc.;
- Log Analysis: Review system and application logs to identify potential issues and security incidents.

During preventive maintenance, engineers should strictly follow operating procedures and maintain before-and-after comparison records. If equipment shows signs of aging or degradation, timely replacement recommendations should be made.

**Step 5: Abnormal Condition Handling and Reporting**

When abnormal conditions are discovered during inspection and maintenance, they are handled according to the following process:
- **General Abnormality** (does not affect business operations): Record abnormality details, add to subsequent maintenance plan, and arrange handling at an appropriate time;
- **Important Abnormality** (may affect business operations): Report immediately to the O&M project manager, develop temporary safeguard measures, and arrange handling within 24 hours;
- **Severe Abnormality** (has affected business operations): Immediately initiate the emergency response plan, notify relevant personnel, and handle according to emergency procedures.

All abnormal conditions must be registered in the O&M management system, recording discovery time, abnormality description, impact scope, handling measures, and current status.

**Step 6: Work Records and Handover**

After daily work ends (17:30), the O&M team holds a post-shift meeting (15 minutes), covering:
- Each engineer reports on the day's work completion;
- Compilation of the day's discovered abnormal conditions and handling results;
- Handover of incomplete work items and items requiring attention;
- Confirmation of the next day's work plan and key tasks.

After the meeting, each engineer fills in complete work logs and inspection records in the O&M management system and submits them to the O&M project manager for review.

### 5.3.4 Inspection System

**Inspection Frequency:**

| Inspection Type | Inspection Frequency | Inspection Time | Inspection Scope |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Daily Inspection | Twice daily | 9:00, 14:00 | All service hall areas |
| Deep Inspection | Once weekly | Saturday 14:00-17:00 | All data rooms, weak current rooms, equipment rooms |
| Special Inspection | Once monthly | Last week of the month | Key systems and critical equipment |
| Pre-Holiday Inspection | Before major holidays | 3 days before holiday | Full coverage, priority assurance |
| Nightly Inspection | Once daily | 22:00 | Core data room and critical equipment |

**Inspection Routes:**

Inspection routes are designed following the principle of "outside to inside, top to bottom, primary to secondary," ensuring comprehensive coverage with emphasis on key areas:

- **First Floor Route**: Main Service Hall → Self-Service Area → Waiting Area → First Floor Data Room → Power Distribution Room;
- **Second Floor Route**: Comprehensive Acceptance Area → Special Approval Area → Second Floor Weak Current Room → Conference Room Equipment Room;
- **Third Floor Route**: Back Office Area → Data Center Data Room → UPS Room → Air Conditioning Room;
- **Fourth Floor Route**: Leadership Office Area → Conference Room → Fourth Floor Weak Current Room → Rooftop Equipment Area.

**Inspection Content:**

| Inspection Category | Inspection Items | Inspection Standards |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Servers | Operating status indicators, CPU usage, memory usage, disk usage, temperature | Indicators normal, resource usage <80%, temperature <35°C |
| Network Equipment | Port status, traffic, packet loss rate, error packet count | Ports UP, packet loss rate <0.1%, no error packets |
| Security Equipment | Operating status, rule base version, alarm logs | Operating normally, rule base up to date, no high-risk alarms |
| Terminal Equipment | Power-on status, network connection, peripheral status, system updates | Operating normally, network connected, patches up to date |
| Data Center Environment | Temperature, humidity, UPS status, air conditioning operation, fire suppression equipment | Temperature 22-26°C, humidity 40-60%, equipment normal |
| Structured Cabling | Cable labels, cable routing standards, patch panel labels, panel status | Labels clear, routing neat, no loose connections |

### 5.3.5 Inspection Records and Reports

**Inspection Records:**

Each inspection requires completing the "On-Site Inspection Record Form," recording:
- Inspection date, time, and inspector;
- Inspection points and equipment names;
- Actual data and status for each check item;
- Discovered abnormal conditions and handling measures;
- Inspector's signature and confirmation.

Inspection records are entered into the O&M management system in real-time, supporting electronic signatures and timestamps to ensure record authenticity and completeness.

**Inspection Reports:**

| Report Type | Preparation Frequency | Main Content | Submission Recipients |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Daily Briefing | Daily | Daily inspection overview, abnormal conditions, handling progress | Procuring Entity O&M responsible person |
| Weekly Report | Weekly | Weekly inspection summary, fault statistics, key issue analysis, next week's plan | Procuring Entity supervising leader |
| Monthly Report | Monthly | Monthly O&M summary, system operation evaluation, improvement suggestions, next month's plan | Procuring Entity senior leadership |
| Special Report | As needed | Special issue analysis, handling plans, improvement suggestions | Procuring Entity relevant responsible person |

All inspection reports have basic data automatically generated in the O&M management system, reviewed by the O&M project manager before submission. Report content is objective, data is accurate, analysis is in-depth, and suggestions are feasible.

## 5.4 Emergency Incident Handling Process

### 5.4.1 Process Overview

Emergency incident handling is an important component of the O&M service system, aiming to establish a rapid and efficient emergency response mechanism to minimize the impact of emergencies on the Hunan Provincial Government Service Hall's operations. Emergency incidents include but are not limited to: system downtime, network interruption, data security incidents, natural disasters, power outages, fire incidents, etc.

This process follows the principles of "rapid response, classified handling, coordinated response, and recovery priority," establishing a comprehensive emergency response plan system to ensure that emergency response can be quickly initiated, emergency handling can be carried out in an orderly manner, and normal operations can be restored as soon as possible when emergencies occur.

### 5.4.2 Detailed Process Description

**Step 1: Incident Discovery and Preliminary Assessment (Response Time ≤5 minutes)**

Emergency incidents can be discovered through the following channels:
- Automatic alerts from the monitoring system;
- Service hotline reports;
- Inspection personnel discovery;
- Procuring Entity staff reports;
- External notifications.

Upon incident discovery, on-duty personnel immediately conduct a preliminary assessment to determine the following information:
- Time and location of incident occurrence;
- Incident type and nature;
- Impact scope and severity;
- Whether there is a trend of escalation.

Based on preliminary assessment results, the incident level (Level 1/Level 2/Level 3) is determined according to emergency classification standards, and the corresponding level of emergency response is immediately initiated.

**Step 2: Emergency Response Activation (Response Time ≤10 minutes)**

Based on the incident level, initiate the corresponding level of emergency response:
- **Level 1 Response**: The O&M project manager serves as on-site commander, activates all emergency resources, notifies all O&M personnel to enter emergency status, and simultaneously reports to the Procuring Entity's senior leadership and company senior management;
- **Level 2 Response**: The O&M project deputy manager serves as on-site commander, mobilizes relevant emergency resources, notifies relevant personnel to stand by, and reports to the Procuring Entity's supervising leader;
- **Level 3 Response**: The on-duty supervisor serves as on-site commander, organizes on-duty personnel for handling, and reports to the Procuring Entity's O&M responsible person.

After emergency response is activated, immediately notify relevant personnel through emergency communication groups (WeChat groups, mass SMS) to ensure timely and accurate information delivery.

**Step 3: Emergency Handling Implementation (Handling Time per Plan Specifications)**

Based on the incident type, handling is carried out according to the corresponding special emergency response plan:

- **System Downtime**: Switch to backup system, investigate fault cause, restore main system operation after repair;
- **Network Interruption**: Activate backup network link, check network equipment, contact the operator to investigate external line faults;
- **Data Security Incident**: Immediately isolate affected systems, preserve evidence, initiate data recovery process, notify the information security department;
- **Power Outage**: Confirm UPS power supply status, contact property management and power supply department, activate backup generator;
- **Natural Disaster/Fire**: Ensure personnel safety, initiate evacuation procedures, protect critical equipment and data.

During emergency handling, the on-site commander coordinates the actions of all emergency teams to ensure orderly and efficient handling. Progress is reported to superiors every 30 minutes.

**Step 4: Business Recovery and Verification (Recovery Time per SLA Specifications)**

After fault resolution, business recovery follows these steps:
- Gradually restore operation of affected systems;
- Test business functions item by item to confirm normal restoration;
- Notify relevant business departments that systems have been restored;
- Confirm business data integrity and consistency;
- Resume normal operating status.

During business recovery, priority is given to restoring core business systems to ensure basic Government Service Hall operations can proceed normally. For systems that cannot be temporarily restored, manual backup plans are activated to ensure business continuity.

**Step 5: Emergency Status Termination and Summary (Termination Time ≤2 hours after recovery)**

After business is fully restored, the on-site commander confirms the following conditions are met before declaring the emergency status terminated:
- All affected systems are operating normally;
- Business functions have returned to normal;
- No risk of secondary disasters;
- The Procuring Entity confirms that normal order can be restored.

After emergency status is terminated, all emergency personnel return to normal working status, and the on-site commander organizes a preliminary summary of the emergency handling process.

**Step 6: Post-Incident Summary and Improvement (Summary Time ≤72 hours after incident)**

Within 72 hours after incident handling is complete, the O&M project manager organizes the preparation of the "Emergency Handling Summary Report," including:
- Incident overview (time, location, sequence of events, impact);
- Cause analysis (direct cause and root cause);
- Handling process review (response speed, handling measures, resource deployment);
- Lessons learned (aspects done well and areas for improvement);
- Improvement measures recommendations (technical improvements, process optimization, training needs);
- Emergency plan revision recommendations.

After the summary report is reviewed by the Procuring Entity, relevant personnel are organized for a retrospective discussion, and improvement measures are incorporated into specific action plans to continuously improve the emergency response plan system.

### 5.4.4 Emergency Classification Standards

| Level | Name | Criteria | Impact Scope | Response Time Limit |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Level 1 | Extraordinarily Major | Core business system complete failure for over 1 hour; data security incident involving sensitive data leakage; natural disaster rendering data center unusable | All government service operations interrupted | Response within 5 min, arrive within 15 min |
| Level 2 | Major | Important business system failure for over 2 hours; widespread network interruption; power system failure causing partial area power outage | Over 50% of government service operations affected | Response within 10 min, arrive within 30 min |
| Level 3 | Significant | Non-core system failure; partial network interruption; single critical equipment failure | Partial government service operations affected | Response within 15 min, arrive within 60 min |

### 5.4.5 Emergency Escalation Mechanism

Establish a three-level emergency escalation mechanism:

- **Automatic Escalation**: If initial handling is not completed within 30 minutes of incident occurrence, automatically escalate one level; if handling time exceeds 2 times the estimated recovery time, automatically escalate one level.
- **Manual Escalation**: When the on-site commander determines escalation is needed based on situation development, manual escalation can be requested.
- **Downgrade and Termination**: When an incident is effectively controlled and the impact scope is reduced, the response level can be downgraded or the emergency status terminated after assessment.

### 5.4.6 Post-Incident Summary and Improvement

After each emergency incident handling is complete, strictly implement the "Four Do Not Let Go" principle:
- Do not let go until the accident cause is thoroughly investigated;
- Do not let go until responsible persons have been dealt with;
- Do not let go until rectification measures have been implemented;
- Do not let go until relevant personnel have been educated.

Establish an emergency management continuous improvement mechanism:
- Organize emergency plan review and revision once per quarter;
- Organize emergency drills once every six months;
- Organize emergency capability assessment once per year;
- Timely update emergency plans and handling procedures based on issues discovered during drills and actual handling.

### 5.5.5 SLA Exceptions

The following situations are not counted in SLA assessment:
- Service delays caused by the Procuring Entity (such as authorization delays, site unavailability, etc.);
- Service interruptions caused by force majeure (natural disasters, war, etc.);
- Faults caused by third-party suppliers (such as operator line failures) where the O&M team actively coordinates;
- Recovery times for which the Procuring Entity has provided written consent for extension;
- Issues occurring during planned maintenance windows.

When the above situations occur, the O&M team should promptly notify the Procuring Entity, provide written explanations, and immediately resume normal SLA standards after the abnormal factors are eliminated.
