### 7.1.2 Organizational Level Description

#### (I) Company Level

The Company Level is the highest decision-making and management level for project O&M services, composed of the Company Executive Leader and Technical Director.

**Company Executive Leader**, as the project's highest decision-maker, is fully responsible for the decision-making and advancement of major project matters. Specifically including: reviewing the project annual work plan and budget proposal, determining project service strategy and direction; coordinating resources from various internal departments to ensure adequate human, material, and financial resources for the project; maintaining high-level client relationships with the purchaser, regularly communicating with the purchaser's leadership to understand service needs and improvement suggestions; approving major change proposals, emergency plans, and special service requests; bearing leadership responsibility for overall project service quality, participating in the handling and decision-making of major quality incidents. The Company Executive Leader shall receive at least one special briefing from the Project Director each quarter and attend the project annual summary review meeting each year.

**Technical Director**, as the project's highest technical authority, provides comprehensive technical support and assurance for the project. Specifically including: responsible for the review and approval of project technical solutions to ensure their advancement, feasibility, and security; guiding the project technical team to resolve difficult technical problems and providing technical decisions for major fault handling; participating in the review and optimization of project technical architecture, promoting technical innovation and best practice implementation; reviewing major technical change proposals and assessing change risks and impacts; regularly organizing technical review meetings to promote continuous improvement of project technical capabilities. The Technical Director shall attend at least one project monthly meeting each month and respond to major technical issues at any time.

#### (II) Project Level

The Project Level is the management and execution level for project O&M services, composed of the Project Director and Project Manager.

**Project Director**, as the project's overall responsible person, bears overall responsibility for the successful delivery of the project. Specifically including: responsible for formulating the project overall plan, annual plan, and phased objectives to ensure the project advances according to plan; establishing and improving the project quality management system, and supervising the implementation of service quality standards; serving as the primary interface for communication with the purchaser, maintaining good client relationships, and ensuring customer satisfaction; approving major change proposals, emergency plans, and special service requests; managing the project budget and cost control to ensure project economic efficiency; managing the O&M team, promoting team building and personnel capability improvement; regularly reporting project progress, risks, and improvement suggestions to the Company Executive Leader. The Project Director shall organize a weekly project meeting each week and a monthly summary meeting each month.

**Project Manager**, as the project's daily management executor, is responsible for the specific implementation and delivery of the project. Specifically including: formulating monthly and quarterly work plans, rationally assigning work tasks, and ensuring that all O&M services are completed on time; managing the project team's daily attendance, performance assessment, and training development; handling the purchaser's daily needs, complaints, and suggestions to ensure service quality meets contract requirements; organizing the preparation of various project reports (daily, weekly, monthly) and timely reporting project status to the Project Director and purchaser; managing project documents and configuration information to ensure the completeness and accuracy of project materials; coordinating internal and external project resources to promote cross-department collaboration and problem resolution. The Project Manager shall organize a daily meeting each day, prepare a weekly report each week, and prepare a monthly report each month.

#### (III) On-site Level

The On-site Level is the on-site execution level for project O&M services, composed of the On-site Technical Lead and On-site O&M Engineers.

**On-site Technical Lead**, as the core manager of on-site technical work, is responsible for the overall coordination of on-site technical matters. Specifically including: responsible for the overall arrangement and technical guidance of on-site technical work to ensure that all technical tasks are completed on time with quality; handling major faults and difficult technical problems, organizing technical breakthroughs and solution reviews; reviewing on-site technical documents, implementation plans, and change plans to ensure the standardization of technical documents; organizing on-site technical training and knowledge sharing to improve the technical level of the on-site team; coordinating with the remote technical support team to ensure efficient remote support response; preparing on-site technical work plans and summaries, and regularly reporting to the Project Manager. The On-site Technical Lead shall organize a daily morning meeting, a weekly technical meeting, and monthly technical training.

**On-site O&M Engineers**, as the direct executors of on-site O&M services, are responsible for the on-site implementation of all O&M tasks. Specifically including: executing daily inspection work according to O&M procedures and SOPs, timely discovering and reporting system anomalies; performing initial assessment and handling of on-site faults, with complex issues escalated promptly; executing system configuration changes, software deployment, patch updates, and other operations; filling in O&M records and work logs to ensure the completeness and accuracy of O&M data; maintaining on-site O&M tools, equipment, and spare parts to ensure orderly material management; participating in fault analysis meetings, summarizing lessons learned, and improving O&M work. On-site O&M Engineers implement a 7×24-hour shift system to ensure all-weather service coverage.

#### (IV) Remote Level

The Remote Level is the backend support level for project O&M services, composed of 3 remote technical support engineers.

**Senior O&M Engineer**, as the core force of remote technical support, is responsible for the resolution and handling of high-end technical problems. Specifically including: responsible for remote diagnosis and analysis of difficult technical problems, providing solutions and recommendations; conducting system performance monitoring and optimization to improve system operational efficiency; participating in system architecture optimization and the design and implementation of technical upgrade solutions; writing technical documents, best practices, and operation manuals to provide technical guidance for the on-site team; guiding the technical work of on-site engineers to improve the overall technical level of the team. The Senior O&M Engineer's working hours are 9:00-18:00 on working days, with 7×24-hour remote support provided in emergencies.

**Security O&M Engineer**, as the remote security support specialist, is responsible for remote monitoring and handling of security matters. Specifically responsible for: security monitoring and log analysis, timely discovering security threats and anomalous behavior; conducting vulnerability scanning and penetration testing to assess system security status; responsible for remote response and handling of security incidents, providing security solutions; formulating security policies and security plans, guiding the work of on-site security engineers; conducting security assessments and compliance checks to ensure systems meet security requirements.

**System O&M Engineer**, as the remote system support specialist, is responsible for remote support of system maintenance and data services. Specifically responsible for: remote implementation and support of system maintenance and software upgrades; system performance monitoring and optimization to ensure stable system operation; executing system backup and recovery operations to ensure data security; writing system O&M documents and manuals, providing system maintenance technical support; providing remote technical guidance and support for the on-site team's system O&M work.

### 7.1.3 Organizational Structure Deepening

#### (I) Company Technical Support Center Function Description

The Company Technical Support Center, as the backend support organization for this project, has the following functional departments:

**Table 7-1-1 Company Technical Support Center Department Functions**

| Department Name | Department Responsibilities | Position Settings | Personnel Allocation | Collaboration Relationship |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Technical R&D Department | Responsible for O&M technology R&D, tool development, automation script writing | 1 Technical Manager, 2 Senior Development Engineers, 3 Development Engineers | 6 persons | Provides technical support and tool assurance for the project level |
| Quality Management Department | Responsible for O&M service quality control, process audit, continuous improvement | 1 Quality Manager, 2 Quality Engineers | 3 persons | Conducts quality supervision and assessment for the project level |
| Security Management Department | Responsible for information security policy formulation, security incident response, compliance audit | 1 Security Manager, 2 Security Engineers, 1 Security Analyst | 4 persons | Provides security support and emergency response for the project level |
| Resource Assurance Department | Responsible for equipment procurement, spare parts management, supplier management | 1 Resource Manager, 1 Procurement Specialist, 1 Warehouse Administrator | 3 persons | Provides material assurance and resource allocation for the project level |
| Human Resources Department | Responsible for personnel recruitment, training, performance assessment, compensation management | 1 HR Manager, 1 Recruitment Specialist, 1 Training Specialist | 3 persons | Provides human resource support for the project level |

**Technical R&D Department** is the company's core technical innovation department, dedicated to providing technical support and tool assurance for O&M services. The Technical Manager is responsible for overall department management and technical planning, formulating technical R&D direction and plans; Senior Development Engineers are responsible for the design and development of core O&M tools and automation scripts, solving technical challenges; Development Engineers are responsible for coding, testing, and maintenance of O&M tools. This department works closely with the project-level O&M service and technical support departments, developing customized O&M tools based on project needs to improve O&M efficiency and automation levels. The Technical R&D Department holds a weekly technical coordination meeting with the project level to understand project technical needs and pain points.

**Quality Management Department** is the company's core department for service quality control, responsible for establishing and maintaining the O&M service quality management system. The Quality Manager is responsible for the planning and construction of the quality management system, formulating quality objectives and standards; Quality Engineers are responsible for quality inspections, process audits, and data analysis, promoting service improvements. This department conducts regular inspections and evaluations of project-level service quality, organizes one internal audit per quarter, and one management review per year. The Quality Management Department collaborates with the Project Management Office to jointly promote customer satisfaction improvement and service improvement.

**Security Management Department** is the company's core department for information security assurance, responsible for the construction and maintenance of the information security management system. The Security Manager is responsible for the formulation of information security policies and the construction of the security system; Security Engineers are responsible for security monitoring, vulnerability management, and security incident response; Security Analysts are responsible for security log analysis, threat intelligence collection, and security incident investigation. This department provides technical security support for the project level, participates in the handling of major security incidents, and regularly organizes security assessments and penetration tests. The Security Management Department reports security status to the Company Executive Leader monthly and organizes a quarterly security review meeting.

**Resource Assurance Department** is the company's core department for material assurance, responsible for equipment procurement, spare parts management, and supplier management. The Resource Department formulates procurement plans based on project needs, selects appropriate suppliers, and ensures that equipment and spare parts arrive on time; establishes a comprehensive spare parts inventory management system to ensure reasonable spare parts inventory levels; maintains supplier relationships and regularly evaluates supplier performance. The Resource Assurance Department works closely with the project-level resource assurance team to ensure timely supply of materials needed for the project.

**Human Resources Department** is the company's core department for human resource management, responsible for personnel recruitment, training, performance assessment, and compensation management. The HR Manager is responsible for the formulation and implementation of human resource plans; the Recruitment Specialist is responsible for personnel recruitment and interview organization; the Training Specialist is responsible for training needs analysis and training plan implementation. This department provides human resource support for the project level to ensure timely deployment and continuous development of personnel needed for the project.

#### (II) Project Level Department Detailed Functions

**Table 7-1-2 Project Level Department Function Description**

| Department/Role | Core Responsibilities | Specific Work Content | Position Settings | Personnel Allocation |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Project Management Office | Overall project management and coordination | Project plan formulation, progress tracking, risk management, stakeholder management, change control | 1 Project Director, 1 Project Manager, 1 Project Assistant | 3 persons |
| O&M Service Department | Daily O&M service execution | System inspection, fault handling, performance monitoring, configuration management, change execution | 1 O&M Supervisor, 4 O&M Engineers, 2 On-call Engineers | 7 persons |
| Technical Support Department | Technical support and problem resolution | Difficult problem resolution, technical consultation, solution design, technical training | 1 Technical Supervisor, 2 Senior Engineers, 2 Technical Engineers | 5 persons |
| Security Management Department | Information security assurance | Security monitoring, vulnerability management, emergency response, security audit, compliance inspection | 1 Security Supervisor, 1 Security Engineer, 1 Security Analyst | 3 persons |
| Quality Management Department | Service quality control | Quality inspection, process audit, service improvement, customer satisfaction management | 1 Quality Supervisor, 1 Quality Engineer | 2 persons |

**Project Management Office** is the project's management hub, responsible for overall project planning, coordination, and control. The Project Director is responsible for the decision-making and advancement of major project matters, the Project Manager is responsible for daily management and execution, and the Project Assistant is responsible for document management and administrative affairs. This office formulates project management systems and processes, establishes project communication and coordination mechanisms to ensure smooth information flow and efficient collaboration among all project participants. The Project Management Office organizes a weekly project meeting each week, a monthly summary meeting each month, and a quarterly review meeting each quarter.

**O&M Service Department** is the project's main execution department for O&M services, responsible for daily system O&M and fault handling. The O&M Supervisor is responsible for the management of the O&M team and the formulation of O&M plans; O&M Engineers are responsible for on-site O&M work including daily inspections, fault handling, and system maintenance; On-call Engineers are responsible for non-working hours on-call and emergency response. The O&M Service Department establishes O&M service processes according to ITSS standards to ensure the standardization and normalization of O&M services. The O&M Service Department organizes a daily morning meeting, a weekly O&M meeting, and a monthly O&M summary meeting.

**Technical Support Department** is the project's core department for technical support, responsible for the resolution of difficult problems and technical consultation. The Technical Supervisor is responsible for the management of the technical team and the review of technical solutions; Senior Engineers are responsible for the analysis of difficult problems and the design of solutions; Technical Engineers are responsible for the implementation of technical solutions and the preparation of technical documents. The Technical Support Department establishes a technical knowledge base to accumulate technical experience and best practices, providing technical support for O&M services. The Technical Support Department organizes a weekly technical meeting and a monthly technical sharing session.

**Security Management Department** is the project's core department for security assurance, responsible for the construction and maintenance of the information security management system. The Security Supervisor is responsible for the formulation of security policies and the management of the security system; Security Engineers are responsible for security monitoring, vulnerability management, and emergency response; Security Analysts are responsible for security log analysis and incident investigation. The Security Management Department establishes comprehensive security management systems and processes to ensure system security and compliance. The Security Management Department organizes a weekly security meeting, monthly security inspections, and quarterly security assessments.

**Quality Management Department** is the project's core department for quality control, responsible for the inspection and improvement of service quality. The Quality Supervisor is responsible for the construction and maintenance of the quality management system; Quality Engineers are responsible for quality inspections, process audits, and data analysis. The Quality Management Department establishes quality inspection and evaluation mechanisms, regularly conducts customer satisfaction surveys, and promotes continuous improvement of service quality. The Quality Management Department organizes weekly quality inspections, monthly quality analysis meetings, and quarterly internal audits.

#### (III) Collaboration Relationship Diagram Text Description

Internal project collaboration adopts a matrix management approach, with specific collaboration processes as follows:

1. **Vertical Collaboration**: Company Level → Project Level → On-site Level → Remote Level form a vertical management chain, with directives transmitted top-down and information fed back bottom-up. The Company Level is responsible for strategic decisions and resource assurance, the Project Level for management and execution, and the On-site and Remote Levels for specific operations and technical support. Vertical collaboration is achieved through regular meetings, reporting systems, and special meetings for information transmission and decision dissemination.

2. **Horizontal Collaboration**: The Project Management Office, O&M Service Department, Technical Support Department, Security Management Department, and Quality Management Department form horizontal collaboration relationships, synchronizing information through weekly and monthly coordination meetings. The O&M Service Department and Technical Support Department collaborate closely when handling faults, the Security Management Department provides security support for all departments, and the Quality Management Department supervises and evaluates service quality across all departments.

3. **External Collaboration**: Establish regular communication mechanisms with the purchaser's informatization department, equipment suppliers, and software vendors to ensure efficient utilization of external resources. Conduct weekly work coordination with the purchaser's informatization department, establish a 7×24-hour technical support hotline with equipment suppliers, and establish regular technical exchange mechanisms with software vendors.

4. **Emergency Collaboration**: In the case of major faults, activate the emergency collaboration mechanism with joint response from the Company Technical Support Center, Project Management Office, O&M Service Department, Technical Support Department, and Security Management Department. Emergency collaboration follows the processes specified in the emergency plan, with clear responsibilities and collaboration methods for all parties to ensure rapid and effective handling of emergencies.

#### (II) Reporting System

| Report Type | Frequency | Author | Reviewer | Recipients | Main Content |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|

| Weekly Report | Weekly | Project Manager | Project Director | Project Director, Purchaser | Weekly work summary, issue analysis, risk warning |
| Monthly Report | Monthly | Project Manager | Project Director | Project Director, Purchaser | Monthly service report, KPI completion, improvement suggestions |

| Annual Report | Annual | Project Director | Company Executive Leader | Purchaser, Company leadership | Annual service summary, cost analysis, next year plan |
| Special Report | As needed | Technical Lead | Project Manager | Project Director, Purchaser | Major fault analysis, security inspection report, etc. |

| Customer Satisfaction Report | Quarterly | Quality Supervisor | Project Manager | Project Director, Purchaser | Satisfaction survey results, improvement suggestions |

#### (III) Emergency Communication

1. **Telephone Communication**: In emergencies, communicate immediately by phone to ensure timely information delivery. Establish an emergency contact directory containing all project personnel's mobile phone numbers and emergency contact information.
2. **WeChat Group Communication**: Use the O&M service WeChat group to publish emergency information and processing progress in real time. Information classification management is implemented in the group, with general information and management information published separately.
3. **Video Conference**: In cases of major faults or emergencies, conduct remote collaborative handling via video conference. Video conference equipment is provided to ensure availability at all times.
4. **On-site Meeting**: For particularly major events, relevant personnel shall immediately arrive at the site for an on-site meeting.

### 7.2.4 Onboarding Process

#### Onboarding Process Overview

To ensure that new personnel can quickly integrate into the team and be competent for their work, a standardized onboarding process is established as follows:

**Pre-onboarding Preparation (3 days before onboarding)**:
1. HR Department confirms the onboarding date and required materials for new personnel
2. Prepare office equipment (computer, monitor, keyboard, mouse, etc.), office supplies, and access cards
3. Create system accounts (email, O&M management system, knowledge base, etc.)
4. Prepare onboarding training materials and job descriptions
5. Notify relevant departments to prepare for reception
6. Assign an onboarding mentor (B-post backup personnel preferred)

**Onboarding Day**:
1. HR Department receives new personnel and processes onboarding procedures
2. Sign employment contracts and confidentiality agreements
3. Issue office supplies and access cards
4. Introduce company overview, organizational structure, and rules and regulations
5. Guide tour of office environment and introduce team members
6. Onboarding mentor conducts one-on-one guidance

**First Week of Onboarding**:
1. Attend company-level onboarding training (corporate culture, rules and regulations, security training)
2. Attend department-level onboarding training (department responsibilities, work processes, collaboration relationships)
3. Attend position-level onboarding training (job responsibilities, operating procedures, tool usage)
4. Onboarding mentor conducts one-on-one guidance, formulates learning plan
5. Familiarize with project environment and system architecture
6. Communicate and coordinate with key position personnel

**First Month of Onboarding**:
1. Complete all onboarding training courses
2. Begin working independently under the guidance of the onboarding mentor
3. Attend monthly project meeting to understand overall project situation
4. Complete monthly work summary and self-evaluation
5. Onboarding mentor conducts monthly evaluation and provides improvement suggestions

**Onboarding Probation Period (1-3 months)**:
1. Complete work tasks according to job responsibility requirements
2. Attend probation assessment (monthly assessment + expiration assessment)
3. Complete probation period work summary
4. HR Department organizes probation evaluation interview
5. Formal confirmation or probation extension

#### Onboarding Training Content

| Training Phase | Training Content | Duration | Training Method | Assessment Method |
|:---|:---|:---:|:---|:---|
| Company-level Training | Company overview, corporate culture, rules and regulations, information security | 2 days | Classroom training | Exam |
| Department-level Training | Department responsibilities, work processes, collaboration relationships, tool usage | 2 days | Classroom training + Practical | Exam + Practical |
| Position-level Training | Job responsibilities, operating procedures, SOPs, emergency plans | 3 days | Mentor-led | Exam + Practical |
| Project-level Training | Project background, system architecture, O&M processes, quality standards | 2 days | Classroom training + On-site | Exam + On-site assessment |

### 7.2.6 Personnel Social Insurance Certificate Requirements

In accordance with the bidding document requirements, we commit to providing the following social insurance certificates:

1. **Certificate Period**: Provide social insurance certificates for three consecutive months (January, February, March) starting from January 2024.
2. **Certificate Content**: Including pension insurance, medical insurance, unemployment insurance, work injury insurance, and maternity insurance — five types of insurance payment certificates.
3. **Issuing Authority**: Issued by the social insurance agency with the official seal of the social insurance agency.
4. **Payment Entity**: The social insurance payment entity must be consistent with the bidding entity name.
5. **Personnel Scope**: All project personnel including Project Director, Project Manager, On-site Technical Lead, On-site O&M Engineers, and Remote Technical Support Engineers.

We commit that the above social insurance certificates are authentic and valid, and are willing to bear corresponding legal responsibilities in case of any falsification.

### 7.2.7 Personnel Stability Assurance Measures

#### (I) Personnel Stability Commitment

1. **Core Project Personnel (Project Director, Project Manager, On-site Technical Lead)**: Maintain stability throughout the project service period; no personnel replacement without the purchaser's written consent.
2. **On-site O&M Engineers**: Maintain stability throughout the project service period; personnel replacement requires 30 days' advance notice to the purchaser, with replacement personnel of equivalent qualifications provided.
3. **Remote Technical Support Engineers**: Maintain stability throughout the project service period; personnel replacement requires 15 days' advance notice to the purchaser.

#### (II) Personnel Replacement Conditions

Under the following circumstances, with the purchaser's consent, personnel replacement may be carried out:
1. Personnel voluntarily resign for personal reasons
2. Personnel unable to continue working due to health reasons
3. Personnel held liable for illegal or regulatory violations
4. Personnel assessed as unqualified by the purchaser, with replacement requested
5. Force majeure preventing personnel from continuing to work

#### (III) Personnel Replacement Process

1. Provide advance notice to the purchaser (core personnel 30 days in advance, other personnel 15 days in advance)
2. Provide detailed resumes and qualification certificates of replacement personnel
3. Replacement personnel must be confirmed through the purchaser's interview
4. Complete work handover to ensure service continuity
5. Personnel replacement must not affect service quality

#### (IV) Personnel Incentive Mechanism

1. **Compensation Incentive**: Provide competitive compensation packages to ensure personnel stability. Establish a compensation grade system with salary levels determined by position, skills, and performance.
2. **Performance Incentive**: Monthly/quarterly performance assessment results are linked to performance-based compensation, with rewards for excellent performance. Performance bonuses account for 20%-30% of total compensation.
3. **Career Development**: Provide career development paths and promotion opportunities for project personnel. Establish dual-track development paths for management and technical tracks.
4. **Training Opportunities**: Provide professional skill training and certification exam opportunities. Provide no fewer than 80 hours of training opportunities annually.
5. **Team Building**: Regularly organize team activities to enhance team cohesion. Organize one team building activity per quarter.
6. **Benefits**: Provide comprehensive benefits including annual physical examinations, holiday benefits, paid annual leave, etc.

## 7.3 Personnel Qualifications

### 7.3.1 System Architect Designer (Senior) Certificate Description

The System Architect Designer (Senior) is a senior-level qualification certificate in the National Computer Technology and Software Professional Qualification (Level) Examination, jointly issued by the Ministry of Human Resources and Social Security and the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology.

**Certificate Features**:
- Proves that the holder possesses advanced capabilities in system architecture design
- Capable of independently leading the architecture design and technical selection of large-scale information systems
- Possesses system planning, design, evaluation, and optimization capabilities
- Certificate is valid long-term

**Application in This Project**:
- The Project Director holds this certificate, ensuring the advancement and feasibility of the project's overall technical solution
- The Remote Senior O&M Engineer holds this certificate, providing technical support for system architecture optimization and difficult problem resolution

**Certificate Holders**:
- Project Director: [Placeholder], 15 years of IT experience, has led the architecture design of multiple provincial government informatization projects
- Remote Senior O&M Engineer: [Placeholder], 12 years of IT experience, rich experience in system architecture design

### 7.3.2 System Planning & Management Engineer (Senior) Certificate Description

The System Planning & Management Engineer (Senior) is a senior-level qualification certificate in the National Computer Technology and Software Professional Qualification (Level) Examination, focusing on IT service planning and management capabilities.

**Certificate Features**:
- Proves that the holder possesses advanced capabilities in IT service planning and management
- Capable of formulating IT service strategies, planning and managing IT service projects
- Possesses IT service continuous improvement and quality management capabilities
- Certificate is valid long-term

**Application in This Project**:
- The On-site Technical Lead holds this certificate, ensuring standardized and normalized management of O&M services
- Capable of formulating scientific O&M service plans and continuously improving service quality

**Certificate Holders**:
- On-site Technical Lead: [Placeholder], 8 years of IT experience, rich experience in IT service management

### 7.3.3 ITSS Service Engineer Certificate Description

The ITSS (Information Technology Service Standards) Service Engineer certificate is an IT service capability certification issued by the China Electronics Standardization Institute.

**Certificate Features**:
- Issued based on the national standard "Information Technology Service — Operation and Maintenance — Part 1: General Requirements" (GB/T 28827.1)
- Proves that the holder possesses basic IT O&M service capabilities
- Covers various elements of the O&M service capability model
- Certificate is valid for 3 years, requiring periodic renewal

**Application in This Project**:
- On-site O&M Engineers hold this certificate, ensuring O&M services comply with national standards
- Capable of integrating ITSS standards into daily O&M work to improve service standardization

**Certificate Holders**:
- On-site O&M Engineer A: [Placeholder], 5 years of IT experience
- On-site O&M Engineer B: [Placeholder], 5 years of IT experience

### 7.3.4 Other Relevant Qualification Certificate Descriptions

#### (I) Information Security Engineer

The Information Security Engineer is an intermediate/senior-level qualification certificate in the National Computer Technology and Software Professional Qualification (Level) Examination.

- **Intermediate Information Security Engineer**: Possesses basic knowledge and skills in information security, capable of configuring security equipment and performing initial handling of security incidents.
- **Senior Information Security Engineer**: Possesses advanced information security capabilities, capable of formulating security policies, conducting security assessments, and handling major security incidents.

In this project, On-site O&M Engineer B holds the Intermediate Information Security Engineer certificate, and the Remote Security O&M Engineer holds the Senior Information Security Engineer certificate, providing strong support for the project's security assurance.

#### (II) CISP (Certified Information Security Professional)

CISP is an information security professional certification issued by the China Information Technology Security Evaluation Center, one of the most authoritative certifications in the domestic information security field.

- Covers information security assurance, network security, system security, application security, and other aspects
- Certificate is valid for 3 years
- In this project, the Remote Security O&M Engineer holds the CISP certificate

#### (III) CISSP (Certified Information Systems Security Professional)

CISSP is an international information security certification issued by (ISC)², recognized globally as a top-level certification in the information security field.

- Covers 8 knowledge domains including security and risk management, asset security, security engineering, network security, etc.
- Certificate is valid for 3 years
- In this project, the Remote Security O&M Engineer holds the CISSP certificate, possessing internationally recognized information security professional capabilities

#### (IV) Oracle OCP (Oracle Certified Professional)

Oracle OCP is a database professional certification issued by Oracle Corporation, proving that the holder possesses professional Oracle database management capabilities.

- Covers core skills including database installation, configuration, backup and recovery, performance optimization, etc.
- In this project, the Remote Senior O&M Engineer holds the Oracle OCP certificate

#### (V) RHCE (Red Hat Certified Engineer)

RHCE is a Linux system administration professional certification issued by Red Hat Corporation, proving that the holder possesses professional Red Hat Enterprise Linux system management capabilities.

- Covers core skills including system administration, network configuration, security hardening, service management, etc.
- Certificate is valid for 3 years
- In this project, the Remote System O&M Engineer holds the RHCE certificate

# Chapter 8 Technical Assurance and Emergency Response Plan


## 8.1 Technical Quality Assurance Plan

### 8.1.1 Quality Control Standards

The quality control of operation and maintenance services for this project strictly adheres to the following standards and specifications:

#### (I) ISO 9001 Quality Management System

Our company has obtained ISO 9001 Quality Management System certification and fully integrates the requirements of the ISO 9001 standard into the entire process of operation and maintenance services:

1. **Customer Focus**: Oriented toward the needs of the procurer, continuously improving service quality
2. **Leadership**: The Project Director is responsible for establishing quality objectives and ensuring the implementation of quality policies
3. **Involvement of People**: All operation and maintenance personnel participate in quality management; each person is a quality responsibility owner
4. **Process Approach**: Operation and maintenance service activities are managed as processes, identifying, controlling, and improving each process
5. **Continual Improvement**: Continuously improving operation and maintenance service quality through the PDCA cycle
6. **Evidence-Based Decision Making**: Making decisions based on analysis of data and information
7. **Relationship Management**: Establishing good cooperative relationships with the procurer and suppliers

#### (II) Daily Inspection

1. **Inspection Frequency**: Conducted daily
2. **Inspection Content**:
   - Equipment inspection: Check item by item according to the Daily Inspection Checklist
   - System monitoring: Check the operational status of servers, networks, and application systems
   - Log review: Check system logs and security logs, handle anomalies promptly
   - Performance analysis: Analyze CPU, memory, disk, network, and other performance indicators
   - Security check: Check the operational status of security devices and execution of security policies
3. **Inspection Records**: Fill in the Daily Inspection Record Form, recording inspection time, inspection content, issues found, and handling status
4. **Exception Handling**: Anomalies found during inspection must be handled promptly; those that cannot be handled immediately must be escalated to the Technical Lead

#### (IV) Special Inspections

1. **Security Special Inspection**: Conducted once per quarter, including vulnerability scanning, penetration testing, security policy checks, etc.
2. **Performance Special Inspection**: Conducted once every six months, including system performance assessment, capacity planning, performance optimization recommendations, etc.
3. **Emergency Special Inspection**: Conducted once per year, including emergency plan effectiveness assessment, emergency resource inspection, emergency drill evaluation, etc.
4. **Compliance Check**: Conducted once per year to ensure operation and maintenance services comply with relevant requirements such as Classified Protection 2.0 and government external network security management.

#### (V) Third-Party Inspection

1. **Annual Audit**: Invite a third-party institution to conduct an annual operation and maintenance service quality audit.
2. **Classified Protection Evaluation**: Cooperate with the procurer to complete work related to classified protection evaluation.
3. **Penetration Testing**: Invite a third-party security institution to conduct annual penetration testing.
4. **Compliance Check**: Cooperate with superior authorities in conducting compliance checks.

### 8.1.6 Technical Quality Assurance Enhancement

#### (I) Quality Control Process

This project establishes a quality control process covering the entire lifecycle of O&M services, with the following key control points:

**Key Control Point 1: Pre-Service Delivery Review**

Before each service delivery, the Project Manager organizes a service delivery review meeting to confirm the following:
- Service scope and deliverables are clearly defined
- Resource allocation is in place; personnel skills meet requirements
- Technical plan and implementation plan have passed review
- Risk assessment is completed; emergency plans are prepared
- The procurer has confirmed the delivery plan and acceptance criteria

**Key Control Point 2: Service Process Monitoring**

During service execution, the following process monitoring measures are implemented:
- All O&M operations must be recorded through the work order system to ensure traceability
- Critical operations must undergo dual-person review to prevent human errors
- Real-time monitoring of service indicators with timely warnings for deviations
- Regular progress briefing meetings to ensure information synchronization among all parties
- Change operations must strictly follow the change management process

**Key Control Point 3: Service Delivery Acceptance**

After each service delivery, the following acceptance procedures are executed:
- The service provider submits service reports and deliverables
- The Project Manager conducts preliminary acceptance against service standards
- The procurer conducts final acceptance confirmation
- Acceptance results are recorded in the Service Delivery Acceptance Form
- Non-conforming items enter the corrective action process

**Key Control Point 4: Service Satisfaction Assessment**

Service satisfaction assessment is conducted quarterly:
- Design satisfaction survey questionnaires (covering dimensions such as response speed, service quality, communication ability, and problem-solving ability)
- Relevant departments of the procurer complete the satisfaction survey
- Calculate satisfaction scores and analyze unsatisfactory items
- Develop improvement measures and track implementation
- Incorporate satisfaction assessment results into performance evaluation

**Key Control Point 5: Continuous Improvement Review**

Continuous improvement review is conducted semi-annually:
- Aggregate and analyze quality data and trends over the past six months
- Evaluate the implementation effectiveness of improvement measures
- Identify new improvement opportunities and optimization directions
- Update quality objectives and improvement plans
- Incorporate review results into management review reports

**Key Control Point 6: Risk Management Review**

Risk management review is conducted quarterly:
- Update the risk register and identify new risks
- Assess changes in existing risk trends
- Check the execution status of risk response measures
- Develop specialized control plans for high-risk items
- Communicate risk review results to relevant parties

**Key Control Point 7: Supplier Quality Review**

Supplier quality review is conducted semi-annually:
- Evaluate supplier service quality and delivery capabilities
- Review supplier qualifications and personnel capabilities
- Check supplier contract compliance status
- Issue rectification requirements for non-compliant suppliers
- Update the qualified supplier list

#### (III) Quality Assessment Methods

This project employs multi-dimensional quality assessment methods to ensure objective and comprehensive evaluation results:

**1. Quantitative Assessment Methods**

- **KPI Indicator Assessment**: Monthly statistics on KPI indicator completion, comparison with target values, calculation of compliance rate
- **Trend Analysis**: Monthly trend analysis of key indicators to identify quality change trends
- **Deviation Analysis**: Root cause analysis for non-compliant indicators, development of corrective measures
- **Statistical Process Control (SPC)**: Establishment of control charts for key quality indicators to monitor process stability

**2. Qualitative Assessment Methods**

- **Expert Review**: Quarterly organization of internal experts to review service quality
- **User Interviews**: Semi-annual in-depth interviews with key users of the procurer to understand service experience
- **Peer Benchmarking**: Comparative analysis with industry benchmarks to identify gaps and improvement directions
- **Maturity Assessment**: Annual operation and maintenance service maturity assessment

**3. Comprehensive Assessment Model**

Weighted comprehensive scoring method with a total score of 100 points:

| Assessment Dimension | Weight | Assessment Content | Scoring Standard |
|:---|:---:|:---|:---|
| Service Delivery Quality | 30% | Delivery timeliness, completeness, accuracy | 0-100 points |
| Technical Capability Level | 20% | Technical solution quality, problem-solving ability | 0-100 points |
| Service Response Speed | 15% | Fault response speed, report submission timeliness | 0-100 points |
| Security Management Level | 15% | Security incident control, compliance | 0-100 points |
| Customer Satisfaction | 10% | Satisfaction survey results | 0-100 points |
| Document Standardization Level | 10% | Document quality, completeness, timeliness | 0-100 points |

Assessment rating classification:
- Excellent: ≥90 points
- Good: 80-89 points
- Pass: 70-79 points
- Fail: <70 points

#### (IV) Quality Review Process

This project establishes a three-level quality review mechanism to ensure the effectiveness of quality management and continuous improvement:

**1. Level 1 Review: Daily Quality Review**

- **Frequency**: Once per week
- **Host**: Project Manager
- **Participants**: On-site technical backbone
- **Review Content**:
  - Review of this week's work order handling quality
  - Discussion of typical problems and handling methods
  - Quality requirements for key work next week
  - Notification of quality anomalies
- **Output**: Weekly Quality Review Record

**2. Level 2 Review: Monthly Quality Review**

- **Frequency**: Once per month
- **Host**: Project Director
- **Participants**: Project Manager, Technical Lead, on-site representatives
- **Review Content**:
  - Monthly KPI indicator completion
  - Monthly quality trend analysis
  - Quality improvement measure implementation status
  - Customer feedback and complaint analysis
  - Quality work plan for next month
- **Output**: Monthly Quality Review Report

**3. Level 3 Review: Quarterly Management Review**

- **Frequency**: Once per quarter
- **Host**: Company Quality Director
- **Participants**: Project Director, Project Manager, Technical Lead, customer representatives
- **Review Content**:
  - Quarterly quality management system operation status
  - Quality objective achievement status
  - Internal and external audit results
  - Effectiveness of preventive and corrective measures
  - Quality system improvement recommendations
  - Resource allocation requirements
- **Output**: Quarterly Management Review Report

#### (V) Quality Improvement Cycle

This project establishes a complete quality improvement cycle mechanism to ensure continuous improvement of service quality:

**1. Improvement Opportunity Identification**

Improvement opportunities are identified through the following channels:
- Improvement items determined at quality review meetings
- Customer complaints and suggestions
- Non-conformities found during internal audits
- Root cause analysis of security incidents and faults
- Industry best practice benchmarking analysis
- Application assessment of new technologies and methods

**2. Improvement Measure Development**

For identified improvement opportunities, specific improvement measures are developed:
- Define improvement objectives and expected outcomes
- Develop detailed implementation plans and timelines
- Assign responsible persons and assisting personnel
- Determine resource requirements and budgets
- Set checkpoints and acceptance criteria

**3. Improvement Measure Implementation**

Implement improvement measures according to the plan:
- Execute improvement activities as planned
- Record implementation process and data
- Coordinate and resolve implementation issues in a timely manner
- Report implementation progress regularly

**4. Improvement Effectiveness Verification**

Verify the effectiveness of improvement measures:
- Compare quality indicator changes before and after improvement
- Assess objective achievement status
- Collect customer feedback
- Verify the sustainability of improvement measures

**5. Standardization and Consolidation**

Consolidate effective improvement measures into standards:
- Update relevant process documents and work instructions
- Organize training to ensure all personnel master the updates
- Incorporate into daily quality inspection checklists
- Review regularly to ensure continued effectiveness

### 8.1.7 ITSS Operation and Maintenance Capability Maturity Model Implementation Details

#### (I) Maturity Level Definition

This project establishes a five-level O&M capability maturity model based on the GB/T 28827.1-2017 standard:

**Table 8-2-2 ITSS O&M Capability Maturity Level Definition**

| Maturity Level | Level Name | Characteristic Description | Key Capabilities |
|:---:|:---|:---|:---|
| Level 1 | Initial | O&M services are disorganized, relying on individual heroism, lacking standardized processes | Passive response, ad-hoc handling |
| Level 2 | Repeatable | Basic O&M processes established but inconsistently executed, relying on individual experience | Basic processes, incident management |
| Level 3 | Defined | O&M service processes are standardized and documented, understood and executed by all | Standard processes, proactive O&M |
| Level 4 | Quantitatively Managed | O&M service quality is quantitatively measurable, data-driven decision making | Quantitative indicators, data analysis |
| Level 5 | Optimizing | Continuous improvement mechanism is mature, O&M services deeply integrated with business | Continual improvement, business alignment |

| 24 | Security Management | Compliance achievement rate | Compliance status of various compliance requirements | 4% |
| 25 | Continuous Improvement | Improvement measure completion rate | Development and execution status of improvement measures | 4% |

#### (III) Maturity Assessment Method

**1. Assessment Process**

This project adopts the following maturity assessment process:

| Step | Assessment Activity | Assessment Method | Output |
|:---:|:---|:---|:---|
| 1 | Assessment preparation | Determine assessment scope, assemble assessment team | Assessment plan |
| 2 | Data collection | Collect system documents, operation records, statistical data | Data checklist |
| 3 | On-site interviews | Interview key personnel to understand actual execution | Interview records |
| 4 | Indicator scoring | Score each item, calculate dimension scores | Scoring sheet |
| 5 | Level determination | Comprehensive scoring to determine maturity level | Level determination result |
| 6 | Gap analysis | Compare with target level, identify gaps | Gap analysis report |
| 7 | Improvement recommendations | Propose improvement recommendations and action plans | Improvement recommendation report |
| 8 | Report preparation | Prepare formal assessment report | Assessment report |

**2. Scoring Standards**

Each indicator is scored on a 0-5 scale:

| Score | Meaning | Determination Criteria |
|:---:|:---|:---|
| 0 | Not implemented | Relevant process or system not established |
| 1 | Initial | Preliminary awareness exists, but not institutionalized |
| 2 | Repeatable | Basic system exists, but execution is inconsistent |
| 3 | Defined | Processes are standardized, executed by all |
| 4 | Quantitatively Managed | Quantitative indicators exist, data-driven decisions |
| 5 | Optimizing | Continuous improvement, deep integration with business |

**3. Maturity Level Determination**

Comprehensive score calculation method:
- Comprehensive Score = Σ(Indicator Score × Weight) / Maximum Score × 100

| Comprehensive Score | Maturity Level |
|:---:|:---:|
| 0-20 points | Level 1 (Initial) |
| 21-40 points | Level 2 (Repeatable) |
| 41-60 points | Level 3 (Defined) |
| 61-80 points | Level 4 (Quantitatively Managed) |
| 81-100 points | Level 5 (Optimizing) |

### 8.1.9 Classified Protection of Cybersecurity (Classified Protection 2.0) Implementation Plan

#### (I) Secure Physical Environment

The physical environment of the computer room for this project is constructed and managed in strict accordance with the secure physical environment requirements specified in GB/T 22239-2019:

**1. Computer Room Location Requirements**
- The computer room location avoids areas with strong earthquakes, strong vibrations, strong noise, and strong electromagnetic interference
- The computer room is not in the basement or top floor of the building to avoid flood risks
- The computer room is far from areas where flammable and explosive materials are stored
- The computer room has convenient transportation conditions for emergency personnel access

**2. Computer Room Construction Standards**
- Computer room construction complies with Class B standards (GB 50174-2017 Data Center Design Specification)
- Computer room area meets equipment deployment and maintenance needs
- Computer room clear height is not less than 2.6 meters
- Computer room floor uses anti-static flooring with load-bearing capacity ≥500kg/m²
- Computer room is equipped with a gas fire suppression system (HFC-227ea)
- Computer room is equipped with a precision air conditioning system, temperature controlled at 23±1°C, humidity controlled at 45%-65%
- Computer room is equipped with a UPS uninterruptible power supply system with backup time ≥30 minutes
- Computer room is equipped with a diesel generator set as backup power

**3. Physical Security Protection**
- Computer room entrances and exits are equipped with electronic access control systems supporting card + password two-factor authentication
- Video surveillance cameras are installed inside and outside the computer room, with surveillance recordings retained for ≥90 days
- Computer room is equipped with a water leak detection system
- Computer room is equipped with a temperature and humidity monitoring system
- Computer room is equipped with smoke and heat fire detectors
- Computer room is equipped with a lightning protection grounding system

**4. Power Supply Assurance**
- Dual utility power feeds with automatic switchover
- UPS system uses N+1 redundant configuration
- Diesel generator set can start and supply power within 15 minutes
- Power distribution cabinets are equipped with power monitoring systems
- Critical equipment uses dual power feeds

#### (II) Secure Communication Network

**1. Network Architecture Security**
- Network architecture uses a three-layer architecture: core layer, aggregation layer, and access layer
- Core layer devices use dual hot-standby to ensure high availability
- Network zones are partitioned according to security levels and business functions
- Different security zones are isolated through firewalls
- Network topology diagrams are regularly updated to ensure consistency with actual configuration

**2. Network Security Device Deployment**
- Next-generation firewall (NGFW) deployed at the Internet egress, supporting application-layer filtering
- Intrusion Prevention System (IPS) deployed in the core switching area
- Intrusion Detection System (IDS) deployed on the internal network
- Web Application Firewall (WAF) deployed to protect web applications
- DDoS protection devices deployed to resist distributed denial-of-service attacks
- Network audit system deployed to record network access behavior

**3. Network Access Control**
- Network Access Control (NAC) implemented; unauthorized devices are prohibited from connecting
- 802.1X authentication implemented to ensure the legitimacy of connecting devices
- VLAN isolation implemented; different business systems are in different VLANs
- ACL (Access Control List) implemented to restrict cross-zone access
- MAC address binding implemented to prevent ARP spoofing

**4. Encrypted Communication**
- All cross-zone data transmissions use SSL/TLS encryption
- Remote management uses SSH encryption protocol
- VPN communications use IPSec or SSL VPN encryption
- Sensitive data transmission uses end-to-end encryption

#### (III) Secure Zone Boundary

**1. Security Zone Classification**

| Security Zone | Security Level | Included Systems | Boundary Protection Measures |
|:---|:---:|:---|:---|
| Internet Access Zone | Low | External interfaces, reverse proxy | Firewall + DDoS protection |
| DMZ Zone | Medium | Web servers, mail servers | Firewall + WAF + IPS |
| Business Application Zone | High | Business application systems, middleware | Firewall + IPS |
| Data Zone | High | Databases, storage systems | Firewall + database audit |
| Management Zone | High | O&M management, monitoring systems | Firewall + bastion host |
| Development/Testing Zone | Medium | Development environment, testing environment | Firewall + isolation policy |

**2. Boundary Protection Measures**
- Firewalls deployed at the boundaries of each security zone, implementing strict access control policies
- Firewall policies follow the "default deny, open as needed" principle
- Firewall policies reviewed monthly to ensure consistency with business requirements
- Intrusion detection/prevention systems deployed at boundaries to monitor attack behavior in real-time
- Traffic monitoring systems deployed at boundaries with real-time alerts for abnormal traffic
- Network audit systems deployed at boundaries to record all cross-zone access behavior

**3. Malicious Code Prevention**
- Anti-virus gateway deployed at network boundaries
- All data entering and leaving the network undergoes malicious code detection
- Malicious code database automatically updated daily
- Malicious code immediately blocked and alerted upon discovery
- Regular assessment of malicious code prevention effectiveness

#### (IV) Secure Computing Environment

**1. Identity Authentication**
- All system users use unique identity identifiers
- Two-factor authentication implemented (username + password + dynamic verification code)
- Password length ≥8 characters, including uppercase and lowercase letters, numbers, and special characters
- Passwords forcibly changed every 90 days
- Accounts automatically locked after 5 consecutive failed login attempts
- Critical systems use biometric-assisted authentication

**2. Access Control**
- Principle of least privilege implemented; permissions assigned according to job responsibilities
- Permission matrix established, clearly defining access permissions for each position
- Privileged accounts subject to approval system with full operation recording
- User permissions reviewed quarterly to promptly clean up expired permissions
- Role-Based Access Control (RBAC) implemented
- Critical operations subject to dual-person review system

**3. Security Audit**
- Audit logging enabled on all systems
- Audit logs include user ID, operation time, operation type, and operation result
- Audit log retention period not less than 12 months
- Audit logs protected against tampering
- Security audit logs reviewed weekly
- SIEM system deployed for centralized log management and correlation analysis

**4. Intrusion Prevention**
- Host Intrusion Detection System (HIDS) deployed on all servers
- Regular vulnerability scanning and penetration testing conducted
- Security patches installed promptly
- Unnecessary services and ports closed
- System security hardening implemented
- Endpoint Detection and Response (EDR) system deployed

**5. Data Integrity**
- Integrity verification mechanisms used for important data transmissions
- Database integrity constraints implemented
- Critical data protected with digital signatures
- Regular data integrity checks conducted
- Data backup integrity verification implemented

**6. Data Confidentiality**
- Sensitive data encrypted with AES-256 for storage
- Data transmission encrypted with SSL/TLS
- Sensitive database fields encrypted for storage
- Keys subject to hierarchical management with regular rotation
- Data desensitized before use in testing environments

## 8.2 Technical Security Assurance Plan

### 8.2.1 Network Security Assurance

#### (I) Firewall Policy

1. **Policy Principle**: Adopt the "least privilege" principle, deny all traffic by default, only open necessary ports and services.
2. **Access Control**:
   - External to internal: Only open necessary web service ports (80/443), all other ports denied
   - Internal to external: Restrict access scope, prohibit access to high-risk websites and malicious IPs
   - Between internal zones: Divide security zones according to business needs, control inter-zone access
3. **Policy Update**: Review firewall policies monthly, adjust promptly according to business changes.
4. **Log Audit**: Enable firewall logging, record all denied and permitted connections.

#### (II) Intrusion Detection

1. **IDS/IPS Deployment**: Deploy intrusion detection/prevention systems at key network nodes.
2. **Signature Database Update**: Update intrusion detection signature database weekly to ensure the latest threats can be detected.
3. **Alert Configuration**: Configure reasonable alert rules to avoid false positives and false negatives.
4. **Incident Handling**: When intrusion behavior is detected, immediately initiate the security incident response process.

#### (III) Vulnerability Scanning

**Table 8-4 Vulnerability Scanning Plan**

| Scanning Type | Scanning Frequency | Scanning Scope | Scanning Tool | Scanning Report |
|:---|:---|:---|:---|:---|
| Routine vulnerability scanning | Once per month | All servers, network devices, security devices | Nessus/OpenVAS | Monthly Vulnerability Scanning Report |
| Special vulnerability scanning | As needed | Specific systems or devices | Professional tools | Special Vulnerability Scanning Report |
| Penetration testing | Once per year | Core systems and networks | Manual + tools | Penetration Testing Report |

#### (IV) Security Audit

1. **Audit Scope**: Operating systems, databases, network devices, security devices, application systems.
2. **Audit Content**:
   - User login and permission change records
   - System configuration change records
   - Sensitive data access records
   - Security incident records
3. **Audit Logs**: Log retention period not less than 6 months.
4. **Log Review**: Review security logs weekly, handle anomalies promptly.

#### Project Overview

The [City Name] Government Service Hall Informatization O&M Project was officially launched in [Year], serving as a core component of the [City Name] "Internet + Government Services" system construction. The project aims to provide comprehensive informatization O&M support services for the [City Name] Government Service Hall, ensuring the stable operation of various information systems, network devices, and terminal equipment within the hall, and improving government service efficiency and public experience.

The project is located at the [City Name] Government Service Center, with a total building area of approximately [ ] square meters, [ ] service windows, covering [ ] departments and [ ] government service items. It serves approximately [ ] visitors per day, with a daily processing volume of approximately [ ] cases. As the core hub of [City Name]'s government services, the hall undertakes the important function of "one-stop" government services for the entire city.

The hall adopts a "comprehensive window + specialized window" service model, where comprehensive windows uniformly accept government service items authorized and entrusted by various departments, achieving "one-window acceptance, integrated services." The hall features functional areas such as self-service areas, waiting areas, and complaint/suggestion areas, equipped with queue management systems, self-service terminals, LED displays, and other convenience facilities, providing a comfortable and convenient environment for the public.

As an important initiative of [City Name] to deepen the "streamline administration, delegate power, and improve services" reform, this project has received high attention from the municipal party committee and government. The project has been listed as an annual livelihood project and a key digital government construction project for [City Name], led by the Municipal Big Data Development Management Administration, with procurement handled by the Municipal Public Resource Trading Center, aiming to create a provincial-level benchmark for government service hall informatization.

#### Service Scope

The service scope of this project covers the informatization system O&M of the [City Name] Government Service Hall and its [ ] sub-centers, specifically including:

- **Network Infrastructure O&M**: Daily O&M and fault handling of [ ] units of equipment including core switches, aggregation switches, access switches, wireless AP devices, network structured cabling systems, and network security devices. The network system covers all floors and functional areas of the hall, achieving full coverage of both wired and wireless networks. Core network devices use dual hot-standby to ensure high network availability;
- **Server and Storage Device O&M**: O&M management of [ ] servers (including [ ] physical servers and [ ] virtualized servers) and [ ] sets of storage devices. The server cluster uses virtualization technology to achieve elastic allocation and load balancing of computing resources;
- **Terminal Device O&M**: Maintenance of [ ] computers, [ ] printers, [ ] self-service terminals, [ ] queue ticket machines, [ ] LED displays, and other terminal devices. Terminal devices are distributed across various windows and self-service areas of the hall, providing convenient service tools for the public and staff;
- **Application System O&M**: O&M support for the Government Service Comprehensive Management Platform, One-Stop Online Service System, WeChat Official Account Service Platform, and [ ] departmental business systems. The application systems cover the entire process of informatization management from business acceptance, review, completion to archiving;
- **Security Assurance Services**: Network security monitoring, vulnerability scanning, security incident emergency response, data backup and recovery, and other security O&M services. Security assurance covers multiple layers including network layer, host layer, application layer, and data layer;
- **Technical Training Services**: Information system operation training and technical support for hall staff. Training content includes system operation, common problem handling, and security awareness training.

Additionally, this project provides the following value-added services:
- Monthly O&M analysis reports for comprehensive assessment of system operational status;
- Quarterly emergency drills to test emergency response capabilities;
- Annual system optimization and upgrade recommendations for continuous performance improvement;
- Special assurance services for major events and holidays.

#### Technical Architecture

This project adopts a "one center, one platform, multiple systems" technical architecture:

- **One Center**: The Government Data Center, deployed on [Cloud Platform Name], using virtualization technology to achieve elastic allocation of computing resources. The core database uses [Database Type] to achieve high availability and disaster recovery. The data center is equipped with UPS uninterruptible power supply, precision air conditioning, fire suppression systems, security systems, and other infrastructure to ensure the safety and stability of the computer room environment;
- **One Platform**: The Government Service Comprehensive Management Platform, serving as the core carrier of hall operations management, integrating functional modules such as window management, queue management, electronic supervision, performance assessment, and data analysis. The platform uses a B/S architecture, supporting both PC and mobile access, achieving comprehensive informatization of hall operations management;
- **Multiple Systems**: Including the One-Stop Online Service System, mobile service platform, self-service system, video surveillance system, access control management system, and multiple business subsystems. Data sharing and business collaboration among systems are achieved through a unified data exchange platform.

The network architecture adopts a "three-network convergence" design, namely the e-government external network, the Internet, and the Internet of Things working in coordination, achieving secure data exchange between different security domains through security isolation and controlled interconnection. Core network devices use dual hot-standby to ensure high network availability. Network security is ensured through the deployment of firewalls, intrusion detection, security audit, and other devices, forming a defense-in-depth system.

The system architecture design follows the following principles:
- **High Availability**: Critical devices and systems use redundant design to ensure that single-point failures do not affect overall operation;
- **Scalability**: System architecture supports smooth expansion to meet business growth requirements;
- **Security**: Designed and deployed according to Cybersecurity Classified Protection Level 3 requirements;
- **Manageability**: Provides unified monitoring and management interfaces to reduce O&M complexity.

- Phase 3 (12 months after launch): Achieve intelligent O&M, fully meet all KPI indicators.

**Quality Objectives:**
- Service report submission timeliness rate: 100%;
