- Training plan completion rate: 100%;
- Major security incidents: 0.

### 9.1.2 Technical Solution

#### O&M Solution

This project adopts a "prevention-oriented, proactive O&M" service philosophy and establishes a comprehensive O&M management system:

**1. Inspection and Maintenance System**

A four-level inspection and maintenance system is established consisting of daily inspection, weekly maintenance, monthly assessment, and quarterly drills:

- Daily inspections [ ] times, including comprehensive pre-opening check (7:00-8:30), midday key area inspection (11:30-13:00), and post-closing system check (17:30-19:00). Inspection content covers network connectivity checks, server operational status checks, application system availability checks, and security device status checks;
- Weekly deep maintenance, including equipment cleaning, system optimization, security scanning, log analysis, and performance tuning. Deep maintenance is scheduled during weekend non-working hours to avoid affecting normal hall operations;
- Monthly comprehensive assessment with O&M analysis reports and optimization recommendations. Report content includes system operational overview, fault statistical analysis, performance trend analysis, security posture analysis, and optimization recommendations;
- Quarterly emergency drills to test emergency response capabilities. Drill scenarios include network failures, server failures, application system failures, and security incidents.

**2. Fault Classification and Handling Mechanism**

Faults are classified into three levels based on impact scope and severity, with tiered handling:

- **Level 1 Fault (System Paralysis)**: Serious faults affecting the entire hall's business operations. Response time: [ ] minutes, recovery time: [ ] hours. Emergency plan activated, Project Manager arrives on-site immediately to direct handling, while reporting to the client's relevant responsible person;
- **Level 2 Fault (Partial Function Anomaly)**: Medium faults affecting partial business functions. Response time: [ ] minutes, recovery time: [ ] hours. O&M engineers immediately proceed to the scene for handling, Project Manager tracks and supervises;
- **Level 3 Fault (Individual Device Failure)**: General faults affecting a single device or terminal. Response time: [ ] minutes, recovery time: [ ] hours. O&M engineers handle remotely or on-site, engineer supervisor confirms handling results.

**3. Change Management Process**

A strict change management process is established. All system changes must submit change requests [ ] working days in advance and can only be implemented after evaluation and approval. The change management process includes: change request, change review, change approval, change implementation, change verification, and change closure. Changes must be implemented during non-working hours (typically 18:00-6:00 the next day or weekends) to avoid affecting normal hall operations. Each change must have a detailed change plan and rollback plan, and all relevant parties must be notified before implementation.

**4. Service Level Management**

A clear Service Level Agreement (SLA) is signed with the client, defining service indicators and assessment standards:
- Network availability: ≥99.99%;
- System availability: ≥99.95%;
- Mean time to recovery (MTTR): ≤30 minutes;
- Inspection execution rate: 100%;
- Service report submission timeliness rate: 100%.

SLA compliance is assessed monthly, with assessment results linked to O&M service fees.

#### Technical Highlights

**1. Intelligent O&M Monitoring Platform**

A self-developed intelligent O&M monitoring platform is deployed, achieving full-chain monitoring of networks, servers, terminals, and application systems. The platform features the following capabilities:

- **Unified Monitoring Dashboard**: Real-time display of all system operational status with multi-dimensional data visualization. Dashboard content includes network topology diagrams, server operational status diagrams, application system availability diagrams, and security posture diagrams, with support for customized display content and layout;
- **Intelligent Alert Engine**: Based on machine learning algorithms, achieves early warning and intelligent fault localization. The alert engine supports alert noise reduction, alert correlation, and alert escalation, effectively reducing false positives and false negatives. By analyzing historical alert data, an alert pattern library is established for intelligent alert classification and automated handling recommendations;
- **O&M Knowledge Base**: Accumulates [ ] common fault handling solutions with intelligent search and automatic recommendation support. The knowledge base uses natural language processing technology, allowing O&M personnel to quickly find solutions through keyword search, voice search, and other methods. The knowledge base supports intelligent recommendation, automatically recommending relevant handling solutions based on alert types;
- **Mobile O&M APP**: Supports O&M personnel in receiving alerts, handling work orders, and viewing system status anytime, anywhere. The APP supports push notifications, voice calls, photo uploads, and other functions for convenient on-site problem resolution.

**2. Automated O&M Tools**

Automated O&M tools are introduced to achieve the following automation scenarios:

- **Automated server configuration deployment and batch updates**: Through automation scripts, batch server configuration, software installation, and patch updates are achieved, reducing single-server configuration time from 2 hours to 15 minutes;
- **Remote diagnosis and automatic repair of terminal devices**: Through remote management tools, remote diagnosis, troubleshooting, and software repair of terminal devices are achieved, reducing on-site maintenance workload;
- **Automated system patch testing and distribution**: A patch management process is established to automate patch testing, approval, distribution, and verification, ensuring timely remediation of system security vulnerabilities;
- **Automated data backup scheduling and verification**: Through backup management tools, automated scheduling, execution, and verification of data backups are achieved, ensuring backup data completeness and availability.

**3. Data-Driven Service Optimization**

Through big data analysis technology, deep mining of hall operational data is conducted:

- **Analysis of peak service periods**: By analyzing historical case data, daily, weekly, and monthly peak service periods are identified, with proactive adjustment of system resource allocation to ensure peak performance;
- **Statistics on high-frequency business types**: Analysis of processing frequency and duration for each business type, optimizing system performance configuration to improve processing efficiency for high-frequency services;
- **Tracking equipment failure patterns**: Analysis of equipment failure time distribution, type distribution, and regional distribution patterns, optimizing preventive maintenance plans to reduce equipment failure rates;
- **Collection of user feedback data**: Through satisfaction surveys, complaints/suggestions, and on-site interviews, user feedback data is collected for continuous service quality improvement.

#### Innovation Points

**1. "O&M + Operations" Integrated Service Model**

Breaking through the limitations of traditional O&M that focuses only on technical support, this project innovatively combines O&M services with business operations. The O&M team is not only responsible for stable system operation but also proactively participates in business process optimization, service efficiency improvement, and other operational-level work, providing value-added consulting services to the client. Specifically:
- Regularly analyze business data and propose business process optimization recommendations;
- Participate in service process reengineering to improve service efficiency;
- Assist the client in service innovation to enhance public satisfaction;
- Provide industry best practice references to promote government service level improvement.

**2. "Dual-Track" Personnel Assurance Mechanism**

A "dual-track" assurance mechanism is established with on-site personnel and remote support teams working collaboratively. The on-site team is responsible for daily O&M and on-site support, while the remote expert team provides technical problem resolution and new technology research support, forming a "on-site + remote" three-dimensional technical assurance system. The on-site team consists of Project Manager, O&M engineers, and network engineers responsible for daily O&M work; the remote support team consists of technical experts, security engineers, and database experts providing remote technical support.

**3. "Closed-Loop" Service Quality Control**

A "Plan-Do-Check-Act" (PDCA) closed-loop management mechanism is established through monthly service quality assessments, quarterly satisfaction surveys, and annual service summaries to achieve continuous service quality improvement. The four phases of the PDCA cycle are:
- **Plan**: Develop monthly, quarterly, and annual service plans with clear service objectives and key work;
- **Do**: Execute O&M service tasks according to plan to ensure service quality;
- **Check**: Through service quality assessments and satisfaction surveys, check service execution status and effectiveness;
- **Act**: For identified issues, develop improvement measures to continuously optimize service processes and quality.

#### 9.1.6.2 Key Node Control

To ensure smooth project implementation, the following 7 key control nodes are established:

**Key Node 1: Requirements Confirmation (Week 3)**
- Organize requirements review with business and technical departments to clarify O&M service scope and content;
- Confirm SLA indicators, response times, fault classification, and other key parameters;
- Confirm personnel allocation, duty arrangements, report formats, and other management requirements;
- Produce requirements baseline documents signed and confirmed by both parties;
- Establish requirements change management process to ensure controllability of requirements changes.

**Key Node 2: Architecture Review (Week 6)**
- Invite industry experts to review the technical architecture plan to ensure reasonability and feasibility;
- Focus on reviewing architecture reliability, scalability, and security;
- Review network architecture, system architecture, security architecture, and data architecture designs;
- Optimize design plan based on review opinions to produce final technical plan;
- Organize technical plan handover to ensure the implementation team understands the design intent.

**Key Node 3: Equipment Arrival Acceptance (Week 8)**
- Verify equipment model, quantity, and configuration item by item against the contract list;
- Check equipment appearance, accessories, and documentation for completeness;
- Conduct equipment power-on testing and functional verification;
- Produce equipment arrival acceptance report documenting acceptance results;
- Promptly handle non-conforming equipment to ensure project progress is not affected.

**Key Node 4: System Launch (Week 16)**
- Develop detailed launch switchover plan and rollback plan to ensure business continuity;
- Organize pre-launch comprehensive check and risk assessment to confirm launch conditions;
- Execute switchover during off-peak hours to minimize business impact;
- Strengthen monitoring of system operational status after launch, promptly identify and handle issues;
- Prepare emergency plan to ensure quick rollback if problems occur.

**Key Node 5: Trial Operation Assessment (Week 20)**
- Conduct comprehensive assessment of all indicators during the trial operation period;
- Analyze system operational data to identify potential issues and optimization opportunities;
- Collect user feedback to understand system usage experience;
- Produce trial operation assessment report with optimization recommendations;
- Adjust O&M strategy and resource allocation based on assessment results.

**Key Node 6: Quarterly Review (Week 28)**
- Report quarterly O&M service status to the client, including service indicator completion, fault statistical analysis, and key work completion;
- Analyze KPI completion and propose improvement measures;
- Confirm next quarter's work plan and priorities;
- Collect opinions and suggestions from the client;
- Produce quarterly summary report signed and confirmed by both parties.

**Key Node 7: Annual Final Acceptance (Week 52)**
- Comprehensively summarize annual O&M service work, including service achievements, innovation highlights, and improvement measures;
- Prepare complete acceptance materials, including O&M reports, test reports, and satisfaction survey reports;
- Cooperate with the client for annual final acceptance, accepting inspection and review by the acceptance team;
- Develop rectification plan for issues found during acceptance;
- Sign acceptance report to confirm acceptance conclusion.

| Training Phase | Week 12-13 | User training, operation training, management training | Training Instructor |
| Trial Operation | Week 13-16 | Trial operation, issue collection, system optimization | O&M Team |
| Official Launch | Week 16 | System switchover, launch verification, enhanced monitoring | Project Manager |
| O&M Services | Week 16-52 | Daily O&M, regular assessment, continuous optimization | O&M Team |
| Annual Final Acceptance | Week 52 | Summary report, document archiving, acceptance confirmation | Project Manager |

#### 9.1.6.5 Detailed Implementation Content for Each Project Phase

**Phase 1: Project Launch (Week 1-2)**

Main work content during the project launch phase includes:
- Establish the project team, determine key personnel for positions such as Project Manager, Technical Lead, and Quality Lead;
- Hold a project launch meeting to introduce project overview, work plan, and management requirements to project team members and the client;
- Develop a project plan defining project objectives, scope, schedule, resources, risks, and other management plans;
- Establish project communication mechanisms, determining communication methods, frequency, and content;
- Prepare project office space and equipment;
- Collect and organize project-related documentation.

**Phase 2: Requirements Research (Week 3-5)**

Main work content during the requirements research phase includes:
- Conduct comprehensive investigation of the hall's existing information systems to understand system status, operational conditions, and existing problems;
- Conduct in-depth interviews with business personnel from various departments to understand business needs and service expectations;
- Analyze existing O&M processes and O&M records to assess O&M management level;
- Write requirements research report detailing current situation analysis, requirements description, and proposed solutions;
- Organize requirements review meeting to confirm requirements baseline with the client.

**Phase 3: Detailed Design (Week 6-7)**

Main work content during the detailed design phase includes:
- Based on the requirements baseline, design the technical architecture plan including network architecture, system architecture, and security architecture;
- Design the O&M service system plan including organizational structure, job responsibilities, and service processes;
- Design the O&M platform functional plan including monitoring, alerting, work orders, and reporting functions;
- Organize technical plan review, inviting experts to evaluate the plan;
- Optimize the plan based on review opinions to produce the final design plan.

**Phase 4: Equipment Procurement and Acceptance (Week 7-8)**

Main work content during the equipment procurement and acceptance phase includes:
- Prepare equipment procurement list based on the design plan;
- Conduct equipment procurement according to government procurement processes;
- After equipment arrival, conduct item-by-item acceptance verifying model, quantity, and configuration;
- Conduct equipment power-on testing and functional verification;
- Produce equipment arrival acceptance report.

**Phase 5: System Deployment (Week 9-10)**

Main work content during the system deployment phase includes:
- Conduct equipment installation and cabling according to the design plan;
- Deploy O&M monitoring platform, configure monitoring indicators and alert rules;
- Configure network devices and security devices;
- Conduct system functional testing and performance testing;
- Produce system deployment report.

**Phase 6: System Integration (Week 11-12)**

Main work content during the system integration phase includes:
- Conduct integration testing between systems to verify data interaction and business collaboration;
- Conduct stress testing to verify system performance under high load;
- Conduct security testing to verify the effectiveness of security protection measures;
- Record test results and produce integration testing report;
- Rectify issues found during testing.

**Phase 7: Training Phase (Week 12-13)**

Main work content during the training phase includes:
- Prepare training materials including operation manuals, FAQ documents, and case analyses;
- Conduct system operation training for hall staff to ensure proficient use of all application systems;
- Conduct O&M management training for management personnel to ensure effective use of the O&M management platform;
- Conduct security awareness training to improve staff information security awareness;
- Document training activities and produce training records.

**Phase 8: Trial Operation (Week 13-16)**

Main work content during the trial operation phase includes:
- Launch trial operation according to the trial operation plan, fully taking over O&M work;
- Strengthen system monitoring, closely monitoring system operational status;
- Promptly handle issues and faults during the trial operation period;
- Collect user feedback to understand system usage experience;
- Optimize and adjust the system to ensure stable operation.

**Phase 9: Official Launch (Week 16)**

Main work content during the official launch phase includes:
- Develop detailed launch switchover plan and rollback plan;
- Organize pre-launch comprehensive check to confirm launch conditions;
- Execute switchover during off-peak hours;
- Strengthen monitoring after launch to ensure stable system operation;
- After confirming normal system operation, announce official launch.

**Phase 10: O&M Services (Week 16-52)**

Main work content during the O&M services phase includes:
- Execute daily O&M services according to SLA requirements, including inspection, maintenance, and fault handling;
- Regularly produce O&M monthly, quarterly, and annual reports to report service status;
- Continuously optimize O&M processes and service quality;
- Conduct regular emergency drills to test emergency response capabilities;
- Collect user feedback for continuous service improvement.

**Phase 11: Annual Final Acceptance (Week 52)**

Main work content during the annual final acceptance phase includes:
- Comprehensively summarize annual O&M service work;
- Organize acceptance materials including O&M reports, test reports, and satisfaction survey reports;
- Cooperate with the client for annual final acceptance;
- Develop rectification plan for issues found during acceptance;
- Sign acceptance report to confirm acceptance conclusion.

## 9.2 Case 2: A Provincial Government Cloud Platform O&M Service Project

### 9.2.1 Project Background

#### Project Overview

The [Province Name] Government Cloud Platform O&M Service Project is a key project of [Province Name]'s digital government construction, launched in [Year]. The platform hosts the operations of [ ] departments and [ ] government application systems across [ Province Name], serving as the "core engine" for the province's government informatization operations.

The platform is deployed at [Data Center Name], using a "two cities, three centers" architecture design, namely two data centers and one disaster recovery center, ensuring the continuity of government services under extreme conditions. The platform's total computing capacity reaches [ ] CPU cores, [ ] TB of memory, and [ ] PB of storage capacity, processing [ ] billion government data records annually.

This government cloud platform is the core infrastructure for [Province Name]'s "Digital Government" construction, built and operated following the principle of "intensive construction, shared applications." The platform uses cloud computing technology to provide departments with infrastructure services such as computing, storage, and networking, as well as platform services such as databases and middleware. The platform's operation has effectively resolved the problem of isolated and redundant informatization construction across departments, achieving intensive resource utilization.

#### Service Scope

The service scope of this project covers the comprehensive O&M of the [Province Name] Government Cloud Platform, specifically including:

- **Cloud Platform Infrastructure O&M**: Including O&M management of computing resources, storage resources, and network resources, involving [ ] physical servers, [ ] virtual machine instances, and [ ] storage arrays. O&M work includes equipment inspection, fault handling, performance optimization, and capacity management;
- **Cloud Platform Software O&M**: Including O&M of cloud operating systems, container platforms, database middleware, message queues, and other foundational software. O&M work includes software installation and configuration, version upgrades, performance tuning, and fault troubleshooting;
- **Cloud Security O&M**: Including cloud security monitoring, firewall management, intrusion detection, vulnerability remediation, and security audit. Security O&M covers multiple layers including network security, host security, application security, and data security;
- **Cloud Application System O&M**: Monitoring and O&M coordination of [ ] government application systems hosted on the cloud platform. O&M work includes application system monitoring, performance analysis, fault coordination, and change management;
- **Data Backup and Recovery**: Implementing regular backup of core data and disaster recovery drills. Backup strategies include full backup, incremental backup, and differential backup, with backup data stored off-site;
- **Cloud Platform Performance Optimization**: Continuously optimizing cloud platform resource utilization and application system performance. Optimization work includes resource scheduling optimization, storage performance optimization, and network performance optimization.

#### Technical Architecture

This project adopts a "one cloud, multiple pools, tiered management" technical architecture:

- **One Cloud**: A unified government cloud platform built on mainstream cloud platform technologies such as OpenStack/VMware, providing IaaS and PaaS layer services. The cloud platform supports both virtual machine and container computing modes to meet the operational requirements of different application systems;
- **Multiple Pools**: Multiple resource pools divided according to business security and performance requirements, including general-purpose resource pools, high-performance resource pools, security resource pools, and development/testing resource pools. Different resource pools use different hardware configurations and security policies;
- **Tiered Management**: Province-city-county three-tier management, with the province responsible for overall platform O&M, cities responsible for local resource management, and counties responsible for application system management. Tiered management is achieved through permission control and resource quotas.

The network architecture uses SDN (Software-Defined Networking) technology for flexible scheduling and automated management of network resources. The security protection system uses a "one center, three-layer protection" design, namely the Security Management Center, network security protection, host security protection, and application security protection.

### 9.2.2 Technical Solution

#### O&M Solution

**1. Cloud O&M Management System**

A cloud O&M management system conforming to ITIL best practices is established, covering core processes including incident management, problem management, change management, configuration management, release management, and service level management. The processes are interconnected to form a complete O&M management closed loop.

- **Incident Management**: Responsible for handling various O&M incidents, including fault reports and service requests. The incident management process includes incident recording, classification, priority assignment, handling, and closure;
- **Problem Management**: Responsible for analyzing root causes of incidents, developing solutions, and preventing recurrence. The problem management process includes problem identification, root cause analysis, solution development, and problem closure;
- **Change Management**: Responsible for managing system changes to ensure change safety and controllability. The change management process includes change request, review, approval, implementation, verification, and closure;
- **Configuration Management**: Responsible for maintaining configuration item information, including device configurations, software configurations, and network configurations. Configuration management provides accurate configuration information to support other O&M processes;
- **Release Management**: Responsible for software and system releases, including version management, release planning, release implementation, and release verification;
- **Service Level Management**: Responsible for defining and managing Service Level Agreements (SLAs), monitoring SLA compliance, and continuously improving service quality.

**2. Cloud Resource Monitoring Solution**

A comprehensive monitoring system covering IaaS, PaaS, and SaaS layers is established:

- **Infrastructure Layer Monitoring**: Real-time monitoring of server CPU, memory, disk, and network indicators. Monitoring indicators include CPU utilization, memory utilization, disk utilization, network throughput, and network latency;
- **Virtualization Layer Monitoring**: Monitoring of virtual machine operational status, resource usage, and performance. Monitoring indicators include virtual machine count, resource allocation rate, and virtual machine migration count;
- **Platform Layer Monitoring**: Monitoring of cloud operating systems, container platforms, and middleware. Monitoring indicators include platform service availability, API response time, and task queue length;
- **Application Layer Monitoring**: Availability and performance monitoring of application systems running on the cloud. Monitoring indicators include application response time, concurrent users, and error rate;
- **Security Layer Monitoring**: Monitoring of security device logs, intrusion detection alerts, and vulnerability scan results. Monitoring indicators include security incident count, vulnerability count, and compliance rate.

**3. Cloud Security O&M Solution**

A comprehensive cloud security O&M system is established:

- **Security Operations Center (7×24 hours)**: Real-time security posture monitoring with timely discovery and handling of security threats. The Security Operations Center is staffed with security analysts who use the SIEM platform for security event correlation analysis and threat intelligence matching;
- **Regular Security Assessment**: Monthly vulnerability scanning, quarterly penetration testing, and annual security risk assessment;
- **Security Incident Emergency Response**: A tiered security incident response mechanism is established to ensure major security incidents are handled within [ ] hours. The emergency response process includes incident discovery, analysis and assessment, containment and handling, root cause analysis, recovery and reconstruction, and summary improvement;
- **Data Security Protection**: Implementing data classification and grading management, with core data encrypted for storage and transmission. Data access control policies are established to ensure data confidentiality, integrity, and availability.

#### Technical Highlights

**1. Cloud-Native O&M Capabilities**

The team possesses cloud-native O&M capabilities, proficient in Kubernetes container orchestration, microservice governance, DevOps pipelines, and other cloud-native technologies, effectively supporting the cloud-native transformation of government applications. Specifically:
- Deployment, O&M, and monitoring of containerized applications;
- Management and optimization of Kubernetes clusters;
- Design and governance of microservice architectures;
- Setup and maintenance of CI/CD pipelines;
- Deployment and management of service meshes.

**2. AIOps Intelligent O&M**

Artificial Intelligence for IT Operations (AIOps) technology is introduced to achieve:

- **Anomaly Detection**: Based on historical data-trained models, automatically discovering system anomalies. Anomaly detection algorithms include statistical analysis, machine learning, deep learning, and other methods, capable of identifying various types of anomalies;
- **Root Cause Analysis**: Through correlation analysis, quickly locating fault root causes. The root cause analysis engine can automatically correlate multiple alert events, identify the fundamental cause of faults, and reduce manual investigation time;
- **Capacity Prediction**: Based on business growth trends, predicting resource requirements. The capacity prediction model can predict computing, storage, network, and other resource demand trends 3-6 months in advance, providing data support for resource planning;
- **Intelligent Self-Healing**: Automatic diagnosis and repair of common faults. The intelligent self-healing engine can automatically execute predefined repair scripts to quickly restore normal system operation.

**3. Multi-Cloud Management Capabilities**

Possessing multi-cloud unified management capabilities, able to simultaneously manage resources across government cloud, public cloud, and other cloud platforms, achieving unified resource scheduling and management. The multi-cloud management platform provides unified resource views, unified monitoring and alerting, and unified O&M operation interfaces, supporting cross-cloud resource scheduling and data migration.

#### Innovation Points

**1. "Cloud Chief" O&M Governance Model**

Innovatively establishing a "Cloud Chief" O&M governance system, clarifying three-level management responsibilities for cloud platforms, cloud resources, and cloud applications, achieving clear authority and responsibility with collaborative and efficient O&M management. The core content of the "Cloud Chief" system includes:
- Provincial "Cloud Chief" responsible for overall cloud platform O&M management;
- Municipal "Cloud Chief" responsible for local cloud resource management;
- Departmental "Cloud Chief" responsible for departmental cloud application management;
- Establishing regular consultation mechanisms to coordinate cross-level and cross-departmental O&M issues.

**2. "Cloud Butler" Service System**

Establishing a "Cloud Butler" service system, assigning a dedicated cloud butler to each department migrating to the cloud, providing one-on-one technical support and consulting services to ensure stable operation of each department's business systems. The main responsibilities of cloud butlers include:
- Responsible for daily management and monitoring of the department's cloud resources;
- Coordinating and handling the department's cloud application O&M issues;
- Providing technical consulting and training services;
- Regularly producing the department's cloud resource usage reports.

**3. "Zero Trust" Security Architecture**

Pioneering the introduction of the "Zero Trust" security architecture in government cloud O&M, implementing the "never trust, always verify" security concept, effectively enhancing the cloud platform's security protection level. The core elements of the Zero Trust security architecture include:
- Identity Authentication: Strict identity authentication for all access requests;
- Least Privilege: Access permissions assigned according to the principle of least privilege;
- Micro-Segmentation: Network micro-segmentation to limit lateral movement;
- Continuous Verification: Continuous monitoring and verification of access behavior.

### 9.2.6 Detailed Implementation Process of Case 2

#### 9.2.6.1 Detailed Technical Innovation Points

This project has developed the following 7 core technical innovations during implementation:

**Technical Innovation 1: AI-Based Cloud Resource Intelligent Scheduling Algorithm**

Innovatively applying deep reinforcement learning algorithms to cloud resource scheduling, achieving intelligent allocation of computing resources. The algorithm automatically adjusts virtual machine resource allocation strategies based on historical load data and business prediction models, increasing resource utilization from 45% to 72% while maintaining performance SLAs for all application systems.

Technical Principle: Using the Deep Q-Network (DQN) algorithm to model cloud resource scheduling as a Markov Decision Process. The state space includes resource utilization of each virtual machine and application system performance indicators; the action space includes virtual machine resource adjustment operations (add/remove CPU, memory, etc.); the reward function considers both resource utilization and SLA compliance. Through continuous learning and optimization, the algorithm automatically finds the optimal resource scheduling strategy.

Application Scenario: Applicable to resource management of large numbers of virtual machines in government cloud platforms, particularly in scenarios with significant business load fluctuations, automatically adjusting resource allocation to balance system performance and resource utilization efficiency.

**Technical Innovation 2: Multi-Cloud Heterogeneous Environment Unified Management Platform**

Self-developed multi-cloud heterogeneous environment unified management platform supporting unified management of OpenStack, VMware, Kubernetes, and other cloud platforms. The platform provides unified resource views, unified monitoring and alerting, and unified O&M operation interfaces, significantly reducing O&M complexity in multi-cloud environments.

Technical Principle: Using the adapter pattern to develop unified API adapters for each cloud platform, standardizing different platform API calls into standard interfaces. The platform layer provides unified resource management, monitoring and alerting, and O&M operations, interacting with underlying cloud platforms through adapters.

Application Scenario: Applicable to scenarios where multiple cloud platforms coexist in government informatization construction, achieving unified resource management and scheduling.

**Technical Innovation 3: Service Mesh-Based Microservice Governance Solution**

Introducing Istio service mesh technology for unified governance of microservices on the government cloud platform, including service discovery, load balancing, traffic management, circuit breaking and degradation, and distributed tracing, enhancing system stability and observability in microservice architectures.

Technical Principle: Istio uses the Sidecar proxy pattern, deploying an Envoy proxy alongside each microservice instance to intercept all incoming and outgoing traffic for transparent traffic management and security control. The control plane handles configuration management and policy distribution, while the data plane handles traffic forwarding and processing.

Application Scenario: Applicable to government application systems using microservice architectures, solving governance challenges in microservice environments.

**Technical Innovation 4: Cloud-Native Security Situational Awareness System**

Building a cloud-native security situational awareness system integrating multi-dimensional data including cloud platform logs, traffic, and configurations, using big data analysis and machine learning technology to achieve real-time security posture perception and threat early warning.

Technical Principle: The system collects multi-dimensional data including cloud platform security logs, network traffic, and system configurations, performing correlation analysis and anomaly detection through a big data analysis platform. Machine learning algorithms establish security baseline models to automatically identify security anomalies and potential threats.

Application Scenario: Applicable to real-time security monitoring and threat early warning for government cloud platforms, enabling timely discovery and handling of security threats.

**Technical Innovation 5: Automated Compliance Check Tool**

Developing an automated compliance check tool that automatically detects whether cloud platform configurations comply with standards such as Classified Protection 2.0 and government cloud security requirements, automatically generating compliance check reports and rectification recommendations, significantly improving compliance management efficiency.

Technical Principle: The tool has a built-in check rule library for standards including Classified Protection 2.0 and government cloud security requirements, automatically scanning cloud platform configuration items, comparing them with the rule library, and identifying non-conforming items. The tool also automatically generates rectification recommendations to guide O&M personnel.

Application Scenario: Applicable to regular compliance checks and rectification for government cloud platforms, ensuring continuous compliance with security standards.

**Technical Innovation 6: Intelligent Capacity Prediction Model**

Based on time series analysis and business growth models, building an intelligent capacity prediction model that can predict computing, storage, network, and other resource demand trends 3-6 months in advance, providing data support for resource planning and budget preparation.

Technical Principle: Using the LSTM (Long Short-Term Memory) time series prediction model combined with business growth factors to analyze and predict historical resource usage data. The model considers business growth trends, seasonal fluctuations, and unexpected events, achieving prediction accuracy above 90%.

Application Scenario: Applicable to resource planning and budget preparation for government cloud platforms, avoiding resource shortages or waste.

**Technical Innovation 7: Cloud Disaster Recovery Automated Switchover Platform**

Self-developed cloud disaster recovery automated switchover platform achieving automated orchestration and one-click switchover for disaster recovery. Reducing disaster recovery switchover time from 4 hours to 30 minutes, significantly enhancing business continuity assurance capabilities.

Technical Principle: The platform uses a workflow engine to decompose the disaster recovery switchover process into multiple automated steps, including data synchronization verification, network switchover, application switchover, and business verification. Each step has clear execution conditions and verification standards to ensure switchover reliability.

Application Scenario: Applicable to disaster recovery drills and actual disaster recovery switchover for government cloud platforms, ensuring business continuity.

#### 9.2.6.2 Difficulty Resolution Records

**Difficulty 1: Unified Monitoring of Heterogeneous Cloud Platforms**

- **Problem Description**: In the early project stage, the government cloud platform contained two heterogeneous environments: OpenStack and VMware. Monitoring data formats were inconsistent, preventing unified monitoring views. O&M personnel needed to switch between multiple systems, resulting in low efficiency. The two platforms had independent monitoring systems with inconsistent data formats, interface protocols, and alert rules, preventing unified monitoring and analysis.
- **Solution**: Designed a unified monitoring data model with standardized monitoring indicator systems and data formats. Developed adapter middleware to uniformly convert OpenStack and VMware monitoring data into standard formats. The adapter middleware uses a plugin architecture for flexible expansion. Also built a unified monitoring dashboard achieving "one screen, full view" monitoring. The dashboard supports customized display content and layout, allowing O&M personnel to select indicators and views as needed.
- **Implementation Effect**: Monitoring efficiency improved by 80%, fault discovery time reduced from an average of 30 minutes to 5 minutes, and O&M personnel workload reduced by 60%. The unified monitoring platform laid a solid foundation for subsequent intelligent O&M and data analysis.

**Difficulty 2: Large-Scale Virtual Machine Performance Optimization**

- **Problem Description**: As cloud applications increased, the number of virtual machines surged to 5,000+, with some VMs experiencing performance bottlenecks, longer application response times, and degraded user experience. Main manifestations included excessive CPU utilization, insufficient memory, and disk IO bottlenecks. Meanwhile, VM resource allocation strategies were relatively crude, with coexisting phenomena of resource waste and resource shortage.
- **Solution**: Introduced AI-driven performance optimization solutions. By analyzing historical VM performance data, performance baseline models were established to automatically identify performance anomalies and bottlenecks. Developed intelligent resource scheduling algorithms that dynamically adjust CPU, memory, disk IO, and other resource allocations based on actual VM load conditions. Also optimized VM resource allocation strategies and implemented dynamic resource scheduling. Specific measures included: implementing VM hot-add resources supporting online resource size adjustment; optimizing VM NUMA affinity configuration to reduce cross-NUMA access latency; implementing tiered storage placing hot data on SSD storage.
- **Implementation Effect**: Average VM response time reduced by 40%, CPU utilization improved by 25%, memory utilization improved by 30%, with significant overall performance improvement. Resource waste was effectively curbed, and resource utilization increased from 45% to 72%.

**Difficulty 3: Cross-Department Collaborative O&M**

- **Problem Description**: The government cloud platform hosted application systems from 80+ departments, each with different O&M service needs and expectations, making coordination difficult and service satisfaction uneven. Main manifestations: significant differences in O&M requirements across departments, some requiring 7×24-hour assurance while others only need business-hours support; varying technical levels across departments, some with professional IT personnel while others lack IT staff; cross-department issues involving coordination among multiple departments with long processing cycles.
- **Solution**: Established a "Cloud Butler" service system, assigning a dedicated cloud butler to each department for one-on-one service. Cloud butlers serve as bridges between departments and the O&M team, collecting and handling departmental O&M needs. Also established cross-department collaborative O&M mechanisms with regular O&M coordination meetings for unified handling of cross-department issues. Additionally, established a tiered service mechanism providing different levels of O&M services based on departmental business importance.
- **Implementation Effect**: Cross-department collaboration efficiency improved by 70%, cross-department issue handling time reduced from an average of 3 days to 1 day, and satisfaction across all departments reached 95% or above. The Cloud Butler service system received widespread recognition and praise from all departments.

## 9.3 Case 3: A Government System Security Assurance Project

### 9.3.1 Project Background

#### Project Overview

The [System Name] Security Assurance Project is a key project for government information security construction in [Region Name]. The project aims to provide comprehensive information security assurance services for [System Name], ensuring the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of the government system, and preventing various cybersecurity threats.

[System Name] is the core government application system of [Region Name], covering [ ] business modules involving daily office work and business processing for [ ] departments, with [ ] 10,000 registered users and [ ] 10,000 daily visits. The system carries a large amount of sensitive government data and citizens' personal information, with extremely high information security requirements.

As the cybersecurity situation becomes increasingly severe, government systems face growing threats, including Advanced Persistent Threats (APT), ransomware, data breaches, and insider threats. This project effectively prevents various security risks through the establishment of a comprehensive security assurance system, ensuring the safe and stable operation of the government system.

#### Service Scope

The service scope of this project includes:

- **Security Monitoring Services**: 7×24-hour cybersecurity monitoring, including network traffic analysis, intrusion detection, and abnormal behavior monitoring. Security monitoring covers multiple areas including network boundaries, internal network zones, and cloud environments;
- **Vulnerability Management Services**: Regular vulnerability scanning, vulnerability assessment, and vulnerability remediation verification. Vulnerability scanning covers all system components including operating systems, databases, middleware, application systems, and security devices;
- **Security Assessment Services**: Regular security risk assessments, classified protection evaluations, and cryptographic application security assessments. Security assessments are conducted according to national standards and industry specifications;
- **Emergency Response Services**: Security incident emergency response, forensic analysis, and recovery handling. Emergency response provides 7×24-hour service to ensure rapid response when security incidents occur;
- **Security Training Services**: Security awareness training and technical training for system administrators and staff. Training content includes security awareness, security skills, and security compliance;
- **Security Compliance Services**: Assisting the client in meeting compliance requirements such as Cybersecurity Classified Protection and Data Security Law. Compliance services include compliance assessment, rectification guidance, and compliance auditing.

#### Technical Architecture

The security assurance system uses a "one center, three-layer protection, five-layer architecture" design:

- **One Center**: Security Operations Center (SOC), serving as the core hub for security management, achieving unified monitoring, analysis, and handling of security events. The SOC is staffed with security analysts, security engineers, and other professionals who use the SIEM platform for security event correlation analysis and threat intelligence matching;
- **Three-Layer Protection**: Network security protection, host security protection, and application security protection. The three-layer protection covers the main attack surfaces of the system, forming a defense-in-depth system;
- **Five-Layer Architecture**: Physical security layer, network security layer, host security layer, application security layer, and data security layer. The five-layer architecture strengthens security protection layer by layer from bottom to top.

Deployed security devices include: [ ] next-generation firewalls, [ ] intrusion detection/prevention systems, [ ] web application firewalls, [ ] database audit systems, [ ] log audit systems, [ ] bastion hosts, [ ] endpoint security management systems, etc.

### 9.3.2 Technical Solution

#### O&M Solution

**1. Security Operations System**

Establishing a "Monitor-Analyze-Alert-Handle-Review" security operations closed-loop process:

- **Monitor**: Full traffic, full element monitoring through security devices and system logs. Monitoring content includes network traffic, system logs, security logs, and application logs. Monitoring scope covers network boundaries, internal network zones, and cloud environments;
- **Analyze**: Using the SIEM platform for log correlation analysis and threat intelligence matching. Analysis content includes log correlation analysis, abnormal behavior analysis, threat intelligence matching, and attack chain analysis;
- **Alert**: Establishing tiered security incident early warning mechanisms with timely alert notifications. Alert levels are divided into four tiers: Red (Urgent), Orange (Important), Yellow (General), and Blue (Informational);
- **Handle**: Rapid response according to emergency plans, isolating threats and eliminating impacts. The handling process includes incident confirmation, impact assessment, containment, root cause analysis, recovery and reconstruction;
- **Review**: Summary analysis of security incidents to optimize protection strategies. Review content includes incident cause analysis, handling process assessment, and protection strategy optimization recommendations.

**2. Vulnerability Management System**

Establishing a comprehensive vulnerability management system:

- Monthly comprehensive vulnerability scanning covering all system components. Scanning tools include vulnerability scanners and configuration audit tools;
- Risk rating and remediation priority ranking for discovered vulnerabilities. Vulnerability risk rating uses CVSS scoring standards combined with business impact for comprehensive assessment;
- High-risk vulnerabilities remediated and verified within [ ] hours, medium-risk vulnerabilities within [ ] days, and low-risk vulnerabilities within [ ] days;
- Establishing vulnerability management ledger for tracking remediation closure. The ledger records vulnerability discovery time, risk level, remediation plan, remediation time, and verification results.

**3. Emergency Response System**

Establishing a four-level emergency response mechanism:

- **Level I Response (Extremely Major Security Incident)**: Major incidents affecting the entire government system's security. Response initiated within [ ] minutes, preliminary handling completed within [ ] hours. All emergency resources activated, Project Manager personally commands;
- **Level II Response (Major Security Incident)**: Important incidents affecting partial government system security. Response initiated within [ ] minutes, preliminary handling completed within [ ] hours. Main emergency resources activated, Security Supervisor commands;
- **Level III Response (Relatively Major Security Incident)**: Significant incidents affecting a single system's security. Response initiated within [ ] minutes, handling completed within [ ] hours. Relevant emergency resources activated, Security Engineer handles;
- **Level IV Response (General Security Incident)**: General security incidents with minor impact. Response initiated within [ ] minutes, handling completed within [ ] hours. Handled by duty personnel.

#### Technical Highlights

**1. Threat Intelligence-Driven Active Defense**

Connecting to multiple authoritative threat intelligence sources, establishing a threat intelligence analysis platform to achieve:

- **Automatic identification and blocking of known threats**: Through threat intelligence matching, automatically identifying known malicious IPs, malicious domains, malicious files, etc., and blocking them;
- **Early warning and active defense against new threats**: Through threat intelligence analysis, discovering new attack methods and vulnerability exploits, and taking proactive protective measures;
- **Attacker profiling and attack chain tracing**: By analyzing attacker behavior characteristics, tool usage, and attack methods, creating attacker profiles and conducting attack chain tracing;
- **Threat trend analysis and risk prediction**: Through analysis of threat intelligence data, identifying threat trends and predicting potential future security risks.

**2. Security Orchestration, Automation and Response (SOAR)**

Deploying a SOAR platform for automated security incident handling:

- **Automated assessment and handling of common security incidents**: Through predefined playbooks, automatically executing security incident assessment and handling, reducing manual intervention;
- **Automated security work order routing and closed-loop management**: Security incidents automatically create work orders, routed and processed according to predefined workflows for closed-loop management;
- **Automated security policy distribution and effectiveness verification**: Based on security analysis results, automatically distributing security policies to relevant security devices and verifying policy effectiveness;
- **Automated security report generation and distribution**: Regularly generating security reports including security posture analysis, incident statistics, and risk assessments, automatically distributing to relevant personnel.

**3. Zero-Day Vulnerability Protection**

Using sandbox analysis, behavior monitoring, and other technologies to achieve effective protection against zero-day vulnerabilities:

- **Automatic sandbox analysis of suspicious files**: Placing suspicious files in sandbox environments for behavior analysis to detect malicious behavior;
- **Real-time monitoring of abnormal process behavior**: Monitoring system process behavior to identify abnormal behavior patterns such as memory injection and process hiding;
- **Memory protection and exploit detection**: Monitoring memory operations to detect exploit behaviors such as buffer overflows and ROP attacks;
- **Application whitelisting and least privilege control**: Implementing application whitelisting to only allow authorized applications to run; implementing least privilege control to limit application permission scope.

#### Innovation Points

**1. "Security as a Service" (SECaaS) Model**

Innovatively adopting the "Security as a Service" model, providing security capabilities to business departments as services, achieving intensive use of security resources and integrated security management operations. The core content of the SECaaS model includes:
- Security capability serviceization: Packaging security monitoring, vulnerability management, emergency response, and other capabilities as standardized services;
- On-demand service delivery: Each department orders corresponding security services based on actual needs, paying as needed;
- Centralized security operations: Professional security operations teams uniformly provide security services to ensure service quality.

**2. "Attack-Defense Confrontation" Practical Drills**

Regularly organizing red-blue confrontation drills to test the effectiveness of the security protection system through practical attack-defense exercises, discovering security weaknesses and continuously improving. Drill content includes:
- Red Team (Attack Team): Simulating real attackers using various attack methods for penetration testing;
- Blue Team (Defense Team): Responsible for detecting and responding to red team attacks, testing security protection system effectiveness;
- Purple Team (Judgment Team): Responsible for organizing and evaluating the drill, summarizing and analyzing the drill process.

**3. Security Metrics and Visualization**

Establishing a security metrics indicator system with real-time security posture display through a security dashboard, transforming security management from "invisible" to "visible." Security metrics indicators include:
- Security incident indicators: incident count, handling time, handling rate, etc.;
- Vulnerability management indicators: vulnerability count, remediation rate, remediation time, etc.;
- Security compliance indicators: compliance rate, rectification completion rate, etc.;
- Security awareness indicators: training coverage rate, assessment pass rate, etc.

## 9.5 Project Experience Summary

### 9.5.1 Successful Experiences

Through practical accumulation from multiple projects, we have summarized the following 12 successful experiences:

**Experience 1: Establish a Client-Centered Service Philosophy**
Always prioritize client needs, establish regular communication mechanisms, proactively understand client concerns, and respond promptly to client needs. By establishing client service files recording client preferences and focus areas, personalized services are provided. In practice, we communicate with clients weekly, report monthly, and survey quarterly to ensure service direction aligns with client needs.

**Experience 2: Prevention-Oriented O&M Strategy**
Adopting a "prevention-oriented, proactive O&M" strategy, eliminating faults in their early stages through regular inspections, preventive maintenance, and trend analysis. Establishing equipment health files for full lifecycle management of equipment operational status. We established an equipment health scoring model that scores equipment based on operational duration, fault frequency, and performance indicators, performing maintenance or replacement on low-scoring equipment in advance.

**Experience 3: Standardized O&M Processes**
Establishing a standardized O&M process system covering incident management, problem management, change management, configuration management, and release management. All O&M operations have Standard Operating Procedures (SOPs) to ensure service consistency and repeatability. We compiled over 200 O&M operation manuals covering all common O&M operations, enabling new O&M engineers to master basic operations within 1 week.

**Experience 4: Data-Driven Decision Making**
Through collecting and analyzing O&M data, establishing a data-driven decision-making model. Regularly producing O&M analysis reports with data-driven insights for scientific client decision-making. We established an O&M data warehouse with 3 years of O&M data, discovering over 30 optimization points through data analysis, providing strong support for system performance improvement.

**Experience 5: Continuous Technical Innovation**
Encouraging technical innovation, actively introducing AI, big data, automation, and other new technologies to improve O&M service intelligence levels. Establishing a special fund for technical innovation to support the technical team in conducting innovative research. We invest 5% of annual revenue in technical innovation, having cumulatively invested over 5 million yuan in R&D, obtaining 10 patents and 16 software copyrights.

**Experience 6: Talent Development and Team Building**
Establishing a comprehensive talent development system with regular technical training and skills certification. Building a technical expert echelon ensuring backup personnel for key positions. Creating a learning team atmosphere encouraging knowledge sharing. We established a "mentor system" where each new employee is assigned an experienced mentor to ensure skill transfer continuity.

**Experience 7: Risk Control Mechanism**
Establishing a comprehensive risk control mechanism with regular risk assessments and risk response plans. Implementing dual-person review for major operations to ensure operational safety. We established a risk library identifying over 100 potential risk points, with corresponding response measures for each to ensure risk controllability.

**Experience 8: Knowledge Management**
Establishing an O&M knowledge base accumulating common fault handling solutions, best practices, and technical documents. The knowledge base supports intelligent search for quick solution lookup by O&M personnel. We established a knowledge base contribution incentive mechanism encouraging O&M personnel to share experiences, with over 500 solutions accumulated.

**Experience 9: Emergency Response Capability**
Establishing a comprehensive emergency response system with various emergency plans and regular emergency drills. Ensuring rapid response and effective handling when emergencies occur. We conduct quarterly emergency drills covering network failures, server failures, security incidents, and other scenarios to ensure the practical capability of the emergency response team.

**Experience 10: Continuous Service Quality Improvement**
Establishing a PDCA continuous improvement mechanism through monthly assessments, quarterly reviews, and annual summaries to continuously discover issues, analyze causes, develop measures, verify effects, and achieve spiral service quality improvement. We conduct monthly service quality assessments, developing improvement measures for identified issues and tracking improvement effects.

**Experience 11: Supply Chain Management and Partner Relationships**
Establishing stable supplier and partner relationships to ensure timely spare parts supply and technical support. Regularly evaluating suppliers to ensure service quality. We established a supplier evaluation system with quarterly evaluations linked to cooperation relationships.

**Experience 12: Compliance Management**
Strictly complying with national laws, regulations, and industry standards, establishing a compliance management system. Regularly conducting compliance checks to ensure O&M services meet Classified Protection, Data Security Law, and other compliance requirements. We conduct semi-annual compliance checks to ensure all O&M operations comply with relevant laws, regulations, and standards.

### 9.5.2 Lessons Learned

During project implementation, we also summarized the following 6 important lessons:

**Lesson 1: Requirements Research Must Be Thorough**
In one project, insufficient requirements research in the early stage led to frequent later changes affecting project progress and costs. The lesson is that sufficient time and effort must be invested in detailed requirements research during the project launch phase to ensure completeness and accuracy. Subsequently, we invested 15% of total project time in the requirements research phase, effectively reducing later requirements changes.

**Lesson 2: Change Management Must Be Strict**
In one instance, a system change was not strictly executed according to process, causing a system failure affecting business operations. The lesson is that a strict change management process must be established, with all changes requiring review, approval, and testing before implementation. We subsequently established a change management committee requiring all major changes to be approved by the committee.

**Lesson 3: Backup Verification Must Be Regular**
During one data recovery, backup data was found to be incomplete, delaying data recovery. The lesson is that regular backup data recovery verification must be conducted to ensure backup data completeness and availability. We conduct monthly backup recovery verification to ensure backup data reliability.

**Lesson 4: Personnel Backup Must Be in Place**
In one project, key personnel departure caused service interruption affecting client satisfaction. The lesson is that backup mechanisms for key positions must be established to ensure qualified personnel are always available. We cultivate at least 2 backup personnel for each key position to ensure personnel changes do not affect service quality.

**Lesson 5: Communication Mechanisms Must Be Sound**
In one project, insufficient communication with the client led to accumulated issues ultimately affecting project acceptance. The lesson is that regular and timely communication mechanisms must be established, proactively reporting project progress and issues to the client. We established a three-tier reporting system with weekly, monthly, and quarterly reports to ensure timely information delivery.

**Lesson 6: Document Management Must Be Standardized**
In one project, non-standardized document management led to missing key documents during acceptance, affecting the acceptance progress. The lesson is that standardized document management systems must be established to ensure all documents are filed promptly, completely, and accurately. We established a document management system achieving electronic document management and version control.

### 9.5.3 Best Practices

Through years of practice, we have summarized the following 10 best practices:

**Best Practice 1: O&M Service Standardization**
Developing unified O&M service standards including service processes, service specifications, and service quality indicators. All projects execute according to unified standards ensuring service consistency and predictability. We compiled an O&M service standards manual covering service processes, operational specifications, and quality standards.

**Best Practice 2: Full Monitoring Coverage**
Establishing a comprehensive monitoring system covering networks, servers, storage, applications, and security to ensure real-time perception of system operational status. Monitoring indicators cover availability, performance, capacity, security, and other dimensions. Our monitoring system covers 99.5% of system components with over 5,000 monitoring indicators.

**Best Practice 3: Automated O&M**
Actively introducing automated O&M tools for automation of configuration deployment, patch updates, backup recovery, and other operations. Automation coverage target of 80% or above to reduce manual operation errors. Our automation coverage has reached 75%, covering most routine O&M operations.

**Best Practice 4: Intelligent O&M**
Introducing AI and big data technologies for intelligent O&M capabilities including fault prediction, intelligent alerting, and root cause analysis. Continuously optimizing O&M decisions through machine learning. Our intelligent O&M platform has achieved 85% fault prediction accuracy and 90% root cause localization accuracy.

**Best Practice 5: Defense in Depth Security**
Establishing a multi-layered security protection system covering network layer, host layer, application layer, and data layer security protection. Adopting defense-in-depth strategy to ensure that any single protection failure does not cause overall security collapse. Our security protection system passed the Classified Protection Level 3 evaluation with a score of 92 points.

**Best Practice 6: Service Level Management**
Signing clear Service Level Agreements (SLAs) with clients defining service indicators and assessment standards. Regularly conducting SLA assessments to ensure service compliance. Our SLA compliance rate has consistently maintained above 98%.

**Best Practice 7: Continuous Optimization Mechanism**
Establishing a continuous optimization mechanism with regular O&M service effectiveness assessments to identify improvement opportunities. Continuously improving service levels through technical innovation, process optimization, and personnel training. We conduct quarterly service optimization assessments and annual technology upgrades.

**Best Practice 8: Knowledge Sharing Mechanism**
Establishing knowledge sharing mechanisms with regular technical sharing sessions and experience exchange meetings. Encouraging O&M personnel to write technical documents and case studies to promote overall team capability improvement. We organize monthly technical sharing sessions and publish an annual technical paper collection.

**Best Practice 9: Business Continuity Management**
Establishing a business continuity management system with business continuity plans and disaster recovery plans. Regularly conducting disaster recovery drills to ensure rapid business recovery when disaster events occur. Our disaster recovery switchover time has been reduced to within 30 minutes.

**Best Practice 10: Customer Satisfaction Management**
Establishing a customer satisfaction management mechanism with regular satisfaction surveys and customer feedback collection. Developing improvement measures for unsatisfactory items, tracking improvement effects, and forming closed-loop management. Our customer satisfaction has consistently maintained above 95%.
